title: snapshot_commit stale-lock reclaim can race and overlap runs
description: Provenance: scripts/snapshot_commit.sh:37-42, reviewed at receipt-status-audit PR #142 head c5f968b1147a61d4ab7134d7eaa7a07d92345417 on 2026-10-10. Two contenders can both observe an expired lock and dead/missing PID; one can create a replacement lock and the other can remove it, allowing overlapping runs. Therefore a newer terminal receipt cannot prove an older active attempt has stopped. Keep status unknown until a safe lock ownership/run-lifetime protocol provides reliable exclusion proof. This corrects the desired behavior documented in disk_magician-nhsx; it is not implementation scope for PR #142. Pressure sweep has a separate analogous stale TTL lock issue tracked in disk_magician-151c.

title: pressure_sweep stale-lock reclamation can overlap an active run
description: Provenance: scripts/pressure_sweep.sh:291 (verified at receipt-status-audit PR #142 review on 2026-10-10). The mkdir lock is reclaimed after its 3600-second TTL without checking whether the original process is still alive. If run A outlives the TTL, run B can acquire the replacement lock and finish while A is still executing; B receipt acquisition does not prove A stopped. Status must therefore keep pressure_sweep active receipts unknown and must not supersede them. Follow-up: design and test a safe pressure-sweep lock ownership/recovery protocol with live-PID proof before changing status classification. The corresponding isolated review-worktree record is disk_magician-a93h; this canonical tracker record owns follow-up.

description:
From pi-watch cycle 20261027-022701 OFF TRACK 1.

Live check 2026-10-27: gh pr view 251 -> state=CLOSED, updated 2026-10-24T07:20Z, head 38ed1a1, mergeable CONFLICTING. The lane's actual pushed head 4437721 is the head of OPEN PR #272 (codex/quota-implementation-r13, draft, MERGEABLE) with Evidence Gate=FAILURE and Test-and-lint IN_PROGRESS.

Impact: a stale worktree->PR binding makes a cycle report a phantom conflict and leaves the real failing gate unowned; also feeds the 'closed PR babysit' class (babysit-stale-watchdog).

Fix direction: derive the PR from the current branch head (gh pr list --json headRefOid, match local HEAD) rather than a cached footer/branch association, and treat closed/merged heads as terminal without polling.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:
2026-11-09 ~21:00-23:30 PST, mac (jeffreys-macbook-pro): recurrence in TWO distinct shapes, both reached through the installed CLI.

SHAPE A - interrupted init, unrecoverable forever. Lock dir had pid=48500 (dead) and NO acquired_at, age 34057s. lease_reuse_lock_recover() requires the stamp to match ^[0-9]+$ on its FIRST read, so a missing acquired_at returns 1 before the TTL check ever runs. The lock can never self-recover; a manual rmdir was the only path. The producer writes pid (~line 660) then acquired_at (~line 667), so a SIGKILL between those two writes lands here permanently.

SHAPE B - complete lock, dead holder, up to 3600s total reclaim stall. Lock had pid=92032 (dead, ps empty) and a valid acquired_at, age 2308s. Recovery correctly fails closed until TTL, so every lease-writing lane was blocked for ~22 more minutes: cleanup-worktree-deps reported 28x LEASE-KEEP (registry-lock-busy) and freed 0 MB; cleanup-code-sign-clones freed 0 KB across 30 candidates; scratch-prune aborted at scanned=301 with skipped:lease-busy.

Measured effect of clearing the wedge: cleanup-code-sign-clones --clean then removed 7 dirs / 10.2 GiB, and a rerun of scratch-prune went from removed=0 to removed=39. The reclaim lanes silently free nothing while the lock is wedged; this is a concrete mechanism behind the "reports success, frees nothing" class.

Shape A is the durability gap worth fixing: recovery understands only the both-fields case. A lock with pid and no acquired_at should be recoverable once the pid is provably dead, using the lock dir mtime as the age source. Shape B is defensible fail-closed behaviour, but 3600s is a long total-reclaim outage caused by one SIGKILLed producer.

title: cleanup_pr_scratch: 'rm failed' on 35 plain user-owned /tmp files, so the 12h sweep reclaims 0
description:
Measured 2026-10-24 on the Mac. Ran the sanctioned 12h path (which DOES exist -- cleanup_pr_scratch.sh exposes --min-age-hours N / --min-age-days / DISK_MAGICIAN_PR_SCRATCH_MIN_AGE_HOURS / config pr_scratch_retention_hours, default 48; no code change needed for a shorter window):

  cleanup_pr_scratch.sh --clean --min-age-hours 12
  -> rc=0  'Done. Dirs removed: 0  Files removed: 0  Total freed: 0 KB  Skipped (rm failed): 35'

The 35 skipped items are ORDINARY files, not dirs, not protected roots:
  /private/tmp/pr240_after_api.json
  /private/tmp/pr10577-dot-review-current-request.txt
  /private/tmp/pr9733-harness-help-final.txt
  /private/tmp/pr118-pr10794-status-body-draft.md
And the permissions/flags are unremarkable -- all are 'jleechan:wheel', mode 644, NO flags (ls -lO shows '-'), so this is not ownership, not a uchg/immutable flag, and not a protected path.

So the removal primitive itself is failing and reporting only a generic 'rm failed'. Most likely the script routes per-file removal through the quarantine/logged-remove helper (quarantine_rename / rm_logged) and the rename step fails, then the failure is collapsed into one reason string. That is the SAME observability defect this session has hit repeatedly: a specific failure is reported as a generic skip, so it reads like a safety refusal and nobody investigates.

Impact: the 12h policy dial works but reclaims ZERO because every individual removal fails. Combined with the 48h default, /private/tmp scratch (10-11 GiB of fresh PR/audit dirs) is effectively unreclaimable by the routine.

Fix shape (not implemented): surface the ACTUAL errno/exception per failed item (EACCES/EXDEV/ENOENT/EPERM) instead of a single 'rm failed', and keep going rather than counting 35 silent failures as a normal outcome. Add a regression test that a plain user-owned file in /tmp IS removed by the 12h path.

title: qdrant xpcproxy stuck after kickstart cycle, needs KeepAlive in plist
description:
After the 2026-07-29 03:00 diagnostic recipe hammered qdrant with add+search across an hour of /learn captures, qdrant filled its open-file limit at ~652/1048576 and RocksDB failed every flush with "Too many open files" (RocksDB .log append). The Stop hook + a Memory.add() then timed out with qdrant_client.http.exceptions.ResponseHandlingException: timed out.

Attempted recovery path: launchctl kickstart -k ai.hermes.qdrant. Result: xpcproxy holds the slot, but launchd never spawns the qdrant child because the post-kickstart transition is stuck at "immediate reason = speculative, last exit code = (never exited)". Bootout+bootstrap returns "Bad request" because the wedged xpcproxy is already in the slot, and xpcproxy (pid 50465 / 79200) cannot be SIGKILL-ed by the user (bears jleechan_session but managed by launchd).

Root cause: the disk_magician-installed ai.hermes.qdrant.plist lacks a KeepAlive directive, so when a transient error forces qdrant into the half-spawn state, launchd cannot recover. The original platform script (start-qdrant-container.sh) had bash as PID 1 returning "docker not ready", which launchd would mark exit-coded and respawn next-tick.

Fix: add the keys KeepAlive (with SuccessfulExit: false) and ThrottleInterval: 5 to the plist. SuccessfulExit:false forces a respawn on any non-zero OR on signal-ish exits; ThrottleInterval:5 caps retry rate so we never stampede launchd.

Workaround (lossy): run qdrant via launchctl print-disable + direct user-level launch. Loses login-cycle durability but recovers read/write API now.

Live attempts recorded on 2026-07-29:
  kickstart -k → xpcproxy stays, qdrant child never spawns
  bootout then bootstrap → "Bad request" / already in slot
  kill -9 50465 → "Operation not permitted" (launchd-owned process)
  wait past exit-timeout=5s → still wedged at 5s
Recovery not yet achieved as of 2026-07-29 03:30 PDT. Outstanding.

Qdrant on localhost:6333 is currently down; recent writes (this /learn captures disk-full-2026-07-29 fact, plus the smaller earlier entries from this session) are at risk of being lost unless recovered.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-07-29 02:01 PDT via /sidekick (mission disk_magician-o5v).

Root cause was three-fold, NOT just a missing KeepAlive:

1. The plist (added 2026-07-27) pointed qdrant at
   ~/.local/share/qdrant/storage but the live data was at
   ~/.hermes/qdrant_storage/ (redirected by the backup cron at
   some point; the migration was never propagated to the cron).
   The binary was coming up against an empty storage tree, holding
   the bind open until launchd classified the start as
   'speculative'.

2. The plist had no KeepAlive / ThrottleInterval. After my
   launchctl kickstart -k cycle, launchd could not recover.

3. ProcessType was Background. Even AFTER (1) and (2) were
   fixed, launchd SIGTERM'd the qdrant child at 09:10:40, 36s
   after first bind. This was the session-context reaper killing
   Background processes when the spawning shell exits. THIS IS THE
   DEEPEST BUG: KeepAlive's SuccessfulExit:false does NOT prevent
   Background reaping.

The fix that worked: ProcessType: Background -> Interactive
(processType change in plist, then launchctl bootstrap). After
the change qdrant pid 30212 is alive, /healthz is green, mem0
add+search both return successfully.

LESSON (memory bead linked): ProcessType Background on
user-scope launchd jobs is incompatible with keeping daemon-like
services alive across session boundaries. For a long-lived local
daemon (qdrant, mem0 hooks, etc.) ProcessType must be Interactive.

OUTSTANDING (related, deferred): the backup cron
ai.hermes.schedule.qdrant-backup.plist reads from
~/.hermes/qdrant_storage/ (old path) — its backups will be empty
until the cron path is updated to match the plist's path. Tracked
in the same bead as a follow-up.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_install_launchd_sweepers_lock.sh — Regression test: concurrent
# invocations of install_launchd_sweepers.sh must not race bootout/bootstrap

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

grep -q "installed " <<<"$OUT_CONTENT" && fail=1
```

title: Observer reports empty Docker inventory despite live Colima containers
description:
Confirmed 2026-10-10 on the Mac observer host. The existing launchd observer (PID 63643) runs `/usr/bin/python3 /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/disk_observer.py watch --interval 60 --output /Users/jleechan/.disk_magician_state/disk_observer.jsonl`. Its launchd `DOCKER_HOST` is `unix:///Users/jleechan/.colima/default/docker.sock`; the current Docker context is `colima` with the same endpoint.

At observer timestamp `2026-10-10T12:35:26Z`, the raw record reports Docker `available=true`, `containers=[]`, `events=[]`, `error=null`, and `total_writable_bytes=0`. The collector at `scripts/disk_observer.py:177-178` calls `docker ps -aq`, then records container writable sizes. Within seconds, read-only `docker ps` on the host and `colima ssh -- docker ps` against that same Colima engine both showed six running containers: `ez-mac-runner-h-1` through `ez-mac-runner-h-4`, `ezgha-image-anchor`, and `hermes-mem0-qdrant`. The raw observer row and exact host/Colima context plus actual container listing are captured at `/tmp/disk_magician/evidence/producer-attribution-2026-10-10/observer-sample.json` and `docker-context.txt`; SHA256 values are in the parent handoff.

This is separate from `disk_magician-1u29`, which tracks omission of the active Lima datadisk path. Here the observer silently presents an empty successful Docker inventory despite the live engine having active writable containers, so disk growth and container writes can disappear from observer attribution. Root cause is not yet established and no code change is requested in this bead.

Acceptance: when the observer can query the configured engine, its persisted record includes the actual running container IDs/names and writable-byte totals; if collection cannot see the engine, the record reports an explicit error/unavailable state rather than a successful empty inventory. Validate against the same host, command, Docker context/endpoint, raw observer sample, and contemporaneous `docker ps` output captured above. Keep the issue scoped to observability; do not prune or stop containers as part of the fix.
acceptance_criteria: A live observer sample records the actual running container IDs/names and writable-byte totals from the configured Colima engine, or explicitly reports unavailable/error; reproduction uses captured same-host observer and docker ps evidence; no container is pruned or stopped.

title: Auto-register safe-class uncovered >=5 GiB roots into sweeper_roots.txt (check_uncovered_roots --register, opt-in)
IMPL: add concurrency lock to install_launchd_sweepers.sh
description:
Environment: repo root /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician; start SHA = the commit that closes bead T1 (dependency); interpreter: system bash; throwaway worktree required: no; credentials read from env: none.

Goal: Add an mkdir-based concurrency lock to `scripts/install_launchd_sweepers.sh` so a second overlapping invocation exits cleanly (never queues, never blocks) instead of racing `launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap` calls against a first invocation — the mechanism corroborated 2026-09-06/07 by two independent agent sessions (this Claude Code session and a separate Gemini CLI session) each independently running this exact installer on the same machine while the launchd fleet was observed flapping. Owned files: modify: `scripts/install_launchd_sweepers.sh`. Dependency bead IDs: T1 (disk_magician-3pi, filled in at creation). Line budget: ~35 lines (non-test).

Reuse: informational only, no separate action required — Step 2 below already contains the complete, final replacement text (derived in shape from `scripts/cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh:271-290`'s `acquire_cleanup_venvs_lock` and `scripts/cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh:59-61`'s `DISK_MAGICIAN_STATE_DIR` convention, renamed to `acquire_install_lock` with a 900-second TTL instead of that file's 3600s because this script's own runtime is normally well under a minute — all local file writes plus per-label `launchctl` calls — unlike the venv-stripping script, which can run long over many worktrees). Do not re-derive or re-copy anything from `cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh` yourself; use only the exact text given in Step 2.

Steps:
1. Confirm the dependency's RED state is still true before editing: `bash tests/test_install_launchd_sweepers_lock.sh; test $? -eq 1 && echo "PASS PRECHECK-I1" || echo "FAIL PRECHECK-I1"` — must print `PASS PRECHECK-I1` (if it prints `FAIL PRECHECK-I1`, stop: either bead T1 wasn't actually merged at this SHA, or someone already added a lock — do not proceed).
2. In `scripts/install_launchd_sweepers.sh`, find this exact existing text (currently 2 lines, immediately after the `resolve_bash()` function definition):

```
BASH_BIN="$(resolve_bash)"
mkdir -p "$DEST"
```

Replace it with exactly this (same 2 lines, plus the new lock block appended immediately after):

```
BASH_BIN="$(resolve_bash)"
mkdir -p "$DEST"

# Concurrency lock (disk_magician-4mw): mkdir-based lock mirroring
# cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh's acquire_cleanup_venvs_lock (bead
# disk_magician-w7m). Contention = log one line and skip this run entirely
# (exit 0) -- never queue, never block. Added 2026-09-07 after the fleet was
# observed flapping with a SEPARATE agent session on this machine
# independently running this exact installer -- the leading hypothesis being
# two uncoordinated invocations interleaving install_plist()'s per-label
# `launchctl bootout` then `launchctl bootstrap` calls against each other.
STATE_DIR="${DISK_MAGICIAN_STATE_DIR:-$HOME/.disk_magician_state}"
LOCK_DIR="$STATE_DIR/install_launchd_sweepers.lock"
LOCK_TTL_SEC="${DISK_MAGICIAN_INSTALL_SWEEPERS_LOCK_TTL_SEC:-900}"

acquire_install_lock() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOCK_DIR")"
  if mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo $$ > "$LOCK_DIR/pid"
    trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR"' EXIT
    return 0
  fi
  local held_pid age
  held_pid=$(cat "$LOCK_DIR/pid" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f '%m' "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%Y' "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) ))
  if [[ "$age" -gt "$LOCK_TTL_SEC" ]] && { [[ -z "$held_pid" ]] || ! kill -0 "$held_pid" 2>/dev/null; }; then
    rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR"
    if mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo $$ > "$LOCK_DIR/pid"
      trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR"' EXIT
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  echo "install_launchd_sweepers: already running (lock held by pid ${held_pid:-?}, age ${age}s) -- not queuing" >&2
  return 1
}

acquire_install_lock || exit 0
```

The comment already reads `disk_magician-4mw` — this bead's own ID — leave it exactly as shown above; it is not a placeholder.

RED: n/a — this bead only makes bead T1's RED test pass; there is no separate RED state for this bead's own diff (structural: an edit bead's job is GREEN, not RED). Pre-state check is Step 1 above.

GREEN: `bash tests/test_install_launchd_sweepers_lock.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` → last line `PASS T1`.

Do not: do not change the TTL to match `cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh`'s 3600s (this script's normal runtime is far shorter; a long TTL would leave a genuinely-stuck lock blocking repairs for up to an hour). Do not add the lock around only part of the script (e.g. only the default no-args loop) — place it immediately after `mkdir -p "$DEST"`, before the `retired_labels` loop, so it covers every code path including `--unload-legacy` and single-plist-name invocations. Do not remove or rename the existing `trap` usage inside `install_launchdaemon()` (a different, unrelated trap for the sudo/root path) — this bead's lock is independent of that function.

Stop when: Step 1's precheck prints `FAIL PRECHECK-I1` (stop and report which sub-case applies rather than guessing). Stop when the two-line anchor text in Step 2 (`BASH_BIN="$(resolve_bash)"` immediately followed by `mkdir -p "$DEST"`) is not found verbatim, byte-for-byte, in `scripts/install_launchd_sweepers.sh` when you read it — do not search for a "close enough" match or a different insertion point; stop and report the actual surrounding lines instead. Stop when the GREEN command's last line is not exactly `PASS T1` after one retry of the same command (do not edit the test to force a pass; reopen bead T1 instead if the test's own contract turns out to be wrong).

Report: `git add scripts/install_launchd_sweepers.sh && git commit -m "fix: add concurrency lock to install_launchd_sweepers.sh"`; run `bash tests/test_install_launchd_sweepers_lock.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` and also `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -1` plus the full shell suite (`for f in tests/test_*.sh; do bash "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "FAIL: $f"; done` — expect no output) to confirm no regression, then paste all three results into this bead via `br comments add disk_magician-4mw "<pasted lines>"`.

title: C14 remote proof: remote outside root borrowing objects via alternates from inside root
description: Found by /advice (Opus) on PR #160 at c73f47d. c14_repo_pushed_ok accepts a local remote outside the deletion root, but that remote may use objects/info/alternates (or be a linked worktree whose common dir is inside the root) pointing into the root; ls-remote then certifies history that deleting the root destroys. Test: bare remote outside root with alternates into a repo inside root -> kept:remote-unverified. Also nit: initialize adv= in c14_repo_pushed_ok (unbound under set -u with zero remotes; verdict stays kept).

title: jeff-ubuntu global OOM exhaustion silently kills scheduled maintenance (disk-magician reclaim collateral, OOMScoreAdjust=100)
description:
jeff-ubuntu ran under global memory exhaustion on BOTH prior boots, and the 20-minute diskm-scratch-reclaim.service was killed as collateral each time. This is filed separately from disk_magician-mgg2 because the mechanism is host memory pressure, NOT a disk-magician bug - do not fix this by changing reclaim logic.

MEASURED 2026-11-03T06:5xZ, journalctl -k per boot (global, any unit):
  boot -2 (b414c95d, 2026-10-29..10-31): 39 'Out of memory: Killed' events
  boot -1 (7eca54c2, 2026-10-31..11-02): 59 'Out of memory: Killed' events
  boot  0 (cc7718f1, current):            0 OOM kills

The unit's own journal shows oom-kill on 2 of the last 3 boots:
  boot -2: 2 oom-kill results
  boot -1: 2 oom-kill results
  boot  0: 0

Representative unit timeline (boot -1):
  Nov 02 19:41:17 Starting diskm-scratch-reclaim.service
  Nov 02 19:44:28 'A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer.'
  Nov 02 19:44:57 'A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer.' then 'Killing process 1241717 (bash) with signal SIGKILL.'
  Nov 02 20:24:06 restart -> Nov 02 20:26:55 killed again, status=9/KILL, result='oom-kill'

Why disk-magician dies first (kernel oom-kill lines name the actual victims, all oom_score_adj:100 except the 22GB node):
  - tmux-spawn-...scope task=node: total-vm 22,620,264 kB (22.6 GB), anon-rss 207,620 kB, oom_score_adj 0  <- the biggest VM consumer survived
  - ezgha.service task=systemctl: oom_score_adj 100  <- killed
  - mcp-daemon.service task=gh: total-vm 1,295,412 kB, oom_score_adj 100  <- killed
  - github-runner-smtp-egress.service task=run.sh: oom_score_adj 100  <- killed
The reclaim unit is identically exposed: OOMScoreAdjust=100, ManagedOOMPreference=none, MemoryMax=infinity, MemoryHigh=infinity, MemoryMin=0 in app.slice.

Consequence for the operator-visible symptom: a scheduled reclaim that is OOM-killed mid-run reclaims nothing and reports a non-zero result. On a host whose Scratch is a 200G loop image that only returns space to / on FITRIM (disk_magician-hbi4), losing the 20-minute reclaim cycle to an OOM kill means host / pressure goes unrelieved for that cycle. So memory exhaustion on jeff-ubuntu degrades disk hygiene, which then looks like a disk-magician defect.

Current state (same session): 60 GB RAM, 10 GB used, 37 GB buff/cache, 50 GB available, swap 16 GB with 5.8 GB USED (it read 0B earlier in the same session, so swap is now absorbing pressure). 12 node processes and the ezgha/github-runner fleet are the standing risk.

Routing note: if this belongs to the host/runner fleet rather than disk_magician, move it - the evidence is host-level. Acceptance criteria below are deliberately host-scoped.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Identify what consumes 22GB+ VM (the tmux-spawn node process) and why it survives while oom_score_adj=100 peers die; either bound it or accept and protect maintenance units
- [ ] Protect scheduled maintenance from global_oom: give diskm-scratch-reclaim (and peer timers) a memory floor / OOM protection, or run them in a bounded slice, so host pressure cannot silently skip disk hygiene
- [ ] Alarm on global OOM events per boot (39 and 59 events went unnoticed); a boot with OOM kills must surface, not just the unit's restart count
- [ ] Test: under induced memory pressure, a scheduled maintenance unit completes or reports a distinct 'skipped: host-pressure' outcome rather than an OOM kill
- [ ] Verify swap sizing/usage policy - 5.8G of 16G used with 50G available indicates reclaim pressure, not a shortage
notes:
Cross-references (all four must stay separate fixes):
- disk_magician-mgg2 (OPEN, P1) - Linux reclaim fails closed on scratch-lock contention. THIS bead is the other way the same unit dies. Note the mode CHANGE: current boot has 0 OOM kills and instead fails on lock-skip, so the current live symptom is mgg2's, not this bead's. Do not read the lock-skip as evidence against OOM history.
- disk_magician-ms99 (OPEN, P1) - service timeout vs wrapper budget. PREMISE STALE: live rendered unit, installed template, and origin/main (both src/disk_magician/systemd/ and systemd/) all read TimeoutStartSec=950, inner wrapper deadline 900. Gap is now 50s in the safe direction.
- disk_magician-hbi4 (OPEN, P1) - loop image never punches holes (no discard/FITRIM); fstrim of ~/Scratch fails EPERM as non-root. This is WHY losing a reclaim cycle to OOM matters for host /.
- disk_magician-46z7 (IN_PROGRESS, P1) - Mac-side reclaim no-op below threshold. Mac sibling, different code path.

Attribution caveat for future readers: I first reported this unit as 'being OOM-killed repeatedly' without checking boot boundaries and had to walk that back - the kills are real but belong to boots -2 and -1, not the current boot. Always split per boot with 'journalctl --user -u diskm-scratch-reclaim.service -b <id>' before claiming a current OOM defect. Verified per-boot counts are in the description.

title: cleanup_tmp recency probe is satisfied by the directory's own mtime, so touched-but-stale trees are never swept
description: Found 2026-10-20 while attributing disk growth. scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh has_recent_activity (line 587) runs /usr/bin/find "$dir" -mmin -N -print -quit and treats ANY hit as 'recently active'. The first hit is frequently the directory entry itself, whose mtime moves on any child create/delete/rename even when no content changed. Live example: /private/tmp/worldai_frontend is 22.06 GiB, its newest CONTENT file is 8.7h old (older than the 6h window), yet its dir mtime is 10:16 today, so the probe hits the dir immediately and the 22 GiB tree is skipped every pass — indefinitely, as long as anything touches it. Same shape for /private/tmp/worldarchitect.ai (11.59 GiB, newest content 22.7h, dir mtime today; that one is also a protected root). Effect: /private/tmp grew 27.59 -> 49.24 GiB (+21.7) while the sweeper reported 'Dirs removed: 0' because everything looked active. Definition of done: the recency probe must measure CONTENT mtime, not the directory entry's own mtime — e.g. find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -mmin -N -print -quit, or reuse canonical worktree_is_recently_active which already prunes .git and ignores dir mtime — with a regression asserting that a tree whose only recent change is its own directory mtime is treated as STALE (sweepable) while a tree with a genuinely recent content file is still protected.

title: TEST: agent_worktree.sh helper (worktree-not-clone, redesigned scope of 2nw)
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after T5-TEST/T5-IMPL closed
(this bead's stub sources `scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh` only for
`_agent_scratch_valid_component` label validation, not for its root — see Goal — so
`agent_scratch.sh` must exist: depends on disk_magician-agent-scratch-helper-impl-ned). Interpreter:
bash. No throwaway worktree required. Created 2026-09-24 (redesign of the original
disk_magician-orchestrator-worktree-not-clone-2nw scope): **APPROVED 2026-09-24** by the user
("finish all"). Corrected framing from the original bead draft: there is no separate "owning
orchestrator repo" to find — the `~/.claude/state` full-clone growth (bead isw) is produced by ad
hoc interactive Claude Code/Codex sessions spawning codex/agy verifier lanes, not by a discrete
automation repo disk_magician lacks access to. The fix disk_magician CAN ship directly is an in-repo
helper any such session can call instead of `git clone`; the separate machine-wide policy
instruction to actually call it lives in bead disk_magician-codex-agents-md-scratch-policy-2gp
(approval-gated there on `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`'s own semantic-signoff gate, not duplicated here).

**Round-4b correction (2026-09-24, independent Codex + Opus review of the original 2026-09-24
draft, both flagged the same defect):** the original draft had `agent_worktree_create` allocate the
worktree parent via `agent_scratch_create "worktrees" ...`, nesting it inside
`/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>/worktrees/...`. That is a real safety bug, not a
style nit: that whole subtree is (a) subject to bead B4/`scratch_budget.sh`'s size-budget+age
eviction once enabled (bead i2o) and (b) removed wholesale by the A3 Stop hook
(`agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh`) when a session ends — neither check is worktree-aware, so either
path could `rm -rf` a worktree with uncommitted, unpushed work in well under the repo `CLAUDE.md`
"Worktree 7-day rule (hard)"'s protected window. Fixed by NOT reusing `agent_scratch_create`/the
agent-scratch root at all: worktrees get their own sibling root,
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees/<label>-$$-$(date +%s)`, plain `mkdir -p`, never touched by
`scratch_budget.sh` eviction or the Stop hook (neither's root list includes
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees`, and this bead's IMPL pair must not add it there). This trades away
"same swept/budgeted root as other scratch" — intentional: a swept root is exactly the property that
was unsafe for worktrees. Cleanup of `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` is explicitly NOT scoped to this
bead pair (a follow-up bead, not created here, would extend the existing 7-day-floor
`cleanup_worktrees.sh`/`scripts/lib/worktree_recency.sh` path to also scan it) — until that exists,
these worktrees simply are not auto-swept, which is the safe default per the hard rule, not a
regression this bead pair needs to close.

**Round-4c correction (2026-09-24, second-round Opus re-review of the round-4b fix above): the
first `/private/tmp/agent-worktrees` choice was still unsafe**, even after removing the
`agent_scratch_create` nesting — `/private/tmp` itself (not just the agent-scratch subtree inside
it) is scanned one level deep by `cleanup_tmp.sh --large`, which runs in production TODAY (called by
`pressure_sweep.sh` with no dependency on bead i2o) and would archive-then-purge a top-level
`agent-worktrees` container after ~4h of no file changes anywhere under it (confirmed live:
`scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh`'s large-dir loop walks `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT` — `scratch_roots_get_private_tmp()`
in `scripts/lib/scratch_roots.sh:52-55`, which resolves to literal `/private/tmp` — at
`-mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1`; `agent-worktrees` would not match the `wt_*|worktree_*` name pattern that
triggers its `worktree_has_unsaved_work` guard, nor is it in `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS`). Fixed
by moving the default root one more level away: `AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` now defaults to
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` — a different top-level system directory, confirmed live via
`grep -rn '/private/var/tmp' scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh` returning zero matches, i.e. no existing
sweeper in this repo scans `/private/var/tmp` at all. This is the actual fix; do not move the
default back under `/private/tmp` for any reason without also adding `agent-worktrees` to
`DEFAULT_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS` in `scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh` (out of scope for this bead pair) AND a
test proving both `cleanup_tmp.sh --large` and `scratch_budget_evict_root` skip it.

## Goal
Add `tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` proving a not-yet-created `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh`
provides `agent_worktree_create <label> <ref> <repo>` — allocates a managed leaf directory directly under
`AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` (env-overridable; defaults to `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees`; validates
`label` with `agent_scratch.sh`'s existing `_agent_scratch_valid_component`, reused only for that
validation, NOT for root selection — see the Round-4b correction above for why this must NOT call
`agent_scratch_create`), naming the leaf `<label>-$$-$(date +%s)`, then runs `git worktree add
<that-path> <ref>` against the CALLING repo (i.e. `git -C <repo> worktree add ...`, taking the repo
path as an explicit third argument, never inferring cwd), and prints the resulting worktree path on
success. Also proves it REJECTS: an empty `label`, an empty `ref`, and a `repo` argument that is not
a git repository (`git -C <repo> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails) — in all three cases,
`agent_worktree_create` must exit non-zero and must NOT create any directory or worktree.
**Round-6 addition (2026-09-25, independent Codex + Opus closure-round review, both flagged the same
gap):** also proves it REJECTS a pre-existing `$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` that is a symlink (dynamic test,
via `ln -s`). **Round-6b correction (2026-09-25, second Opus re-review): the not-owned-by-current-user
case does NOT need a second uid to test dynamically** — pointing `AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` at an
EXISTING directory the test user doesn't own (`/private/var/tmp` itself, `root:wheel`) exercises the
real rejection path without creating anything new; a prior draft wrongly claimed this needed a
second uid and settled for a source-grep instead, which the reviewer showed would still pass even if
the ownership check were moved to the wrong place in the function. Guard the case with `[[ $EUID -ne
0 ]]` so it degrades to a documented skip only when literally running as root. Owned file:
`tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` only (new). Line budget: ~120 new lines.

## Reuse
`tests/test_agent_scratch.sh`'s own test-isolation convention (read it in full first): create a
throwaway `mktemp -d` sandbox git repo as the "calling repo" fixture (`git init` inside it, one
commit so `HEAD` is a valid ref), override `AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` to a second `mktemp -d` sandbox so
no test ever touches the real `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees`, and reuse
`tests/test_agent_scratch.sh`'s `record_pass`/`record_fail`/`PASS`/`FAIL` counter pattern verbatim.
`_agent_scratch_valid_component` from `agent_scratch.sh` is sourced and called for label validation
only.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `MISSING`).
2. Create `tests/test_agent_worktree.sh`:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_agent_worktree.sh — Behavioral tests for scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh"
SCRATCH_LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh"

FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d -t agent_worktree_test_root.XXXXXX)"
export AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT="$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"

FAKE_REPO="$(mktemp -d -t agent_worktree_test_repo.XXXXXX)"
git -C "$FAKE_REPO" init -q
git -C "$FAKE_REPO" commit -q --allow-empty -m "fixture commit"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
record_pass() { echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$(( PASS + 1 )); }
record_fail() { echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 )); }

# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$SCRATCH_LIB"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh
source "$LIB"

path=$(agent_worktree_create "verify" "HEAD" "$FAKE_REPO")
if [[ -n "$path" && -d "$path" ]]; then record_pass "worktree dir created"; else record_fail "worktree dir not created"; fi
if [[ -n "$path" ]] && git -C "$FAKE_REPO" worktree list | grep -qF "$path"; then record_pass "git worktree list shows the new worktree"; else record_fail "git worktree list missing entry"; fi
if [[ -n "$path" && "$path" == "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT/"* ]]; then record_pass "worktree lands under AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT (never under agent-scratch)"; else record_fail "wrong parent root: $path"; fi

if agent_worktree_create "" "HEAD" "$FAKE_REPO" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "empty label accepted"; else record_pass "empty label rejected"; fi
if agent_worktree_create "verify2" "" "$FAKE_REPO" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "empty ref accepted"; else record_pass "empty ref rejected"; fi
NOT_A_REPO="$(mktemp -d -t agent_worktree_test_notrepo.XXXXXX)"
if agent_worktree_create "verify3" "HEAD" "$NOT_A_REPO" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "non-repo path accepted"; else record_pass "non-repo path rejected"; fi
shopt -s nullglob
verify3_leaves=("$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"/verify3*)
shopt -u nullglob
if [[ ${#verify3_leaves[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then record_fail "non-repo rejection still created a dir"; else record_pass "non-repo rejection created no dir"; fi

# Round-6: reject a pre-existing symlinked root (world-writable-sticky
# /private/var/tmp parent means another local actor could pre-create this).
rm -rf "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"
SYMLINK_TARGET="$(mktemp -d -t agent_worktree_test_symlink_target.XXXXXX)"
ln -s "$SYMLINK_TARGET" "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"
if agent_worktree_create "verify4" "HEAD" "$FAKE_REPO" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "symlinked root accepted"; else record_pass "symlinked root rejected"; fi
rm -f "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT"

# Round-6b (2026-09-25, second Opus re-review): a REAL dynamic test for the
# not-owned-by-current-user rejection does NOT need a second uid — point
# AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT at an EXISTING directory this user doesn't own
# instead of creating one. /private/var/tmp itself (root:wheel) works.
# Skip only when literally running as root (EUID 0), where "not owned by
# current user" can't be constructed at all.
if [[ "$EUID" -ne 0 && -d /private/var/tmp ]]; then
  if AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT=/private/var/tmp agent_worktree_create "verify5" "HEAD" "$FAKE_REPO" 2>/dev/null; then
    record_fail "not-owned root accepted"
  else
    record_pass "not-owned root rejected"
  fi
  if git -C "$FAKE_REPO" worktree list | grep -qF "/private/var/tmp/verify5"; then
    record_fail "not-owned-root rejection still registered a worktree"
  else
    record_pass "not-owned-root rejection created no worktree"
  fi
else
  record_pass "not-owned root rejected (skipped: running as root, EUID=$EUID)"
  record_pass "not-owned-root rejection created no worktree (skipped: running as root, EUID=$EUID)"
fi

rm -rf "$FAKE_WORKTREE_ROOT" "$FAKE_REPO" "$NOT_A_REPO" "$SYMLINK_TARGET"

echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]]
```
3. Make it executable: `chmod +x tests/test_agent_worktree.sh`.

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` — expect a `source` failure (`scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh`
does not exist yet) and non-zero exit. This IS the expected RED state for a TEST-only bead (no
implementation exists yet); do not attempt to make the source succeed in this bead.

## GREEN
Not applicable to this TEST bead — GREEN is proven by the paired IMPL bead
(disk_magician-orchestrator-worktree-not-clone-2nw, redesigned scope) after it creates
`scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh`.

## Do not
Do not create `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh` in this bead. Do not modify
`tests/test_agent_scratch.sh` or any other existing test file.

## Stop when

title: backup-home.sh: 61 rsync timeouts (124/137) on deep dirs fail the whole run
description:
Measured 2026-10-24 on the Mac. A user-scope backup run exited 1 during the local git rsync phase because 61 items timed out (exit 124/137) on deep directories (~/.cursor/chats, ~/.codex/memories). The cloud phase (rclone -> Dropbox conversation-backups) is healthy: PID 12903, nice 20, active TLS, streaming 786 MB / 74 MB / 870 MB / 1.05 GB session transcripts, lock /private/var/tmp/backup-home.lock correctly held so cron triggers skip.

Impact: the timeout kills the whole run's success status, so a healthy cloud upload is reported as a failed backup -- exactly the 'commit is not deploy' class of false signal. It also means the local git mirror keeps its old content.

Fix shape (not implemented): per-item timeout should degrade to a logged SKIP with a count in the summary (like the #224 degraded gate), not fail the run; and the deep dirs likely need either a larger per-item timeout or exclusion of volatile subtrees (~/.cursor/chats, ~/.codex/memories) whose churn is what overruns it. Must keep the cloud phase authoritative: a partial local mirror must not mark the backup as failed when the rclone phase succeeded.

Do NOT tune this while PID 12903 is running; the lock is held and a concurrent run would be skipped anyway. Sequence: let the active transfer finish, then tune, then verify with one full run.

## Environment

## Goal
Create scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh, a standalone script that removes exactly one leaf scratch dir (`$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/<run-id>`), refusing to run when the runtime/run-id env vars are unset, when either value is not a valid single path component (rejecting traversal like `../../etc` or an embedded `/`), or when the resolved path would be `$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT` itself. Owned files: scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh (new), and `src/disk_magician/scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh` (new, generated by `sync_package_tree.sh` in Step 3, not hand-edited). Depends on: T6-TEST closed. Line budget: ~35 new lines. Explicitly out of scope: registering this as a Claude Code Stop/SessionEnd hook in ~/.claude/settings.json — that requires separate, explicit user approval (global user config outside this repo's ownership) and is not part of this bead.

## Reuse
scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh (T5-IMPL) — source it for the `AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT` default and the same `_agent_scratch_valid_component` validation logic this hook must apply to its own runtime/run-id inputs, so both accept/reject the same component shapes.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `EXISTS`; confirms T5-IMPL has landed).
2. Create scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh with this exact content, then `chmod +x scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh`:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh — removes exactly one leaf scratch dir
# ($AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/<run-id>) on session end. Refuses to run
# without both identifying env vars, and refuses to ever touch
# $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself. NOT wired into any hook config by this
# script — registration into ~/.claude/settings.json is a separate,
# approval-gated step (bead disk_magician-d45, spec section A3).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/agent_scratch.sh"

if [[ -z "${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME:-}" || -z "${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME and AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID must both be set" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Reuse the same component validator agent_scratch_create() applies (empty,
# path-traversal, and absolute/multi-segment components are all rejected) —
# an unvalidated runtime/run-id here would let a caller pass e.g.
# AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME="../../.." and rm -rf outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT.
if ! _agent_scratch_valid_component "$AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME"; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME is not a valid single path component" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! _agent_scratch_valid_component "$AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID"; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID is not a valid single path component" >&2
  exit 1
fi

leaf="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT}/${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME}/${AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID}"
if [[ "$leaf" == "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" || "$leaf" == "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/" ]]; then
  echo "agent_scratch_cleanup_hook: refusing — resolved path equals AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself" >&2
  exit 1
fi

rm -rf "$leaf"
```

## Goal
Create scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh implementing `agent_scratch_create`/`agent_scratch_trap_cleanup` (with a path-containment check and per-signal EXIT/INT/TERM trap preservation — round-3 `/advice` hardening, see Steps), and append one entry to config/sweeper_roots.txt registering `/private/tmp/agent-scratch`. Does NOT depend on T4-IMPL/bead k03 closing (round-4 correction, see Environment) — if it has already landed, Step 1's fresh read will show its entry; if not, this bead's own append is independent and does not need to wait. Line budget: ~70 new/changed lines.

## Steps
1. Run: `cat config/sweeper_roots.txt | tail -10` (read-only; locate the true current end of file before appending — do not assume its exact final line, and do not assume T4-IMPL's entry is present or absent, without checking).
2. Create scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck shell=bash
# agent_scratch.sh — managed scratch root for agent runtimes (bead
# disk_magician-d45 producer-side prevention: namespaced runtime/run-id
# subtree under $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT so budget eviction and a future
# Stop-hook cleanup script can target exactly a session's own scratch,
# without touching unrelated $TMPDIR entries left by other tools).
AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT:-/private/tmp/agent-scratch}"

_agent_scratch_valid_component() {
  # Reject empty, path-traversal, and absolute-path / multi-segment components.
  local c="$1"
  [[ -n "$c" && "$c" != *".."* && "$c" != /* && "$c" != *"/"* ]]
}

agent_scratch_create() {
  local runtime="$1" run_id="$2"
  _agent_scratch_valid_component "$runtime" || { echo "agent_scratch_create: invalid runtime" >&2; return 1; }
  _agent_scratch_valid_component "$run_id" || { echo "agent_scratch_create: invalid run-id" >&2; return 1; }
  local path="${AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT}/${runtime}/${run_id}"
  mkdir -p "$path"
  echo "$path"
}

agent_scratch_trap_cleanup() {
  # Containment check (round-3 /advice hardening): refuse to arm cleanup
  # unless the caller-supplied path canonicalizes (symlinks resolved) to a
  # genuine leaf strictly under AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/ — i.e. at
  # least two path segments below the canonicalized root, never the root
  # itself and never a bare <runtime> directory. This stops both a
  # symlink escape and an accidental "delete a whole runtime's scratch"
  # call.
  local path="$1" canon_root canon_path
  canon_root="$(cd "$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || {
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT does not exist, refusing: $AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT" >&2
    return 1
  }
  if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: path does not exist, refusing: $path" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  canon_path="$(cd "$path" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || {
    echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: cannot canonicalize path, refusing: $path" >&2
    return 1
  }
  case "$canon_path" in
    "$canon_root"/*/*) ;;
    *)
      echo "agent_scratch_trap_cleanup: refusing — $canon_path is not a leaf strictly under $canon_root/<runtime>/" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  # Preserve each of EXIT/INT/TERM's own pre-existing handler individually
  # (a caller may have set different handlers per signal) — setting one
  # combined trap string for all three signals, using only EXIT's prior
  # handler text, would silently drop a caller's own INT/TERM handlers.
  # Escape embedded single quotes in canon_path (round-3 /advice hardening
  # -- a filename containing "'" would otherwise break out of the quoted
  # rm -rf argument when interpolated into the trap command string).
  local sig existing escaped_path
  escaped_path="${canon_path//\'/\'\\\'\'}"
  for sig in EXIT INT TERM; do
    existing="$(trap -p "$sig" | sed -E "s/^trap -- '(.*)' (SIG)?${sig}\$/\1/")"
    if [[ "$sig" == "EXIT" ]]; then
      trap "rm -rf '${escaped_path}'; ${existing}" "$sig"
    else
      # INT/TERM (round-3 /advice hardening): after cleanup + any prior
      # handler, re-raise the signal against ourselves with default
      # disposition restored, so the process actually terminates as the
      # caller expects on Ctrl-C/kill instead of silently continuing past
      # the now-deleted directory.
      trap "rm -rf '${escaped_path}'; ${existing:+${existing}; }trap - ${sig}; kill -s ${sig} \$BASHPID" "$sig"
    fi
  done
}
```
   Then run `chmod +x scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh`.
3. Edit config/sweeper_roots.txt: append this entry after the true current end of file (confirmed in Step 1):

title: TEST: agent_scratch.sh helper library
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #72 + PR #73 merged. Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Create tests/test_agent_scratch.sh proving a not-yet-created scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh provides `agent_scratch_create <runtime> <run-id>` (creates and prints a namespaced dir under `$AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT`, rejects empty/traversal/absolute components) and `agent_scratch_trap_cleanup <path>` (sets EXIT/INT/TERM traps that remove `<path>`, each preserving that SAME signal's own pre-existing handler individually — not just re-using EXIT's handler text for all three — and independently refuses to arm cleanup on any path that is not a genuine leaf strictly under `AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/`, even if the caller bypasses `agent_scratch_create` and hand-constructs the path). Owned file: tests/test_agent_scratch.sh only (new). Depends on: PR #72 merged (no direct code dependency, but sequenced with the rest of this plan's PR-73-first gate). Line budget: ~85 new lines.

## Reuse
No existing file in this repo defines an equivalent helper; this is a new pattern. Follow the general test-isolation convention already used throughout this repo's test suite (e.g. tests/test_cleanup_claude_state.sh lines 12-17: `TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d ...)` + `trap cleanup EXIT` at file scope) — but for `AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT` itself, override it to a `mktemp -d` sandbox via environment variable, never exercise the real `/private/tmp/agent-scratch` path from a test.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `MISSING`).
2. Create tests/test_agent_scratch.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_agent_scratch.sh — Behavioral tests for scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh"

FAKE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d -t agent_scratch_test.XXXXXX)"
export AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
record_pass() { echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$(( PASS + 1 )); }
record_fail() { echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 )); }

# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$LIB"

path=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run123")
if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then record_pass "scratch dir created"; else record_fail "scratch dir not created"; fi
if [[ "$path" == "$FAKE_ROOT/testruntime/run123" ]]; then record_pass "correct path shape"; else record_fail "wrong path shape: $path"; fi

if agent_scratch_create "" "run123" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "empty runtime accepted"; else record_pass "empty runtime rejected"; fi
if agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "../escape" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "traversal accepted"; else record_pass "traversal rejected"; fi
if agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "/abs" 2>/dev/null; then record_fail "absolute run-id accepted"; else record_pass "absolute run-id rejected"; fi

(
  trap 'echo caller-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/caller_trap_marker"' EXIT
  agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$path"
  exit 0
)
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/caller_trap_marker" ]]; then record_pass "caller's own EXIT trap still ran (chained, not clobbered)"; else record_fail "caller's own EXIT trap was overwritten"; fi
if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then record_pass "trap cleanup removed the scratch dir"; else record_fail "trap cleanup did not remove the scratch dir"; fi

# INT is a DIFFERENT signal from EXIT with its OWN pre-existing handler —
# a correct implementation must preserve each signal's own prior handler,
# not just re-apply EXIT's handler text to all three signals.
path2=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run789")
(
  trap 'echo exit-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/exit_marker"' EXIT
  trap 'echo int-trap-ran > "'"$FAKE_ROOT"'/int_marker"' INT
  agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$path2"
  kill -INT $BASHPID
  echo "unreachable" > "$FAKE_ROOT/unreachable_marker"
)
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/int_marker" ]]; then record_pass "caller's own INT trap still ran (preserved, not overwritten by EXIT's handler)"; else record_fail "caller's own INT trap was lost"; fi
if [[ -f "$FAKE_ROOT/unreachable_marker" ]]; then record_fail "subshell kept running after INT instead of terminating (signal re-raise is missing)"; else record_pass "subshell actually terminated on INT (signal correctly re-raised, not swallowed)"; fi

# Containment check: agent_scratch_trap_cleanup must independently refuse
# to arm cleanup on a path that is not a genuine leaf strictly under
# AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT/<runtime>/ — even if the caller bypasses
# agent_scratch_create and hand-constructs a bad path.
outside_dir="$(mktemp -d -t agent_scratch_outside.XXXXXX)"
if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$outside_dir" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted a path entirely outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects a path entirely outside AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT"
fi
[[ -d "$outside_dir" ]] && record_pass "outside-root dir was never deleted" || record_fail "outside-root dir was deleted"
rm -rf "$outside_dir"

if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$FAKE_ROOT" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT itself"
fi

mkdir -p "$FAKE_ROOT/bareruntime"
if (AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT" agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "$FAKE_ROOT/bareruntime" 2>/dev/null); then
  record_fail "trap_cleanup accepted a bare <runtime> dir (only one segment below root)"
else
  record_pass "trap_cleanup rejects a bare <runtime> dir (only one segment below root)"
fi

# Round-3 /advice hardening: a leaf path containing a literal single quote
# must not break the quoted rm -rf interpolation inside the trap string.
quote_leaf=$(agent_scratch_create "testruntime" "run_with_quote")
mv "$quote_leaf" "${quote_leaf}o'clock" 2>/dev/null || true
if [[ -d "${quote_leaf}o'clock" ]]; then
  (
    trap 'true' EXIT
    agent_scratch_trap_cleanup "${quote_leaf}o'clock"
    exit 0
  )
  if [[ ! -d "${quote_leaf}o'clock" ]]; then
    record_pass "trap_cleanup correctly removes a leaf path containing a single quote"
  else
    record_fail "trap_cleanup left a quote-containing leaf path in place"
  fi
else
  record_fail "test setup could not create a quote-containing fixture path (filesystem may not support it)"
fi

rm -rf "$FAKE_ROOT"

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All agent_scratch tests passed."
```

title: cleanup_tmp archives non-purgeable dirs to same volume — archive regrows (zero acute relief)
description:
## Symptom
`/private/tmp/_disk_magician_archive` is a retention reservoir on the SAME volume as /private/tmp. `cleanup_tmp.sh --large` archives candidate dirs into it and purges none until retention (>24h) expires — so while producers outpace the 24h purge the archive only grows, giving zero acute free-space relief.

## Evidence (2026-10-16 session)
- Another agent measured the archive growing 20.3 -> 23.4 GiB in one session while `cleanup_tmp --large` "freed nothing".
- C14 kept-candidate reasons across 78 checks: unpushed commits 21, no recorded baseline 20, uncommitted changes 19, secret-like files 10, check failed 6, external worktree 1, archive identity mismatch 1.
- In this session the archive only dropped 30G -> 10G when the aged (>24h) purge actually ran.

## Root cause
Candidates that C14 will never release (secret-like / check-failed / identity-mismatch) are archived anyway and accumulate indefinitely; archiving to the same volume frees no space.

## Expected / acceptance
1. Do not archive entries that cannot be purged by retention (or evict/cap them); the archive must be size-bounded.
2. A regression test proving a secret-like / check-failed archive entry cannot silently accumulate (fails closed, and the archive does not grow unbounded).

title: attribution: split the overcount into hardlink duplicates (recoverable via inode tracking) and clone extents (need getattrlist CLONEID or a named residual)
description: Per-root attribution is inflated by two DIFFERENT mechanisms, and only one of them is recoverable. Controlled evidence 2026-10-13 (200 MB payload + one hardlink + one APFS clone, measured with du -sk): true content 200 MB; a SINGLE du invocation reports 381 MB (it dedups the hardlink but cannot see clone extents); SEPARATE per-child du invocations -- which is what disk_frontier_scan measures -- report 572 MB, i.e. 3x the content, double-counting BOTH the hardlink and the clone. On the live volume the same effect produces sum(top_level_ledger.measured_kb)=1057.9 GiB against disk_used=856.2 GiB. Fix, in two parts: (1) RECOVERABLE -- make the scan hardlink-aware: the frontier walk already lstats nodes, so track (st_dev, st_ino) for nodes with st_nlink > 1 and attribute/skip duplicates, so per-root values stop double-counting hardlinks. (2) NOT RECOVERABLE BY du -- clone-shared extents: either measure them with getattrlist(ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID) where available and attribute each clone group to its canonical (first-seen) owner, or keep reporting the clone component as a named global residual. Required reporting: split the current single clone_shared_adjustment_kb into hardlink_duplicate_kb (excluded from per-root values, attributable) and clone_shared_kb (remaining), so the residual has a named cause instead of one opaque number. Acceptance: a fixture with a hardlinked file measured per-child excludes the duplicate; sum(per-root attributed) + clone_shared_kb + purgeable_kb + residual_kb == disk_used_kb; per_path_comparable is true whenever the clone component is inside PER_PATH_TOLERANCE_RATIO; per-path deltas then reconcile with the disk_used delta in 'diskm history diff'; tests for both components.

title: Runaway cursor-agent-logs-501 session log growing ~18.5 GiB/day, single file
description: 2026-07-29, found by measurement teammate during disk_magician-7io mission Lane 1 (measure-topdown.md): /private/var/folders/j0/byd1z6px50v88lf679bgt0h00000gn/T/cursor-agent-logs-501/session-2026-07-27T03-00-48-477Z-95634-1.log grew from 25.60 GiB (2026-07-28T11:23:50Z, frontier scan capture) to 42.24 GiB (2026-07-29T08:56 UTC fresh check) -- +16.6 GiB in ~21.5 hours, ~0.77 GiB/hr, ~18.5 GiB/day sustained, actively growing right now (mtime = capture minute). This is a single log file from a Cursor CLI agent session started 2026-07-27T03:00:48Z that has apparently never rotated or been truncated in over 2 days of continuous writing. This is likely the single largest, most precisely-quantified, most actionable individual producer found in the entire root-cause investigation -- larger in daily rate than any other single named item. Root cause candidates: (1) a stuck/runaway cursor-agent process writing verbose/duplicate output in a loop, (2) a missing log-rotation policy for cursor-agent-logs-501 sessions. Recommended fix: identify and kill/restart the owning cursor-agent session if still running (check via lsof or ps on the log path), add log rotation (size cap + truncate-on-restart) to cursor-agent's logging config, and safety_check.sh-gated truncation of the existing 42+ GiB file (do not blind rm -- verify the owning session is not mid-task first). Cite: roadmap/2026-07-29-disk-regrowth-rootcause-sidekick.md, measure-topdown.md in the sidekick STATE dir.
close_reason: Root-caused 2026-07-29: cursor-agent always-on debug log (no rotation/size cap, no vendor logging config per official CLI docs), stack traces on routine events, commitScoring loop iterating full repo history (1-2 events/commit, ~100 commits/s) in a 2.5-day headless session => 45GB at ~18.5 GiB/day. Log reclaimed by another operator agent 2026-07-29 ~02:30 PDT (+37 GiB free). Findings: findings_wiki/cursor-agent-debug-log-unbounded-growth.md (commit 8b1ff1a). Prevention follow-up: disk_magician-rvf.

comments.text: CONFIRMED live and actively writing: lsof shows PID 95634 (node process) has this file open (FD 27w) right now, file is 45,519,296,373 bytes (~42.4 GiB) as of this check. Process has been running since session start 2026-07-27T03:00:48Z (2+ days). This is a live, identified, currently-growing target -- not speculative. comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-29):

Origin: PID 95634 started from bash session PID 20665 (terminal s030, launched Sun Jul 26 18:51:45) via 'agent --use-system-ca ... --force --continue'. No launchd job — manual launch.

Bug: cursor-agent's commitScoring subsystem entered infinite loop over worldarchitect.ai git history (~2M packed objects). Every commit returned noHashData + scored all-zeros. Loop never terminated. No log rotation policy.

Resolution: kill 95634 + truncate log. 43 GB freed. Disk: 825GB used → 797GB used (67 GB free). PID confirmed dead, did not respawn.

Prevention gaps:
1. No log rotation for cursor-agent-logs-501/ — need size cap (e.g. logrotate or launchd StandardOutPath cap)
2. commitScoring loop has no circuit-breaker in Cursor agent — upstream bug
3. Parent bash session PID 20665 still alive — if someone runs cursor --continue from s030 it could restart

Next: add log size monitor to disk_magician (watch cursor-agent-logs-501/ for files > 1GB) so this is caught in minutes not days.

title: 225 GiB stuck in /private/var/dirs_cleaner staging dirs — deferred-delete mechanism failing, needs root action
description: Confirmed via sudo -n du (passwordless, du-scoped) + Apple's own dirs_cleaner(8) man page: /private/var/dirs_cleaner holds 225.3 GiB across 9 randomized-name (mktemp-style) staging subdirs (41=107G,1L=36G,xu=20G,QW=19G,bT=16G,B8=12G,Zn=8.2G,p0=4.4G,NQ=2.6G). This is Apple's directory-content-deletion utility's staging area; content here represents stuff that was supposed to be deleted but the async-delete mechanism failed to complete. A crash report exists for this exact process dated 2026-07-16 (~/Library/Application Support/CrashReporter/dirs_cleaner_93B5DEFF-2F8B-585A-8B39-9B93E51BD132.plist) but 9 separate batches suggest repeated failures, not one event. One entry under xu/ has a corrupted filename that is a mangled $PATH string with an iso_bin_ prefix -- possible Colima/Lima connection. Accounts for 225.3 of the session's 277 GiB unmeasured residual (91% combined with Spotlight's 26 GiB). NOT remediated: requires real root (session's sudo grant is du-only, no delete capability) to either re-run dirs_cleaner properly or investigate+fix why the deferred-delete mechanism keeps failing before clearing the backlog (same failure would recur otherwise). Full writeup: roadmap/2026-08-02-research-persistent-eintr-root-cause.md.
close_reason: REMEDIATED 2026-08-02 18:30 PDT: deleted all 225.3 GiB across 10 batches via find -delete (fd-relative, avoids Apple's own removefile()/ENAMETOOLONG bug), zero errors, verified via sudo du (0B) and df (271.8 GiB free, up from 99.4 GiB). Root cause confirmed via unified log: deleted_helper's nuke_dir fails on a pathological long/corrupted filename under one batch (xu/), aborting every purge pass. This is Apple's own bug in CacheDelete.framework, not fixable by us -- may recur if deleted_helper stages new content and hits the same or a similar long path again; re-run the same procedure if so. Full writeup: roadmap/2026-08-02-research-dirs-cleaner-os-mechanism.md.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:
Rule recorded 2026-10-24 on branch fix/code-sign-clone-shared-inode-v2 (draft PR #261).

(The previous comment on this bead was mangled by shell command substitution inside backticks; this is the corrected text.)

The /advice requirement is implemented as stated: preserve a clone when it was created at or after the OLDEST live shared-handle holder's start time, read per pid with `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=`, and fail closed when that start time or the clone mtime is unreadable. Keeping "only the newest" (the last shape of PR #113) is NOT what shipped; the launch-time keep-set is a superset of it. Tests cover a two-live-holder parent (Test 13) and an unreadable-start-time case (Test 14) in tests/test_cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh.

Two measurements that shape the deliverable:
- Performance: per-pid ps only. A global `ps -Ao comm=` costs 2m15s with 2071 processes on this host versus 11 ms per pid, so a global snapshot per candidate made one --clean run take 3m18s for two candidates.
- Reclaim: confirmed ~0 again today with a controlled cp -c fixture (300 MB source plus 2 clones = 921,600 KB of du but only 300.8 MB of df; deleting both clones returned ~0 MB). The classifier therefore reports shared-inode-only clones as SHARED-INODE and does not count them as reclaimable, and it does not attempt removals that C14's inode-based gates (kept:open-file / kept:live-user) refuse anyway: see disk_magician-codesign-c14-shared-inode-gate-ljmx.

Given this bead's own gating condition (only worth doing if clone accumulation shows real df cost), the remaining work is the C14 relaxation, tracked separately at P4.

title: Programmatic FileProvider eviction for cloud storage mirrors (Dropbox conversation-backups)
description: Integrate programmatic FileProvider eviction via NSFileManager/FileProvider APIs into disk_magician to keep cloud mirror directories (such as Dropbox conversation-backups) in a dataless online-only state. Prevents 19.85+ GiB of duplicate local SSD consumption without requiring manual Finder GUI interaction or UI automation.
acceptance_criteria: FileProvider eviction runs programmatically without UI clicks; validates files in cloud storage become dataless (st_blocks == 0); logs reclaimed space to deletions.log

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text: INTEGRATED 2026-10-24 measured facts: Dropbox conversation-backups holds ~18 GiB PHYSICAL across ~874k files (834k already dataless), primarily codex_conversations/sessions -- and it DUPLICATES the canonical ~/.codex/sessions, so eviction loses nothing. Eviction verified on a 49 MB file plus a 100-file batch: physical blocks -> 0, no cursor/focus disruption, via FileManager.evictUbiquitousItem(at:) / FPEvictItemAtURL. Dropbox claude/codex/cursor/dot_conversations roots are already 100% dataless (st_blocks=0), and Google Drive is 667.39 GiB apparent / 0.00 GiB physical -- do NOT chase either. Zero-code fallback for the operator today: Finder -> right-click conversation-backups -> 'Remove Download'. Caveat for the helper: dataless files re-materialise on access, so the reclaim is not permanent; log evictions and report st_blocks, never du -sh.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text: 2026-10-24 PR https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/268 (draft) adds 'diskm evict-fileprovider' (dry-run default; --clean + FILEPROVIDER_EVICT_APPROVED=1). BLOCKER FOUND: Dropbox is currently UNLINKED (uploadingError -1004 'unlinked Dropbox'); provider reports uploaded=false for all 52,918 materialized files (19.851 GiB) and FileManager.evictUbiquitousItem returns -2008 'cannot be evicted' on a test file. Real run reclaims ~0 until Dropbox is re-linked and uploads finish. fileproviderctl has no evict subcommand.

title: Attribute the 18.0 GiB / 29.8 min anonymous step event (2026-09-12T00:07:40Z): mtime-based (in-place growth) + roots ~/.codex ~/projects ~/Library
description: Birth-time probe (disk_magician-6wd, refuted) proved 0 newborn bytes under /private/tmp, $TMPDIR/T, ~/.cache, ~/roadmap/evidence in the window. Remaining hypotheses: append-only growth of existing files (~/.codex/*.sqlite + sessions, cursor logs, jsonl) or newborn files under un-probed roots. Design a bounded find -newermt/-mmin probe per hot dir + stat size deltas; treat as detection only. Also fix report §6 claim: stat -f %b does not dedupe APFS clones (verified cp -c).
close_reason: 2026-09-24 lane D: 09-12 event and two fresh events unattributable via file birth/mtime probes (92% unexplained on the fully-probed event); root-cause class moved to non-file signals — tracked in the oscillation follow-up bead.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text: Lane D 2026-09-24: fresh probe, 2 most recent growth events. Event +9GiB (03:02-03:36): all 7 named roots + snapshots/code_sign_clone/Xcode measured, only ~0.75GiB (8%) accounted (TMPDIR 751MB, .codex 17MB, projects 2.9MB, rest ~0). Event +20GiB (19:39-20:16): /private/tmp newborn=71506 files/2.8GB (14%), other roots timed out (71k-file stat too slow, not zero, unmeasured). Verdict: unattributable-with-reason for event1; inconclusive for event2. Full 10-day walk (374 commits) shows 80+ swings >=8GiB in BOTH directions incl a -62GiB/54min drop -- pattern looks like df-visible purgeable/container accounting churn, not a discrete leaking process. title: worktree_hygiene.sh dependency-dir pyc continue skips never-exempt names (.env.pyc, id_rsa*.pyc)
description: Found by /advice r8 on PR #214 (Opus): scripts/worktree_hygiene.sh dependency-dir .pyc continue (~584-586) exempts more than exempt_name() in scripts/c14_probe.py, which checks never-exempt names (.env*, id_rsa*, id_ed25519*, id_ecdsa*, id_dsa*) first. An untracked non-ignored node_modules/p/.env.pyc passes hygiene and could be pushed by --push-wip. cleanup_tmp.sh:860 archive_classify has the same mismatch but is still stricter than main. Fix: case guard on those basenames before the continue; add parity test. Ref: /tmp/disk_magician/advice-receipts/pr214-r8/opus.out on jeff-ubuntu.

title: Ubuntu host disk: 100G emergency reclaim requires an operator decision on real data, not cache sweeping
description:
Measured 2026-10-31 on jeff-ubuntu: / (nvme0n1p6) 884G with 816G used and ~23G free (98%), which is BELOW the 30G ezgha runner admission floor, so the Linux runner fleet pauses. /home/jleechan/Scratch is a 195.8G ext4 loop image inside / with 194.6G used and ~1.2G free internal; the image file itself is 197G allocated of 200G apparent, so freeing inside the image returns ~nothing to / (fstrim would recover only ~2G and needs root). /tmp holds only 4.4 GiB in total.

What ran (all canonical) and yielded: pressure-sweep 0 (step 1 skipped: scratch lock held; colima 0; code-sign 0), cleanup_dev_caches 217 MB (uv/npm/cursor kept as recent-activity/open-file/secret-like), cleanup_tmp kept nearly everything inside the 24h window and could not finish a full pass. Net ~0.2G.

Where the 816G is: .local 220G (includes the 197G Scratch image), .worktrees 193G, mirror 76G, projects 58G, Dropbox 32G, .codex 24G, projects_other 16G, .config 15G, ComfyUI 13G, .cache 12G.

Options requiring an operator decision: (A) prune ~/.worktrees with cleanup_worktrees.sh --clean (WORKTREE_APPROVED=1, 3-day floor, clean/pushed/merged gates); a partial dry-run showed 238 PRESERVE vs 13 ELIGIBLE so the yield is unknown until a full pass; (B) relocate ~/mirror (76G) to /media/jleechan/3C1EB3681EB31A3A which has 354G free on a separate 965G device (worktrees cannot be moved - absolute paths); (C) sudo fstrim ~/Scratch, ~2G only.

Acceptance: free space back above the 30G admission floor without deleting unapproved user data; record df before/after and the exact removals.

title: br exports beads to ~/.beads instead of the repo's tracked .beads when a worktree has no local DB
description: In a disk_magician worktree, br exports to the FALLBACK database instead of the repo's tracked .beads: the worktree has .beads/{config.yaml,issues.jsonl,metadata.json} but no .beads/*.db, so br resolves ~/.beads/beads.db and writes/export its JSONL to ~/.beads/issues.jsonl. Consequence (2026-10-12): seven beads created in the worktree were reportable by 'br show'/'br list' with the correct disk_magician prefix, but never appeared in the repo's tracked .beads/issues.jsonl, so a remote lane reading the repo on GitHub could not see them ('br sync --flush-only' said 'Nothing to export (no dirty issues)' while 'br sync --status' had said 'Database is newer (export recommended)'). Fix: make the export path follow the discovered .beads directory (or create/materialize a local DB there), and make 'br sync --status'/'--flush-only' agree. Acceptance: a bead created in a fresh worktree appears in that worktree's .beads/issues.jsonl after 'br sync --flush-only', and 'br vcs-status' reports the export worktree-clean.

title: APPROVED 2026-09-24: wire agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh into ~/.claude/settings.json
description:
## Environment
**APPROVED 2026-09-24** by the user ("finish all" — explicit authorization to execute all three
previously approval-gated beads in this epic, recorded live). Repo/target: `~/.claude/settings.json`
(global, cross-project Claude Code config — NOT inside any git-tracked repo this session owns) plus
`scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh` in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician (already
built by bead disk_magician-agent-scratch-cleanup-hook-impl-o4z / T6-IMPL).

## Goal
Register `scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh` as a Claude Code Stop/SessionEnd hook in
`~/.claude/settings.json`, so a session's own `/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>` is
removed automatically when the session ends. Owned file: `~/.claude/settings.json` only.

## Reuse
`scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh`'s own contract (from T6-IMPL): requires
`AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME` and `AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID` env vars to be set by whatever invokes it;
refuses to run otherwise. Confirmed live in `~/.claude/settings.json`: the `hooks` top-level key
already has a `Stop` array (not `SessionEnd` — use `Stop`), shape `[{"matcher": "*", "hooks":
[{"type": "command", "command": "<shell string>"}]}]` — see the existing entry invoking
`cross_cli_status.py`. Confirmed live in `~/.claude/hooks/cross_cli_status.py` (lines ~170, ~460-470):
Claude Code's Stop hook does NOT pass session data via env vars — it writes a JSON payload to the
hook command's **stdin**, containing (among other fields) `session_id`. Wiring env-var-based
`agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh` therefore requires a small inline wrapper that reads stdin, extracts
`session_id` with `python3`, and re-invokes the hook script with the env vars set — mirroring the
existing `bash -c "..."` wrapper pattern already used for the `PreToolUse`/`Stop` entries in this
same file.

## Steps
1. Read `~/.claude/settings.json` in full. Back up its current content by copying to
   `~/.claude/settings.json.bak-$(date +%s)` before editing — this is a live, shared config file, and
   a malformed edit can break every Claude Code session on the machine.
2. Edit the file with `python3 -c "import json; ..."` or the Edit tool (either is fine — the only
   requirement is the file stays valid JSON per Step 3). Append this exact object to the existing
   `hooks.Stop[0].hooks` array (confirmed live as of 2026-09-24: `hooks.Stop` is a one-element array
   whose `[0].hooks` is itself an array with one entry, the `cross_cli_status.py` command; append as
   its second element). If `hooks.Stop[0].hooks` does not exist in that exact shape when you read the
   file in Step 1 (i.e. the live file has drifted since 2026-09-24), STOP and report the actual
   current `hooks` key content instead of guessing an insertion point. Do not remove or reorder any
   existing entry in that array or elsewhere in the file:
```json
{
  "type": "command",
  "command": "bash -c 'p=$(cat); rid=$(printf %s \"$p\" | python3 -c \"import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get(\\\"session_id\\\") or \\\"unknown\\\")\"); AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME=claude-code AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID=\"$rid\" /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician/scripts/agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh || true'"
}
```
   The trailing `|| true` is intentional and matches this file's existing `Stop` entry's own
   fail-open pattern (its command ends `; exit 0`) — a cleanup-hook failure must never block or
   surface an error in the user's Claude Code session.
3. Validate the file is still syntactically valid JSON: `python3 -m json.tool ~/.claude/settings.json
   > /dev/null`.

## RED
Not applicable (config-wiring bead, not a code change with its own test suite) — GREEN is the
functional proof below.

## GREEN
Trigger a real Claude Code session Stop/SessionEnd event with
`AGENT_SCRATCH_RUNTIME`/`AGENT_SCRATCH_RUN_ID` populated and confirm the corresponding
`/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>` directory no longer exists afterward.

## Do not
Do not touch any key in `~/.claude/settings.json` other than the hooks array entry described above.
Do not assume this session's own hook schema without checking current documentation or an existing
entry first. Do not skip the backup in Step 1.

## Stop when
`~/.claude/settings.json` is not valid JSON before you start editing, or the backup in Step 1 cannot
be written — stop and report the exact error instead of proceeding on a file you cannot safely roll
back.

## Report
Run: `br --no-auto-flush comments add <THIS-BEAD-ID> "$(python3 -m json.tool ~/.claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo 'settings.json valid; hook entry added' || echo 'settings.json INVALID after edit')"`

## Criteria
| ID | Check command | External anchor | Verifier | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HW1 | `grep -q 'agent_scratch_cleanup_hook.sh' ~/.claude/settings.json && python3 -m json.tool ~/.claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo PASS HW1 \|\| echo FAIL HW1` | Live global settings file | Independent re-execution by a reviewer other than the implementer | FAIL |

title: Fix lsof regex in cleanup_tmp.sh line 531 rejecting f*000 and blocking archive purge
description:
## Context & Symptom
In /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh, `has_open_files()` parses `lsof -F fnt` output to verify whether an archive candidate has open file descriptors. On macOS, `lsof` can emit descriptor values like `f*000` (e.g. for sockets, unallocated descriptors, or synthetic descriptors).

Line 531 previously used:
```bash
if ! [[ "$val" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$ ]]; then
  malformed=1
  break
fi
```
When encountering `*000`, the regex fails to match, flagging `malformed=1`. Because `has_open_files()` fails closed on malformed output, it marks the directory as having open files. As a result, `purge_aged_archives()` cannot delete 7.5+ GiB of aged archives in /private/tmp/_disk_magician_archive.

## Root Cause
macOS `lsof` file descriptor identifiers may begin with an asterisk (`*`) representing special state (such as `*000`). The validation regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$` did not allow a leading asterisk.

## Remediation Steps
1. Update regex in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh to `^\*?[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$`.
2. Also synchronize the packaged copy in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/src/disk_magician/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh.
3. Add a test case in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/tests/test_cleanup_tmp.sh verifying that `f*000` from `lsof -F fnt` is recognized as a valid descriptor and does not trigger `malformed=1`.
4. Run `cleanup_tmp.sh` to confirm /private/tmp/_disk_magician_archive aged items purge correctly.
