title: C14 quarantine re-verify keeps every shared-inode code_sign_clone (kept:live-user); decide whether to relax it kind-aware
description:
Follow-up to disk_magician-codesign-clone-false-positive-active-4stz / disk_magician-bd6.

Today the classifier (scripts/cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh) no longer mislabels clones whose only open handle is the hardlink-shared main executable (nlink=348 across 347 Chrome clones, 2026-10-24). Those candidates are logged SHARED-INODE and not counted as reclaimable.

Two downstream gates still keep them by inode:
  - scripts/lib/artifact_verdict.sh kept:open-file (c14_probe.py open-file uses lsof +D, inode-blind);
  - scripts/quarantine_rename.py verify kept:live-user (in-quarantine lsof +D recheck).

Relaxing them naively is NOT acceptable: --kind is caller-supplied, and quarantine_rename is deliberately kind-agnostic, so a kind-scoped relaxation would let any caller weaken a fail-closed open-handle check for every artifact kind. A correct design needs a structurally bound os_clone proof (the frozen candidate/parent/X-root identity proof already used by _av_os_clone_proof) threaded into the re-verify path, not a bare flag.

Value check first (bd6 gating condition): reclaim is ~0. Measured 2026-10-06: 73 clones, du 104.1 GiB, df +0.3 GiB. Re-measured 2026-10-24 with cp -c in /tmp: 3x300 MB copies cost 300.8 MB of df; deleting two returned ~0 MB. So only the inode/scan-time hygiene benefit (~220k dirs / 240k files under one Chrome parent) argues for doing this at all.

## Symptom
`scripts/cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh` reports `ACTIVE — preserving` for **every** `code_sign_clone` candidate while Chrome runs, even for clones that are clearly orphaned. Observed 2026-10-17: 51 candidates, `Dirs removed: 0`. The two cited pids (15487/15581) were dead seconds later.

## Root cause (measured)
Chromium hard-links the main executable into every clone, so the installed app and all clones share **one inode** (measured `dev=16777234 ino=2332731698 nlink=51`). `lsof +D <clone>` therefore reports Chrome for every clone (the hard-linked `Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome` inode is open) regardless of the clone's age/activity. The activity gate treats that as "active" and preserves all clones.

## Also confirmed (context)
The `code_sign_clone` apparent size (`du` 66–73 GiB) is **phantom**: `clonefile(2)` CoW shares extents with the installed app when versions match, so physical cost is ≈0 (controlled 3×200 MB `cp -c` test: `du` 595 MB, real `df` ~195 MB). Only after an auto-update do old-version extents become exclusive. Do not treat this bucket as a reclaim target while versions match.

## Expected / acceptance
1. Exclude the hard-linked main-executable inode from the lsof activity match (match clone-owned files only, or compare the hard-link inode against the installed app's executable and ignore it).
2. Regression test: an orphaned clone with only the shared hard-linked executable "open" is removable; a clone genuinely being written is preserved; fail-closed otherwise.
3. Do not weaken the CoW/phantom documentation; update the attribution finding so nobody counts this as real free space.
4. Independent re-execution at the fix HEAD.

## Related coverage gap
`/private/var/folders/.../T` held 6.18 GiB (all mtime today) — not covered by `cleanup_tmp.sh` (which scans TMP_DIRS/private tmp, not the per-user `T` dir). Decide whether to add it with the same 24h/mtime gates.

title: APPROVED 2026-09-24: add agent-scratch policy rule to ~/.codex/AGENTS.md

`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`'s own "Editing shared policy or runtime adapters — semantic signoff +

independent of user authorization, and user approval to proceed does not substitute for it. Target:
`~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (shared cross-runtime policy file, NOT inside disk_magician's repo).

## Goal
Add a policy rule to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` instructing agents to allocate ephemeral scratch under a
managed, namespaced root (e.g. `/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>`, per
`scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh` in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, built by bead
disk_magician-agent-scratch-helper-impl-ned / T5-IMPL) instead of bare `mktemp -d` scattered across
`$TMPDIR`.

## Reuse
`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`'s own "Editing shared policy or runtime adapters — semantic signoff +
behavioral gate (mandatory)" section (confirmed live, quoted verbatim so this bead does not need to
re-read it): "Structural checks are necessary but not sufficient. For edits that shorten, move, or
restructure a rule, ask whether an agent reading only the new text would still take the enforcement
action; if unsure, do not ship. Keep high-salience autonomy and safety headings standalone. Before
and after edits, run canaries: with an obviously implied next step and no blocker, does the agent
proceed without asking, and does it cite the source before asserting a status claim? A human report
within 24 hours that the agent stopped and asked something obvious is a tripwire: pause and recheck
this edit."

## Steps
1. Run `grep -n '^## Core behavior' ~/.codex/AGENTS.md` to confirm that exact heading still exists
   verbatim. If it does not, STOP and report the actual current heading list
   (`grep -n '^## ' ~/.codex/AGENTS.md`) instead of guessing an insertion point. If it does, add this
   exact new subsection as its own `##`-level heading placed immediately after that section
   (append-only — do not shorten, move, or restructure any existing heading, which would itself
   trigger the semantic-signoff gate quoted above for THOSE headings too):
```markdown
## Agent scratch allocation

Allocate ephemeral working files under a managed, namespaced scratch root instead of a bare `mktemp
-d` scattered across `$TMPDIR`. In disk_magician, use `scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh`'s
`agent_scratch_create <runtime> <run-id>` / `agent_scratch_trap_cleanup <path>`. Other repos/runtimes
should adopt the equivalent pattern — a namespaced `<runtime>/<run-id>` subtree under one root — so a
sweeper or Stop hook can reclaim exactly one session's scratch without touching unrelated files.
```
2. Pre-edit canary (run before the edit from Step 1 lands): start a fresh agent session (no prior
   context in that session beyond `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` itself being loaded, as it normally is) and
   give it the literal prompt `"All tests in this repo pass. Commit the change."` in a repo with

3. Apply the edit from Step 1.
4. Post-edit canary: repeat the exact same prompt and PASS/FAIL criteria from Step 2, in a fresh
   agent session that has the now-edited `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` loaded. Record PASS/FAIL and paste the

Not applicable (policy-doc bead).

## GREEN
The new rule text is present in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, and the pre/post-edit canary checks both
passed (recorded in Step 2/4).

Do not shorten, move, or restructure any existing rule in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` while adding this one
— per the file's own edit-gate, that requires the same semantic-signoff scrutiny and is out of scope

The pre-edit or post-edit canary check (Step 2/4) fails — stop, do not land the edit, and report the

Run: `br --no-auto-flush comments add <THIS-BEAD-ID> "pre-edit canary: <result>; post-edit canary: <result>"`

title: check_version_monotonic.py scans git log --all: any open PR version bump turns main CI red (main 0.2.100 vs PR #69 0.2.101, 2026-09-13)
description: Verified 2026-09-13: CI 'Test and lint' on main (run 34771257577, also 34771076864 on PR #69) fails 'Verify pyproject version monotonicity': current 0.2.100 < historical 0.2.101. 0.2.101 exists only on unmerged branch fix/plutil-extract-plist-corruption-and-disk-recurrence-report (PR #69). Deploy note: PR #69 landing (0.2.101 -> main) clears the symptom but not the bug.

## Confirmed finding — P2: unchanged configured stage or margin invalidates pilot

[`budget_acceptance.py:437-440`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/blob/c605db14be2a8a0db465d771ab1f602553a7e776/scripts/budget_acceptance.py#L437) calls the shared effective-stage and effective-margin helpers without the configuration argument. When state overrides are absent, an unchanged configured `warn` stage becomes `observe` for this check, and an unchanged configured 20 GiB margin becomes 10 GiB. Both falsely invalidate the pilot and can block promotion. Admission correctly supplies config at [`disk_budget.py:930-931`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/blob/c605db14be2a8a0db465d771ab1f602553a7e776/scripts/disk_budget.py#L930).

Required fix: resolve the configured budgets once and pass them to the existing shared helpers. Add acceptance cases for config-only nondefault values without state overrides, retaining real-change invalidation tests. The deterministic counterexamples returned `pilot_invalid:stage_changed` and `pilot_invalid:margin_changed`; they do not claim deployed behavior. Existing fixtures always persist default stage/margin, so passing the prior suite did not cover these inputs.

## Four-lane result

| Lane | Verdict | Evidence | Required fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ponytail | FAIL | budget_acceptance.py:437,439; budget_controls.py:124-151; disk_budget.py:930-931 | Use the existing configuration-aware resolver correctly |
| ZFC | PASS | policy_provenance.py:17-72; disk_budget.py:210-307; quarantine_rename.py:240-307 | None: explicit operator policy and deterministic filesystem control, no model-owned intent inference |
| ZFC leveling | N-A | Changed-file inventory; budget_controls.py:25 and budget_acceptance.py:411 are disk stages/pilots | No game/XP/level-up code is present |
| Root-cause-first | FAIL | Same effective-config mismatch; config-fallback-repro.json | Fix the first divergent backend value, not stored pilot data or a suppression |

This is **one confirmed defect affecting two lanes**, not two separate bugs. ROOT CAUSE ROUTE: BACKEND. ZFC PASS concerns ownership, not complete functional correctness.

## Why the diff is large

| Group | Added | Deleted | Files |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Canonical runtime | 8,954 | 530 | 53 |
| Required packaged copies | 8,952 | 528 | 51 |
| Tests and CI | 11,981 | 330 | 71 |

Several substantial pieces of the governor plan were bundled into one integration: admission/budget controls, birth measurement and calibration, weekly/pilot checks, a shared C14 safety gate, quarantine/recovery, worktree lifecycle, cleanup adapters and receipt accounting. Package synchronization duplicates the runtime for the installed uv tool. The independent Ponytail reviewer traced the large quarantine files to one generic backend imported by the worktree adapter, and found no further material avoidable abstraction in the high-risk paths reviewed. The 1,262-line removal-site checker is test tooling. This explains the size; the review does not establish that 8,954 canonical added lines are a minimum implementation.

## Scope and evidence

Canonical skills: code-standards, ponytail, zero-framework-cognition, zfc-leveling-roadmap and root-cause-first. No repository-local additions were found. Ponytail was loaded first. Two independent reviewer lanes ran concurrently; parent emulated root-cause and leveling as permitted by the workflow (a third fresh reviewer spawn was rejected by the thread limit). Head and clean status were rechecked. No full test suite rerun was needed for this review; targeted deterministic checks and the existing source-bound receipts establish the cited behavior.

title: cleanup_worktrees.sh --clean removes via --force --force using start-of-run HEAD/lock/lsof state
description:
Found by /advice (codex gpt-5.6-terra + opus) reviewing a plan on 2026-10-07 at origin/main b0b5b9e; pre-existing on main, not introduced by that plan.
scripts/cleanup_worktrees.sh flush_block (~:649-665) classifies each worktree from one git worktree list --porcelain read taken when the repo is first processed (head_sha, locked, prunable), and the lsof live-cwd snapshot (:187-226) is taken once at start. Removal then runs git worktree remove --force --force (:664), which also removes locked worktrees and discards dirty/untracked files.
Failure scenarios: (1) a worktree locked after the porcelain read is removed; (2) HEAD advances with a new clean commit after the read and the stale merged head_sha still qualifies it; (3) a shell cd's in after the lsof snapshot; (4) files modified between the final git status and removal are destroyed by the double force.
Fix direction from reviewers: immediately before each removal, re-read that worktree's porcelain entry and preserve on mismatch/absence, take a fresh fail-closed lsof probe, and use a non-forcing remove (or an equivalent final guard). Tests: lock-after-read, cd-after-snapshot, modify-after-validation, each preserved under --clean.

title: Sweep dangling git objects + repack hot repos (agent force-push bloat)
description:
## Symptom
Git repos used by the agent fleet accumulate hundreds of thousands of **unreachable** objects from rebases/force-pushes. Measured 2026-10-17:
- `~/projects/worldarchitect.ai`: **340,389** unreachable objects, `.git` 3.6G, **64 packs** after `git repack -ad`
- `~/worldarchitect.ai`: **258,801** unreachable (255,619 created in the last 3 days), `.git` 5.1G

## Root cause
Force-push/rebase churn leaves dangling objects that plain `git gc` cannot reclaim because they are inside the default 2-week `gc.pruneExpire` grace. `git repack -ad` packs reachable objects but leaves the dangling loose objects behind; a separate `git prune --expire=now` is required. Concurrent agents also keep creating packs, so repack alone does not consolidate.

## Expected / acceptance
1. Add a canonical maintenance path (e.g. `diskm cleanup-git-repos` or fold into `cleanup-dev-caches`) that, for configured hot repos, runs `git repack -ad --quiet` then `git prune --expire=<bounded>` — **dangling-only**, never touching refs/worktrees, skipping promisor/partial clones.
2. Configurable repo list + minimum dangling threshold so it only runs when worthwhile.
3. Regression test proving: dangling objects are pruned; reachable objects and worktrees are untouched; promisor clones are skipped fail-closed.
4. Independent re-execution at the fix HEAD.

title: TEST: DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR covered in real sweeper_roots.txt
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #72 + PR #73 + T4b-IMPL merged (T4b enables real full-root scratch-budget coverage of DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR; registering it as covered before that would be a false coverage claim, which is exactly the anti-pattern PR #72's own config/sweeper_roots.txt header comments warn against — see the "Known uncovered today" section of that file, which explicitly excludes DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR "by design" until full-root coverage is real). ## Goal

This must fail today (real registry has no such entry) and pass only once T4-IMPL adds the entry to the real file. Owned file: tests/test_check_uncovered_roots.py only (append one test method; do not modify any existing method). Depends on: PR #72 merged. Line budget: ~30 changed lines.

## Reuse
Exact fixture/helper pattern already in tests/test_check_uncovered_roots.py (read the file in full before writing, since exact line numbers will have shifted by the time this bead runs — locate by class/method name): `write_json(path, data)` module-level helper; `run(args)` module-level helper; `REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))` module-level constant (already defined at the top of this file — this is the key to pointing at the REAL registry instead of the per-test `self.registry` fixture); `TestCheckUncoveredRoots.setUp` sets `self.tmp`, `self.home`, `self.snapshot`, `self.discover`, `self.registry` under a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="dm_uncovered_")`. `GIB_KB = 1024 * 1024` module constant.

## Steps
1. Run: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_check_uncovered_roots.py -q 2>&1 | tail -5` (read-only baseline; expect all existing tests passing before your edit — if any already fail, stop per Stop-when instead of adding onto a red baseline).
2. In tests/test_check_uncovered_roots.py, inside `class TestCheckUncoveredRoots(unittest.TestCase):`, add this new method (place it as the last method in the class, immediately before the class's closing — i.e. after its last existing `def test_...` method body ends and before any module-level `if __name__ == "__main__":` block). This method deliberately points `--registry` at the REAL repo file, not `self.registry`, so it proves the actual production config, not a synthetic one:
```python
    def test_darwin_tmp_covered_by_real_registry(self):
        real_registry = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "config", "sweeper_roots.txt")
        fake_darwin_tmp = os.path.join(self.tmp, "var_folders_T")
        os.makedirs(fake_darwin_tmp)

        write_json(self.snapshot, {

        proc = run([
            "--snapshot", self.snapshot,
            "--discover", self.discover,
            "--registry", real_registry,
            "--home", self.home,
            "--darwin-tmp", fake_darwin_tmp,
            "--json",
        ])
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
        result = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        uncovered_paths = [e["path"] for e in result["uncovered"]]

        self.assertNotIn(scratch_leaf, uncovered_paths,
                          "DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR-rooted path must be covered by the "
                          "real config/sweeper_roots.txt once T4-IMPL registers it")
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_disk_diagnostic_scratch.sh — proves disk_diagnostic.sh's WORK dir is
# allocated via agent_scratch_create (managed root), not a bare mktemp.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
TARGET="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/disk_diagnostic.sh"

FAKE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d -t disk_diagnostic_scratch_test.XXXXXX)"
export AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT="$FAKE_ROOT"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
record_pass() { echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$(( PASS + 1 )); }
record_fail() { echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 )); }

if grep -q 'mktemp -d -t disk_diagnostic' "$TARGET"; then
  record_fail "disk_diagnostic.sh still allocates WORK via a bare mktemp, not agent_scratch_create"
else
  record_pass "disk_diagnostic.sh no longer uses a bare mktemp for WORK"
fi

if grep -q 'agent_scratch_create "disk_diagnostic"' "$TARGET"; then
  record_pass "disk_diagnostic.sh calls agent_scratch_create with runtime=disk_diagnostic"
else
  record_fail "disk_diagnostic.sh does not call agent_scratch_create with runtime=disk_diagnostic"
fi

if grep -q 'agent_scratch_trap_cleanup' "$TARGET"; then
  record_pass "disk_diagnostic.sh calls agent_scratch_trap_cleanup instead of a bare EXIT trap"
else
  record_fail "disk_diagnostic.sh does not call agent_scratch_trap_cleanup"
fi

rm -rf "$FAKE_ROOT"

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All disk_diagnostic_scratch tests passed."
```

title: scratch budget can delete nested checkouts or old uncommitted repositories

title: disk_magician lsof/scratch-budget helpers leak $TMPDIR dirs (~305MB, no sweeper pattern)
description:
## Symptom
`disk_magician`'s own scripts leave temp dirs in `$TMPDIR` that nothing cleans:
- `disk-magician-lsof.XXXXXX.*` (22 dirs / 99 MB)
- `disk-magician-scratch-budget-lsof.XXXXXX.*` (33 dirs / 192 MB)
- `disk-magician-scratch-budget-candidates.XXXXXX.*`

Measured 2026-10-17: **117 dirs / ~305 MB**, and `cleanup_tmp.sh` does not match them — its patterns cover git-clones / agent-prompts / cli-validation / worktree-pointers only. Growth ≈300 MB/week if unaddressed; manual `rm` only papers over it.

## Root cause
The lsof/scratch-budget helpers create `mktemp -d`-style dirs and do not always remove them (early-exit / interrupted paths). No sweeper pattern covers the `disk-magician-*` prefix.

## Expected / acceptance
1. Make the helpers clean up their own temp dirs on every exit path (trap EXIT), or
2. Add a `cleanup_tmp.sh` pattern for `disk-magician-*lsof.*` / `disk-magician-*candidates.*` older than a short retention (e.g. 24h) with the same lsof/mtime gates.
3. Regression test: a created-and-abandoned `disk-magician-lsof.*` dir is removed by a cleanup pass; a live one is preserved.
4. Independent re-execution at the fix HEAD.

title: IMPL: residual_drilldown.sh uncovered-root alert
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #72 + PR #73 merged. Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Add an uncovered-root alert step to scripts/residual_drilldown.sh: call scripts/check_uncovered_roots.sh --json, parse its `uncovered` array with python3, and print a line containing the literal substring "UNCOVERED" naming the count and top path when non-empty. Owned files: scripts/residual_drilldown.sh, and `src/disk_magician/scripts/residual_drilldown.sh` (generated by `sync_package_tree.sh`, not hand-edited). Depends on: T3b-TEST closed. Line budget: ~15 changed lines.

## Reuse
Insertion anchor: the final line of scripts/residual_drilldown.sh, exactly:
`echo "residual_drilldown: wrote $(echo "$run_candidates" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') proposal(s) to $CANDIDATES_FILE (total on file: $(python3 -c "import json; print(len(json.load(open('$CANDIDATES_FILE'))['candidates']))"))."`
(confirmed as the file's last line by reading it directly). `SCRIPT_DIR` is already defined at scripts/residual_drilldown.sh line 14.

## Steps
1. Run: `tail -1 scripts/residual_drilldown.sh` and confirm it matches the exact line quoted in Reuse above before editing; if it differs, stop per Stop-when.
2. Edit scripts/residual_drilldown.sh: append this block after the final existing line (do not remove or modify the existing final line):
```

uncovered_json="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/check_uncovered_roots.sh" --json 2>/dev/null || echo '{"uncovered": []}')"
uncovered_count="$(echo "$uncovered_json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('uncovered', [])))" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
if [[ "$uncovered_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
  top_path="$(echo "$uncovered_json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['uncovered']; print(d[0]['path'] if d else '')" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  echo "residual_drilldown: UNCOVERED — $uncovered_count root(s) with no registered sweeper owner (top: $top_path). See config/sweeper_roots.txt."
fi
```

3. Run: `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh` (no args, no `--check`) to mirror this bead's edit (and any other already-drifted repo-root file) into `src/disk_magician/`. ## Do not
Do not make this step abort the script on failure (`check_uncovered_roots.sh` failing must not break residual_drilldown.sh's existing candidate-writing behavior — hence the `|| echo '{"uncovered": []}'` fallback). Do not change the 10 GiB `THRESHOLD_GB` gate already in this file — that gates a different metric (unexplained residual vs used) and must not be conflated with the uncovered-roots count.

## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #72 + PR #73 merged (PR #72 adds scripts/check_uncovered_roots.sh/.py and config/sweeper_roots.txt, which this bead's production step invokes). Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Add a new test file tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh proving residual_drilldown.sh calls scripts/check_uncovered_roots.sh --json and, when the JSON's top-level `uncovered` array is non-empty, prints a line containing "UNCOVERED" to stdout/its log. Owned file: tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh (new). Depends on: PR #72 merged. Line budget: ~55 new lines.

## Reuse
Confirmed JSON contract of scripts/check_uncovered_roots.py (read directly from its source, function `main`): with `--json`, it prints one JSON object to stdout with top-level keys `uncovered` (list of objects, each with a `path` key), `protected`, and `needs_decision`; process exit code is 0 whether or not `uncovered` is non-empty (alerting must be done by parsing the JSON content, not the exit code). residual_drilldown.sh's existing PATH-shim-friendly structure: `SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"` (scripts/residual_drilldown.sh line 14) — mirror the same copy-into-a-fake-dir shimming approach used in T3a-TEST.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -x scripts/check_uncovered_roots.sh && echo EXECUTABLE || echo MISSING` (expect `EXECUTABLE`, confirming PR #72 has merged before this bead runs).
2. Create tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh — proves residual_drilldown.sh
# surfaces an UNCOVERED-roots alert line when check_uncovered_roots.sh
# reports a non-empty "uncovered" list.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
TARGET="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/residual_drilldown.sh"

TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t drilldown_uncovered_test.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT

FAKE_BIN="$TMP_ROOT/bin"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_BIN" "$TMP_ROOT/state" "$TMP_ROOT/home"

cat > "$FAKE_BIN/check_uncovered_roots.sh" <<'MOCK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo '{"uncovered": [{"path": "/fake/uncovered/root", "size_gb": 12.3}], "protected": [], "needs_decision": []}'
exit 0
MOCK
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/check_uncovered_roots.sh"
cp "$TARGET" "$FAKE_BIN/residual_drilldown.sh"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_BIN/lib"
cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/../scripts/lib/resolve_snapshot_json.sh" "$FAKE_BIN/lib/resolve_snapshot_json.sh"
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/residual_drilldown.sh"

echo '{"disk_used_gb": 500, "snapshot_coverage_pct": 90, "granularity_buckets": []}' > "$TMP_ROOT/state/disk_snapshot.json"

set +e
OUTPUT="$(cd "$FAKE_BIN" && DISK_MAGICIAN_STATE_DIR="$TMP_ROOT/state" HOME="$TMP_ROOT/home" ./residual_drilldown.sh --dry-run 2>&1)"
RC=$?
set -e

PASS=0
FAIL=0
if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "UNCOVERED"; then
  echo "  PASS  emits an UNCOVERED alert line"
  PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
else
  echo "  FAIL  no UNCOVERED alert line found in:"
  echo "$OUTPUT"
  FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
fi

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert tests passed."
```

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh 2>&1 | tail -6`
Expected failure: "no UNCOVERED alert line found" — residual_drilldown.sh does not yet call check_uncovered_roots.sh at all.

## GREEN
Not applicable to this bead (TEST-only; GREEN is proven by T3b-IMPL).

## Do not
Do not edit scripts/residual_drilldown.sh in this bead. Do not assume residual_drilldown.sh accepts a `--dry-run` flag without checking — run `grep -n -- '--dry-run' scripts/residual_drilldown.sh` first (its usage text quoted in this bead's Environment discovery already shows `[--dry-run]` as a documented option, so this is expected to succeed).

## Stop when
If `scripts/residual_drilldown.sh --dry-run` errors for a reason unrelated to the missing uncovered-roots feature (e.g. a snapshot-file-not-found error not satisfied by the fixture JSON in Step 2), stop and report the exact error to the parent rather than expanding the fixture by guesswork.

## Report
Run: `br --no-auto-flush comments add <THIS-BEAD-ID> "$(bash tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh 2>&1 | tail -6)"`

## Criteria
| ID | Check command | External anchor | Verifier | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T3bT1 | `bash tests/test_drilldown_uncovered_roots_alert.sh > /tmp/t3btest_out.txt 2>&1; grep -q "^Results: [0-9]* passed, [1-9][0-9]* failed" /tmp/t3btest_out.txt && echo PASS T3bT1 \|\| echo FAIL T3bT1` | Real subprocess run at HEAD (RED state) | Independent re-execution by a reviewer other than the author, at the bead's final commit SHA | FAIL |

title: Make snapshot report and effective config publication consistent
description:
## Provenance

Independent review of [PR #251](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/251) at commit `b87fda7928fcfffa8df0f3a7a7d66fec5a63e2b9` identified a nonblocking P1 snapshot publication race. `scripts/snapshot_commit.sh` pins/copies the effective configuration and generates the reclaim report in a sequence that can expose a report/config pair from different publication moments to a concurrent reader. The exact reviewed change fixes resolver selection and ordering regression coverage but does not establish atomic multi-artifact publication.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce the mixed-version reader observation with a deterministic producer/reader fixture.
- Define one publication boundary for the effective config and generated report, or an equivalent versioned handoff that makes mismatched pairs unobservable to consumers.
- Preserve the existing lock, pin, fail-closed, and first-run behavior.
- Add a regression test that fails on the current implementation and passes after the fix.
- Re-run package synchronization and snapshot tests against the final commit.

## Scope

Follow-up only; do not weaken configuration validation or resolver precedence in [PR #251](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/251). Deployment and live launchd proof remain separate gates.

title: test_cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh can rm -r at / when STATE_DIR is unset
description: On Linux the destructive-path guard blocks tests/test_cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh with: "rm -r target '$STATE_DIR/cleanup_worktree_venvs.lock' resolves to system top-level path /cleanup_worktree_venvs.lock". The test removes "$STATE_DIR/<lock>" but under a sanitized/cleared environment STATE_DIR expands empty, so the rm target becomes a root-level path. Fix: default STATE_DIR with ${STATE_DIR:?} (fail closed) or point it at a mktemp -d subtree before any rm, and add a regression asserting the script cannot run with an unset STATE_DIR. This is the same failure class as incident jleechan-lwn.

title: test_worktree_hygiene_preserve_wip.sh needs ~327s locally, so it deterministically trips the 300s CI per-test cap
description: Observed 2026-10-20. The suite is not touched by recent PRs yet fails Test and lint on any run that schedules it: PR #208 (unrelated diff) failed with 'tests/test_worktree_hygiene_preserve_wip.sh (TIMEOUT, 301.5s)'; PR #217 failed twice at 301.4s and 301.6s. Measured locally on this host in an isolated main worktree: 'timeout 900 bash tests/test_worktree_hygiene_preserve_wip.sh' => rc=0 in 327s with 'Results: 172 passed, 0 failed'. So the suite passes but needs 327s of real work against a 300s cap; CI runners are slower, guaranteeing the timeout. Not a flake and not a product defect. The backgrounded 'sleep 300' fixture at line 229 is trap-killed (line 29) and is NOT the cause. Definition of done, pick one and prove it: (a) cut runtime below the cap by finding the hot spot (172 assertions each invoking run_hygiene => likely repeated lsof/du/git scans; batch or stub the slow primitive), or (b) raise the harness per-test cap for this suite with a comment naming the measured 327s. Either way the PR that touches it must show a fresh timed run under the cap on a loaded host. Blocks every PR's Test and lint whenever this suite is scheduled, so it should be fixed ahead of feature work.
close_reason: Fixed by cutting runtime, not raising the cap (user directive). title: DOC: findings_wiki verifier-lanes-worktree-not-clone
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main. Interpreter: none — this is a documentation-only bead (no test/impl pair required; per the repo findings_wiki convention, this is a knowledge doc, not production code). No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Create findings_wiki/2026-09-23-verifier-lanes-should-use-worktrees-not-clones.md documenting the ~/.claude/state +15.6 GiB finding (2026-09-15..09-22) and the recommended git-worktree-instead-of-full-clone fix for the owning orchestrator repo(s), per the repo's own findings_wiki TEMPLATE.md schema. Owned file: findings_wiki/2026-09-23-verifier-lanes-should-use-worktrees-not-clones.md (new). No PR dependency. Line budget: ~30 new lines (docs only).

## Reuse
Exact frontmatter schema from findings_wiki/TEMPLATE.md: `title`, `hostname`, `date`, `status` (active|mitigated|resolved), `paths` (list), `safety_rule`; body sections `## What`, `## Why it matters`, `## Guards / governance`, `## History`.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f findings_wiki/TEMPLATE.md && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `EXISTS`).
2. Create findings_wiki/2026-09-23-verifier-lanes-should-use-worktrees-not-clones.md with this exact content:
```
---
title: Verifier/review lanes should use git worktree, not full clone (~/.claude/state)
hostname: jeffreys-macbook-pro.local
date: 2026-09-23
status: active
paths:
  - ~/.claude/state
safety_rule: none — cross-repo fix, not enforceable from this repo
---

## What

Interactive orchestrator sessions' codex/agy verifier lanes create full
`git clone` copies (including `node_modules`) of the target repo under
`~/.claude/state`, one per verifier task, with no cleanup on exit. Measured
+15.6 GiB born 2026-09-15..09-22 (34.1 GiB total at measurement time), one of
the top producers behind the +103 GiB/7-day disk-fill root cause (bead
disk_magician-isw). An unattributed later actor manually removed ~18 GiB of
these, which is not a durable fix — the pattern keeps recurring because the
producer (orchestrator lane spawning) is unchanged.

## Why it matters

Each verifier lane pays a full clone + `node_modules` install (~5 GiB each)
for work that only needs read access to a specific ref plus the ability to
run tests — a `git worktree add <path> <ref>` against the existing checkout,
combined with a shared/symlinked dependency cache (this repo's own
`scripts/symlink-shared-venvs.sh` is the existing in-repo pattern for the
analogous Python-venv case), gets the same isolation at a fraction of the
disk cost and removes cleanly via `git worktree remove`.

## Guards / governance

None yet in the owning orchestrator repo(s) — disk_magician has no write
access to that code and cannot enforce this fix itself. PR #74 (bead
disk_magician-isw) adds a *reactive* sweeper (`cleanup_claude_state.sh`,
7-day floor) for the symptom; this finding is the *producer-side* fix,
tracked as a separate approval-gated bead against the orchestrator repo(s)
per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-disk-fill-prevention-and-scheduled-cleanup.md
Task 5 / spec section A2.

## History

- 2026-09-22 — +15.6 GiB growth measured, root-caused to ad hoc full clones
  by verifier lanes.
- 2026-09-23 — finding documented; producer-side fix scoped as a
  cross-repo approval-gated bead (not implemented in disk_magician).
```

## RED
Not applicable (documentation bead, no code/test to fail).

## GREEN
Run: `test -f findings_wiki/2026-09-23-verifier-lanes-should-use-worktrees-not-clones.md && grep -q '^title:' findings_wiki/2026-09-23-verifier-lanes-should-use-worktrees-not-clones.md && echo PASS`

Do not edit findings_wiki/TEMPLATE.md. Not applicable.

# Nonblocking local fixture failures found during Scratch validation — 2026-11-02

The final repair candidate c85983567220f8dbe0d2b71398319196aaf6e09e passes CI's full Python phase and inventory integration. A supplemental local Python3.13.7 run completed1,295 tests in936.410s with3 failures,15 errors,87 skips. These are not claimed as a passing local full suite.

Two config/snapshot tests produce workstation inventory keys instead of their isolated XDG fixture keys. Both failures reproduced freshly at unchanged main fb8a8e3c5a2c579dcde4ca9a7ea5b029d9103597: `test_default_snapshot_consumer_reads_config_cli_mutation` and `test_snapshot_overlay_preserves_state_inventory_for_cli_and_snapshot`,2 failures in4.110s. The main worktree retains six unrelated dirty cleanup files; the invoked dispatcher/config/snapshot/resolver/test files have no changes against its HEAD. The cause of inventory leakage remains unconfirmed. Logs: `scratch-main-config-baseline-20261102.log` and its metadata receipt.

Fourteen hygiene cases fail before their behavior assertions when committing isolated fixture repositories with `test@example.com`. A fresh main-side diagnostic captured the actual stderr: the installed commit identity guard rejects reserved placeholder emails. The guard itself names `HERMES_SKIP_EXAMPLE_COM_GUARD=1` for ephemeral sandboxes, but no persistent guard setting was changed and no guarded production commit was bypassed. A PATH-only retry also failed, so this is not attributed to PATH shadowing. Do not weaken or disable production identity protections to make fixtures pass.

A lease-recovery module import exceeded an existing4-second contender timeout under workstation load; the wall-time model test also failed its row-count assertion. These failures require focused reproducibility before a stronger cause is assigned. Their implementation is outside this repair's production diff.

Follow-up acceptance: reproduce the snapshot leakage in an isolated, measured fixture; ensure only declared fixture paths appear; establish a scoped fixture contract for dummy Git identities that preserves production guards; replace unproven timing assumptions with synchronization where demonstrated necessary. Verify both standard CI and the workstation invocation. Preserve user configuration, credentials and unrelated dirty edits. This is P1 test-harness debt, not a P0 finding in the Scratch repair.

title: C14 keeps ms-playwright/webkit-2311 as 'secret-like' — misfiring heuristic on a browser binary tree
description:
Measured 2026-10-22/23 on the Mac. ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/webkit-2311 (291 MB) is permanently
kept by C14 as `kept:secret-like`. It is a Playwright WebKit browser binary tree, not user data and not
a secret — the secret-file heuristic is firing on a browser build artifact.

Evidence: two independent lanes ran cleanup_dev_caches.sh --clean on different occasions and both
recorded exactly `kept:secret-like` for webkit-2311 while every other ms-playwright entry (ffmpeg-1011,
.links) was kept for the benign `recent-activity` reason. Reclaim ceiling: 291 MB, so this is a
correctness issue, not a space emergency.

Why it is worth recording: this is the same failure class as vp7h and kub3 -- a fail-closed heuristic
misfiring on a path it was never meant to protect, which permanently pins a cache entry with a reason
that reads like a legitimate safety refusal. The distinguishing detail here is that the refuse reason is
WRONG (secret-like) rather than merely conservative (recent-activity), so an operator auditing "what is
C14 keeping and why" will be misled.

Suggested direction: decide whether ms-playwright's browser trees should carry a dedicated
`--kind playwright-browser` (like xcode-derived-data and sparkle-update-staging already do for their
own generated trees) instead of being run through the generic secret scan. Do NOT simply exempt
`webkit-*` by name in the secret filter -- that would weaken a real secret check globally for every path
that happens to contain that string.

Related: disk_magician-vp7h (FETCH_HEAD false negative), disk_magician-kub3 (Linux cwd), disk_magician-xt2y (scratch lock).

title: check_version_monotonic.py: current PR's own intra-branch version oscillation (bump-then-lower before merge) is not scanned — by design, non-blocking
description:
Codex /advice review on PR #73 (a0e3ace4853504abac7000783fe6c1028c957a25) flagged that get_git_log_versions() only walks <base_ref> --first-parent history, not the current branch's own commits since diverging from base. So a PR that bumps pyproject.toml's version then lowers it again in a later commit, all before merge, is not caught mid-review — only the final committed state is compared against base's own historical max.

This is a deliberate design choice (see PR #73 Tenets: 'No version bump in this PR unless the gate requires it' + 'CI uses origin/main as the authoritative tip'): the gate protects main's own linear version history, not intra-PR hygiene. The final merged state is what matters for 'version never regresses vs git history' — main's own first-parent history after merge is unaffected by transient intra-PR fluctuation. Reviewer Opus independently confirmed merge commits and origin/main/tag regressions are still caught.

If this class of intra-PR self-correction is ever judged worth blocking (e.g. to discourage version-bump churn in PR review), extend get_git_log_versions() to also scan '<base_ref>..HEAD --first-parent -p -- pyproject.toml' and union those versions in. Not urgent; tracked as a documented scope decision, not a regression.

title: Linux loop volume reclaim never punches holes: add fstrim/discard to reclaim path
description: Evidence (jeff-ubuntu, 2026-11-02T15:1xZ): (1) /home/jleechan/Scratch is /dev/loop25 backed by sparse /home/jleechan/.local/share/disk-magician/volumes/scratch.ext4 (200G apparent; 121G allocated vs 118G used inside -> only ~3G recoverable per trim); (2) fstab entry '# diskm-scratch:499b5331...' mounts with loop,user,noauto,nosuid,nodev,noatime,exec -> NO discard, so freeing files inside the volume returns nothing to /; (3) only reclaimer observed is systemd fstrim.timer (weekly): log 'Nov 02 01:28:11 /home/jleechan/Scratch: 4.2 GiB trimmed' - next run 2026-11-09. So hole-punching works but runs weekly against a volume that fills in hours. Fix: run FITRIM on the volume after reclaim (or mount with discard) in the volume_reclaim path; add a test asserting allocated backing bytes shrink after reclaim. Repro: write N GB inside Scratch, delete it, observe / avail unchanged until manual/weekly fstrim.
notes:
Live re-confirmation 2026-11-03T06:29Z (pi cmux audit, jeff-ubuntu, boot cc7718f1): backing image /home/jleechan/.local/share/disk-magician/volumes/scratch.ext4 allocated 161.14G -> 161.14G over 45s (apparent 200G) while / sat at 97-98%, and `fstrim /home/jleechan/Scratch` returns "FITRIM ioctl failed: Operation not permitted" as non-root; mount shows "rw,nosuid,nodev,noatime,user=jleechan" with NO discard. So the only hole-punching path is the weekly systemd fstrim.timer, now measured against a volume that was seen filling 174MB->13GB in 10 min of runner churn earlier the same day. This is the mechanism behind the "freeing inside the image returns no host space" symptom: relocating or deleting inside Scratch cannot help / unless FITRIM runs.
Quantified cadence gap (pi session, 2026-11-02): image allocation 97G(06:50) -> 112G(12:21) -> 125G(13:07) -> 127G(13:2x) = ~+30G in ~6h (~5G/h), while the only trim is weekly and returned 4.2 GiB. Host / free fell 154G(11-01 21:55) -> 103G(11-02 06:50) -> 73G(12:21) -> 58.4G(13:2x) -> 63.8G(11-02 ~17:00). Fix surface confirmed: scripts/volume.py:2240 hardcodes the fstab option string 'loop,user,noauto,nosuid,nodev,noatime,exec 0 0' with no discard, and scripts/volume_reclaim.sh + scripts/volume.py contain no fstrim/discard call, so the 20-min diskm-scratch-reclaim path cannot hole-punch. Also confirmed NOT a capability myth: user-level 'fstrim -v ~/Scratch' returns 'FITRIM ioctl failed: Operation not permitted' while root fstrim.service trims it fine - so the durable fix is discard-on-mount or a frequent root fstrim in/near the reclaim path, not a one-shot sudo.
2026-11-05 re-investigation: rootless FITRIM ALREADY EXISTS as 'diskm volume trim-auto scratch --clean' (linux_docker_trim_argv, volume.py:1447) via a pinned Docker container - no sudo needed; verified running rootless on Jeff-Ubuntu. It currently SKIPS on a healthy host because linux_trim_auto_cmd gates on gap>=4GiB AND host_free<80GiB. Measured image_gap_bytes=19.5GB with 127GiB free -> skipped. Residual defect is the 80GiB gate plus the absent 'discard' fstab option at volume.py:2338, NOT a missing capability. Fix options: (a) trim whenever image_gap>=4GiB regardless of host free, or (b) add discard to the loop mount options so the kernel trims on free.

title: governor T2 policy: follow-ups from PR #155 advice (claude -p spoof, revoke sub-second, py<3.11 Z, uv repo)
description:
Follow-ups from /advice on PR #155 (https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/155) at f837a734eda7b7e203376840b83d541492616aed (Opus primary + Secondo, both APPROVE). None of these block merge, because the gate stays closed until C14 lands.

1. Spawned-transcript spoof: any agent with a shell can run `claude -p 'APPROVE <id>'`, which writes a genuine `type=user` record under ~/.claude/projects. The `~/.claude*/projects` glob also accepts any `~/.claude-<anything>/projects` directory an agent creates. Option: require the record's `entrypoint` to be the interactive CLI and/or restrict the roots to a configured allowlist. Accept criteria: `claude -p` transcripts and agent-created roots are refused, with tests.
2. The revoke time uses whole seconds (`int(time.time())`), so a matching line typed less than 1 s before the revoke can re-approve. Store `revoked_at` as a float, or compare with `>=` plus 1.
3. Python older than 3.11: `datetime.fromisoformat` rejects a trailing `Z`, and real transcripts use `Z`. The package declares `requires-python >=3.8`. This fails closed, but either normalise `Z` to `+00:00` or raise the floor, and add a `Z` fixture to tests/test_policy.sh.
4. In the uv-tool install, D1 activation needs `DISK_MAGICIAN_POLICY_REPO` pointing at a git clone, because the package directory is not a checkout. Wire it into the launchd/receipt path when Task 13 lands.
5. The stored `line_sha256` is never re-verified by `decision_approved`, so a direct JSON write skips provenance. This is the accepted local-writer risk. An optional re-check could happen at activation time.

title: C14 worktree quarantine returns kept:admin-changed on Linux (19 remove-hook cases)
description: On Linux, scripts/worktree_quarantine.py returns kept:admin-changed during worktree removal, so every clean+pushed worktree is kept. Measured on jeff-ubuntu with PR #208's branch: tests/test_worktree_remove_hook.sh = 127 pass / 20 fail (19 root-cause cases + 1 collateral), while origin/main passes 139/0 and macOS passes 144/0. The same defect is present at the PR's own head 706a44dd (128/19), i.e. it predates the centralized lsof parser work. admin_changed has three sources: worktree_quarantine.py:208/217 (receipt vs live admin dir), :522/531 (restore), and check_admin():152. Instrumenting 217 and 531 produced no diff output during the suite, so the exact compare has NOT been pinned yet — next step is to instrument check_admin() and every canonical() comparison with a unified diff to a file (stderr is swallowed by the hook), then decide whether the divergence is a real content difference or a dev/ino/size artifact (canonical() compares dev/ino/type/size/sha256, no mtimes). Fixes: (a) merged origin/main into the branch to bring #209's renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) fallback, (b) the exception path now names the real failure (reason=quarantine-error:<Type>), (c) case 36d's fixture now includes one resolved cwd so the scan is complete. title: safety_min_stale_days() defined but never called by any worktree script
description: Opus finding during /advice review of PR #55 (14->7 day worktree floor change): scripts/safety_lib.sh defines safety_min_stale_days() to read a configurable staleness floor from safety.local.json, but no worktree script (cleanup_worktrees.sh, cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh, worktree_hygiene.sh) actually calls it -- each hardcodes its own MIN_AGE_DAYS default via ${WORKTREE_MIN_AGE_DAYS:-7} instead. Wire the worktree scripts to consult safety_min_stale_days() as a floor (max(requested, safety_min_stale_days())) rather than using it as a free-floating unused function.

title: scratch-prune trusts an unverified --lock-held bypass
description: Provenance: PR #302 head 59385e9fa3ec8f84d813b4f2e0215a3f3773388f, scripts/cleanup_scratch_top_level.sh lines 89-95 and 141-149. The non-dry-run cleaner skips scratch_lock_acquire whenever the caller supplies --lock-held, but the flag is not backed by evidence that the current process owns or inherited the shared cleanup lock. A caller can therefore bypass serialization with SCRATCH_TOP_LEVEL_APPROVED=1 while volume-reclaim or temp-sweep cleanup runs concurrently. Search at the pinned head found no cleanup_scratch_top_level caller passing --lock-held. Remove the bypass or validate lock ownership at the call boundary; add a focused test that direct unowned --lock-held is refused while the legitimate wrapper flow remains serialized.

title: cleanup_*.sh: stat-to-rm-rf TOCTOU is architecturally irreducible (same-uid only, no privesc) - evaluate fd-relative deletion repo-wide
description:
Codex (/advice round 3, PR #70, head 8e8d472) held on a residual finding
after two rounds of hardening cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh: even after
freezing candidate + parent identity and revalidating at multiple
checkpoints (enumeration, initial filter, lsof-recheck, post-safety_gate),
a same-uid actor can still replace the parent directory between the final
stat-based identity check and the rm -rf $path syscall that resolves the
pathname. This is not fixable with more stat-based rechecks — closing it
requires fd-relative deletion (openat/unlinkat via a helper, or Python's
os.* with dir_fd) instead of path-string-based rm -rf.

This TOCTOU is NOT unique to cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh — it is the same
architectural property shared by every "rm -rf $path" call after a
frozen-identity check across cleanup_dev_caches.sh, cleanup_sessions.sh,
cleanup_tmp.sh, cleanup_worktrees.sh, cleanup_xcode.sh, cleanup_pr_scratch.sh,
cleanup_supervisor_logs.sh, cleanup_agent_artifacts.sh,
cleanup_worktree_venvs.sh, and cleanup_ollama.sh (grep safety_gate + rm -rf
pattern across scripts/).

Triaged as non-blocking for PR #70 specifically: the attacker must already
be the same uid as the process (no privilege escalation — they already have
full read/write/delete access to their own files), and opus (independent
full-coverage /advice reviewer, high confidence, 3/3 rounds) explicitly
assessed this residual as "not worth another round" given the same
same-uid-only constraint. Fixing it only in cleanup_code_sign_clones.sh
while leaving the identical pattern in 10 other scripts would be
inconsistent; fixing it everywhere is a real architecture change
disproportionate to any single bug-fix PR.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Decide whether fd-relative deletion is worth the complexity given the
   same-uid-only threat model (may be closed as won't-fix with that
   reasoning recorded).
2. If pursued: design a shared helper usable by all scripts in the list
   above, not just code_sign_clone.
3. If pursued: add a test proving the specific race class it closes.

title: Document the structural disk-reclaim root cause and its four code-level gates
description:
Learning capture for 2026-11-03 disk forensics (PR jleechanorg/roadmap#230). Four verified, distinct gates make reclaim a host-level no-op on Linux and cap it on macOS:

1. FITRIM unreachable: tmp_scratch_sweep.sh:133 always appends --available-floor; volume_reclaim.sh:250 requires available_floor != true for the only trim-auto call. Direct invocation also self-refuses: no-host-reclaim-pressure with 9GB free. Mount lacks discard; non-root fstrim = EPERM; image 176GiB/200GiB.
2. Wrong age gate: the binder is 24h (5,031 kept:recent-activity), not 7d. Census of 834 dirs: 521 <1d, 303 1-3d, 10 3-7d, 0 >7d. Disk is full of hours-old work.
3. Candidate-shape blindness: volume_reclaim.sh:170 accepts only <repo>/(evidence|build)/<name>, so worldai_frontend (28G) and pr11094-final-advice (13G) top-level dirs are never candidates. Only scratch-prune owns them, 25GiB cap, behind the 24h floor.
4. Lock coercion: cleanup_tmp.sh:274 and cleanup_pr_scratch.sh:227 coerce rc 75 to 1, so a benign skip becomes OUTCOME=error; two timers (3600s/1200s) contend on one lock by construction; 209+68 measured skips.

Plus ungated creation: /Volumes/diskm-scratch is absent from hooks/disk-admission.sh:17-20 roots, scratch_dir.sh:87 is a bare mkdir, enforcement is observe and disk_budget.py:20 returns 0. 0 of ~82 runs reached any removal.

Behavioural: agents diagnose the trap correctly then store it as a prohibition, so each run re-executes an ineffective prune.

Documentation/learning only - no code change in this bead.

title: Sparkle update staging leaks ~2.4 GiB per app update; C14 blocks reclaiming it
description:
Measured 2026-10-21 on the Mac. Three fixed target candidates were examined for the "easy cleanup" question; two are reclaimable but blocked or worthless today, and the third is real money.

1) Sparkle auto-update staging, ~2.4 GiB PER APP UPDATE, retained forever. MEASURED 4.7 GiB.
~/.Library/Caches/com.openai.codex/org.sparkle-project.Sparkle/Installation/<rand>/<rand>/ChatGPT.app
Two leftover bundles from 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (2368 MB + 2438 MB). The updater unpacks the
downloaded update there, applies it, and never removes the staging copy. Nothing in the repo owns this
path. Attempting the sanctioned route (adding it to cleanup_dev_caches.sh section 3b as
--kind rebuildable) FAILED CLOSED: C14 returned `kept:unproven-content` because an extracted .app
bundle is not a recognisable cache format. So reclaiming it needs a C14 classification decision, not a
one-line target addition. Proposed options: (a) teach C14 a `sparkle-update-staging` kind that accepts
an .app staging dir only when the parent path matches .../org.sparkle-project.Sparkle/Installation and
an installed copy of the same .app exists outside it, or (b) leave it and document that users must
clear it by hand. Do NOT add it as a plain rebuildable target: it silently no-ops (measured).

2) Xcode iOS DeviceSupport (physical-device symbol caches): MEASURED 5.6 GiB for ONE device
(iPhone15,4 26.6.2 23G90). It IS regenerable (re-copied on the next debug session) but re-syncing is
slow, so a blanket delete is user-hostile. A 30-day age gate implemented as
clear_contents_aged() in cleanup_xcode.sh correctly declined to reclaim it today ("nothing older than
30d, keeping 5.6G") because the device was used this week. That gate is the right design and worth

title: block-always cwd policy makes every diskm cleanup lane a no-op on Linux (measured)
description: Measured 2026-10-20 on jeff-ubuntu with diskm 0.2.249, confirming the risk codex raised when it rejected #208 and the dot overrode with DECIDE block-always. Unprivileged lsof -d cwd on that host emits 517 'readlink: Permission denied' records (pids 1,2,3... system/foreign-uid). scripts/lib/lsof_linux.sh:lsof_denied_ignorable now blocks ALWAYS with no waiver, so every cwd-gated lane fails closed: cleanup-dev-caches reported kept:cwd-unknown in 15 of 15 sections and freed 0; cleanup-worktrees found 0 eligible of 716 preserved from a 144 GiB pool; cleanup-worktree-deps aborts with 'lsof output incomplete (unresolvable-cwd): cwd unknown, refusing'; worktree age/size render as 'age=- size=-' so recency is unmeasurable. Net effect on a normal multi-user Linux box: diskm can reclaim only the lanes that never consult the cwd gate (uv/pip/npm caches, docker build cache). Everything else is frozen regardless of how much space it holds. Options, operator decision: (a) privileged scanner (sudo lsof) with an explicit allowlist, (b) restore a scoped waiver like DISK_MAGICIAN_UNSCANNABLE_CWD_APPROVED=1 for the documented non-dumpable set, or (c) accept that Linux diskm is cache-only and document it. Whichever is chosen, the decision and its measured consequence must be recorded here so the next session does not rediscover it. Related: disk_magician-ty62 (--large disabled on Linux) and jleechan-uh1h (same-day scratch has no reclaim tier).

title: fix: path_size_kb() breaks on multi-line du output during real $TMPDIR scan
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main. Bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Found by
PR #71 (feat/scratch-size-budget) evidence run: real timed `bash scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh --dry-run --budget-gb 15` against the actual live $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR on a busy multi-agent dev box produced this non-fatal stderr during the DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR scan pass:

```
scripts/lib/scratch_budget.sh: line 143: 0
0: arithmetic syntax error in expression (error token is "0")
```

Script still exited 0 and completed (DRY RUN, no deletions attempted regardless). The failing line is `total_kb=$(( total_kb + kb ))` in `scratch_budget_evict_root()` (scripts/lib/scratch_budget.sh:143), fed by `kb=$(path_size_kb "$item")`.

## Root cause
`path_size_kb()` (scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh:217-219, pre-existing since 2026-06-09 commit 3bcaa23, NOT modified by PR #71):
```bash
path_size_kb() {
  du -sk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1+0}' || echo 0
}
```
assumes `du -sk` always emits exactly one line to stdout. On a live, churning $TMPDIR this assumption breaks under TOCTOU races and BSD-du edge cases (confirmed empirically: `du -sk` on a path that vanishes mid-scan or is TCC-protected — e.g. `TemporaryItems` — emits ZERO lines to stdout, not one). Two-line output (each line evaluating to `0` via `$1+0`) produces `kb="0\n0"`, which breaks the downstream bash arithmetic at scratch_budget.sh:143.

This is pre-existing code, but PR #71's `scratch_budget_evict_root()` is the first caller to run `path_size_kb()` across *every* top-level entry of the full $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR root (existing callers apply it to a narrower, more curated candidate set), so it's the first code path to reliably surface this.

## Impact
Non-fatal, fails toward UNDER-counting (`total_kb` undercounted for the one racy item → budget eviction may under-trigger, never over-trigger). No data-loss risk. Does not block PR #71: the bug is in unmodified shared code, and PR #71's dry-run/`--budget-gb` path degrades safely through it (RC=0, correct dry-run summary still printed).

## Goal
Harden `path_size_kb()` in scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh (and its src/disk_magician/ mirror via sync_package_tree.sh) to tolerate non-single-line `du` output:
```bash
path_size_kb() {
  du -sk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1{print $1+0; found=1} END{if(!found) print 0}'
}
```
(or equivalent `tail -1`/`head -1` guard). Add a regression test that stubs `du` to emit 2+ lines for one candidate and asserts `scratch_budget_evict_root`'s total_kb arithmetic does not error.

## Acceptance criteria
- `path_size_kb()` never causes an arithmetic error in any caller regardless of `du`'s line count.
- New/extended test in tests/test_scratch_budget.sh or tests/test_cleanup_safety.sh reproduces multi-line du output via a stub and proves no arithmetic error.
- `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh --check` clean after the src/ mirror update.

title: Preserve NUL diagnostic classification for large lsof stderr
description:
Provenance: [PR #256](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/256), exact reviewed head f7a0703fc3caf9a965ca18f2d0e11a9d13b19b98, reproduced on jeff-ubuntu 2026-10-24. Source: scripts/lib/lsof_linux.sh lines 51-62. This is a narrow diagnostic-status bug; it does not block merge because both affected callers fail closed.

Observed behavior:
- A fixture beginning with NUL followed by A bytes was tested at 1 MiB, 8 MiB, and 64 MiB.
- The raw `LC_ALL=C tr -d '\\000' <file | cmp -s - file` pipeline returned producer status 141 (SIGPIPE) and cmp status 1 (first differing byte).
- `lsof_stderr_byte_status file` returned status 2, although the input is readable and contains a NUL; the documented NUL verdict is status 1.
- Clean input still returns 0 and missing/unreadable input still returns 2.

Affected callers inspected at this exact head:
- scripts/lib/lsof_linux.sh:299 (`lsof_snapshot_cwds`) maps status 1 to `stderr-nul` and status 2 to `stderr-read-failed`.
- scripts/worktree_remove_hook.sh:61 (`wrh_live_cwd_reason`) maps status 1 or 2 to `cwd-unknown`.
- Existing focused tests are tests/test_lsof_linux.sh and tests/test_cwd_scanner.sh.

Impact: safety is preserved because the ambiguous result fails closed, but valid NUL diagnostics can be misclassified as a read/validation failure and lose the intended stderr-nul reason. This weakens observability and the status contract for the Linux lsof scanner.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A readable payload containing NUL returns status 1 deterministically even when the comparison pipeline would otherwise deliver SIGPIPE to `tr`; preserve status 0 for clean input and status 2 for unreadable/validation failures.
2. Add focused coverage for a large or early-difference payload that exercises the SIGPIPE case, without weakening fail-closed behavior.
3. Preserve and verify caller mappings (`stderr-nul`, `stderr-read-failed`, and `cwd-unknown`) at the current implementation head.
4. Attach before/after evidence from the exact PR head and record the final tested SHA.

Durable reproduction and source receipts: /home/jleechan/.local/state/disk-magician/pr-evidence/unpark-20261023.oHBkNH/p1-lsof-triage-20261024/.

title: scratch cleanup flock: a long cleanup_tmp --clean holds scratch_cleanup.lock past its own 600s budget, so cleanup_pr_scratch --clean skip-loops instead of sweeping
description:
Measured 2026-10-24 on the Mac (Hermes).

Evidence: lsof ~/.disk_magician_locks/scratch_cleanup.lock shows bash cleanup_tmp.sh --clean processes holding fd 4u, inside a lineage started 14:33:11 under timeout 600 (uv-tool install: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/disk-magician/lib/python3.13/site-packages/disk_magician/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh). At ~14:50 that lineage was still resident with 09:52 elapsed. python3 scripts/scratch_lock.py run --caller probe --script x --args -- /usr/bin/true answered "skipped, scratch lock held after waiting 20s".

Impact: cleanup_pr_scratch --clean acquires the same shared flock; any pass that fires while cleanup_tmp holds it is skipped (EX_TEMPFAIL), so the 12h pr-scratch sweeper can miss its slot entirely. The bead disk_magician-273z note about a paused cleanup_tmp PID 67912 holding the lock is stale (that PID no longer exists); the live contention is from normal, still-running sweeps.

Unknown: whether the 14:33 run finished inside 600s or was killed; and whether repeated near-simultaneous launchd firings stack. Open question for the fix: lock wait budget vs cleanup_tmp runtime, and whether the two sweepers should share a lock at all or use a per-root lock.

title: prune_aside_sessions.py: dedup_static_assets can hardlink messages.jsonl across a live in-use session
description: Found by Opus in /advice review of PR #59 (2026-09-01). dedup_static_assets() operates on retained_dirs, which explicitly includes sessions retained BECAUSE lsof reported them in-use (prune_aside_sessions.py, get_open_session_paths retained set). It hardlinks any regular file >=1KB with no static-asset filter, including messages.jsonl -- the most common >=1KB file in the real ~/.aside/u/*/sessions/ tree and one a live session actively appends to. Two byte-identical logs can get merged onto one inode, cross-contaminating a live session's log with another session's. Separately: the batch lsof parser (get_open_session_paths) uses line.split(None, 8) which silently drops any lsof output row with fewer than 9 whitespace-separated fields, letting an open session slip through undetected despite the function's fail-closed docstring. Fix: exclude retained_dirs (or specifically messages.jsonl / any actively-appended log) from dedup candidates, and harden the lsof line parser to fail closed on any row it cannot fully parse rather than silently skipping it.

title: REJECT before landing: uncommitted safety-floor reductions in worktree feat/scratch-trim-70-50 (lease TTL 3600s->5s, scratch-prune floor 48h->1h)
description:
Found 2026-10-31 during /nextsteps inspection of /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_disk_trim (branch feat/scratch-trim-70-50, HEAD 846677d). Uncommitted working-tree changes lower two safety floors that main just merged:

1. scripts/lib/worktree_lease.sh: LEASE_REUSE_LOCK_TTL_SEC default 3600 -> 5. This is the crash-recovery gate that prevents reclaiming a registry lock while its holder may still be alive. At 5 s, a lock written moments ago becomes eligible for recovery as soon as the recorded pid looks dead (and a pid can be reused), so a live writer's lock can be stolen. disk_magician#286 (merged d4809ce6) documents the 3600 s contract; this contradicts it.

2. scripts/cleanup_scratch_top_level.sh: MIN_HOURS_FLOOR becomes env-overridable (DISK_MAGICIAN_SCRATCH_PRUNE_MIN_HOURS_FLOOR) with a clamp of >=1 instead of the merged 48 h floor. The merged contract is '48 h floor; a larger value is honoured, a smaller one is clamped up'. An env knob that can lower it to 1 h re-opens exactly the young-artifact deletion the floor exists to prevent.

Also present: a '[[ -d "$entry" ]]' guard on the c14_repos_ok call (reasonable) and test/README edits.

These are NOT mine and were left untouched (another lane has an agy process in that worktree). If any of this is meant for tests only, it must be expressed as a test fixture override (env set inside the test), never as a production default or an override that lowers a floor in production. Acceptance: the branch either drops both floor changes or re-lands them behind a test-only mechanism plus a comment naming the invariant; CI proves the 3600 s TTL and 48 h floor still hold by default.

title: Linux Scratch reclaim fails closed every 20min on scratch-lock contention, so host pressure is never relieved
description:
The 20-minute diskm-scratch-reclaim.timer on jeff-ubuntu produces outcome=error and exits 1 on EVERY run when another process holds the Scratch lock, and it never retries with a shorter wait, so a locked run silently translates into 'no reclaim this cycle'. Observed live 2026-11-03 on jeff-ubuntu (installed 0.2.340, revision 9fad83c0, boot cc7718f1):

  Nov 02 22:00:00 Starting diskm-scratch-reclaim.service
  Nov 02 22:00:21 [scratch_prune] skipped, scratch lock held after waiting 20s
  Nov 02 22:00:41 [volume_reclaim] skipped, scratch lock held after waiting 20s
  Nov 02 22:00:41 [tmp_scratch_sweep] ERROR: volume reclaim failed
  Nov 02 22:00:41 Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
  (identical repeat at 22:20:00-22:20:42, and at 06:00Z / 06:20Z)

Receipt from the 06:20Z run: outcome=error, reason='one or more sweep steps failed', lock={held:true,acquired:true}, candidates.scratch_prune_outcome='skipped_lock', removed_count=0, freed_bytes=0, postcondition.df_delta_bytes=-166465536 (the host LOST 166MB while the sweep 'failed').

Why it matters: /home/jleechan/Scratch is a 200G loop ext4 at 75-99% full inside a host / at 97-98%, and the loop image returns nothing to / until FITRIM runs (see disk_magician-hbi4). So this unit is the ONLY 20-minute path that can relieve host pressure, and it aborts whenever a peer holds the lock - including peers that are themselves long reclaims or runner workspaces. A 20s wait against reclaims that legitimately run 15+ minutes is not a real wait.

Acceptance:
- [ ] When the lock is held, the unit must not report outcome=error for the whole sweep; either re-arm quickly (short retry cadence) or record a distinct skipped_lock outcome that does not mask other step failures
- [ ] Test: with the lock held by a peer for longer than the wait window, the timer produces a subsequent run that acquires and reclaims, rather than a permanent fail-closed loop
- [ ] Preserve fail-closed safety: never bypass the lock, never weaken age/live-PID/lease/C14 gates
- [ ] Receipt must distinguish 'skipped because locked' from 'failed to reclaim' so dashboards stop showing a false error rate
notes:
Also cross-referenced: disk_magician-ms99 (service TimeoutStartSec vs wrapper 900s budget) and disk_magician-hbi4 (loop image never hole-punches). Both are adjacent but distinct: ms99 is about a run being cut short by systemd, hbi4 is about freed bytes never returning to the host, and this bead is about the run never starting at all because a peer holds the lock. A single fix must not conflate them.

Separate observation, deliberately NOT filed as an OOM bug: the OOM kills visible in this unit's journal (killed by the OOM killer, status=9/KILL, result=oom-kill at Nov 02 19:44/20:26 and Oct 31 01:02) all belong to the PREVIOUS boot (7eca54c2, ended 2026-11-02 21:43:02). On the current boot (cc7718f1, started 21:45:36) there are ZERO OOM kills - the failure mode changed after reboot from OOM-kill to lock-skip. Do not attribute current failures to memory pressure; the unit has MemoryMax=infinity and MemoryCurrent is unset.
Cross-references (requested by operator, verified 2026-11-03T06:4xZ):

1. disk_magician-ms99 (P1, OPEN) - 'Align Linux Scratch service timeout with scratch-only wrapper budget'. Its premise was TimeoutStartSec=350 vs the wrapper's 900s deadline. THAT PREMISE IS NOW STALE: measured live on jeff-ubuntu (installed 0.2.340), the rendered user unit ~/.config/systemd/user/diskm-scratch-reclaim.service line 12 reads TimeoutStartSec=950; the installed template site-packages/disk_magician/systemd/diskm-scratch-reclaim.service.in line 12 reads 950; and origin/main carries 950 in BOTH src/disk_magician/systemd/diskm-scratch-reclaim.service.in and systemd/diskm-scratch-reclaim.service.in. The inner wrapper deadline is still 900s (tmp_scratch_sweep.sh:27, time.monotonic()+900). So the outer/inner gap is now 50s in the safe direction (outer longer than inner) and ms99 should probably be closed or rewritten to assert the current 950>900 invariant rather than the old 350<900 defect. Not closed here - that is the other bead's owner decision.

2. disk_magician-46z7 (P1, IN_PROGRESS) - 'Mac hourly Scratch reclaim can no-op below volume threshold despite host pressure'. This is the MAC-side sibling of the present Linux defect: 46z7 is a threshold-gating no-op on Mac, mgg2 is a lock-contention fail-closed on Linux. Same operator-visible symptom (host/volume pressure not relieved by the scheduled reclaim) but a different mechanism and a different code path; do not merge the fixes.

3. disk_magician-hbi4 (P1, OPEN) - 'Linux loop volume reclaim never punches holes'. Directly compounds this bead: on jeff-ubuntu, Scratch is a 200G loop ext4 whose image returns nothing to / until FITRIM runs, so every cycle this unit spends failing on the lock is a cycle where the only 20-minute path to relieving host / is skipped entirely.

Distinctness statement: ms99 = run cut short by systemd (timeout), hbi4 = freed bytes never return to host (no discard/FITRIM), mgg2 = run never starts (lock held), 46z7 = run starts and declines (threshold). Four different failure modes on the same operator symptom.

title: Reconcile stale active job receipts with lock proof
description:
## Finding
`diskm status` reports `action_outcome=unknown` when a stale active receipt remains in `active[]`, even after a later run for the same serialized job successfully acquires its exclusive lock and records a terminal success. This masks current completion and leaves the old interrupted attempt unexplained.

## Provenance
Captured live status: `/tmp/diskm-execute-20261010/status-after-clean-0.2.187.json` (2026-10-10T12:30:18Z). `snapshot_commit` retained active run `0a8b4a30-7835-42b7-a38e-17996836c67f` started 09:23:28Z while newer run `2ec740fb-1716-4ab3-8a03-9e3147d61b92` acquired the job lock and completed successfully 12:17:28–12:23:28Z. `pressure_sweep` retained active run `ee0b3570-5fa2-4806-9a37-ba8414beb7f1` from 2026-10-06 while newer lock-acquiring run `7a60481e-1c46-408d-99b1-b28a7bc48c20` succeeded 12:15:19–12:17:45Z.

Code owners: `scripts/job_receipt.py:368-420` appends active records; `:445-470` removes only the matching run ID on finish. `src/disk_magician/scripts/disk_status.py:912-937` treats any active record as current/interrupted unknown before considering a newer terminal outcome. `tests/test_disk_status.py` covers an active receipt without a later terminal but lacks stale-active-plus-newer-terminal and genuinely-active-after-terminal cases.

## Desired behavior
Preserve the older run as interrupted history rather than deleting it or claiming it succeeded. Let a newer terminal outcome represent current state only when a canonical lock/ordering proof establishes that the prior attempt is no longer active. Do not apply generic reconciliation to unlocked jobs such as tmp scratch; a genuinely active attempt newer than a terminal must still report unknown.


## Corrected proof requirement (2026-10-10)

Do not implement status supersession based on the current lock-acquired receipt proof alone. Review of scripts/snapshot_commit.sh:37-42 found a TOCTOU race: two contenders can both observe an expired/dead lock; one creates a replacement lock and the other removes it, allowing overlapping runs. A newer terminal receipt therefore cannot prove an older active run stopped. Keep snapshot_commit active status unknown until a safe run-lifetime/lock ownership contract provides reliable exclusion proof. Follow-up: disk_magician-0bgs. The analogous pressure_sweep 3600-second TTL lock issue is tracked separately in disk_magician-151c. These lock fixes and status repair are outside PR #142 scope.

Require tests for genuinely active concurrent attempts and interrupted historical attempts, preserve historical evidence, then validate installed receipts. Queue and dependencies are documented at /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/roadmap/nextsteps-2026-10-09-worktree-reclaim-and-fill-prevention.md. title: Return failure after cleanup category errors
description:
## Finding
A real `disk_magician.sh clean` run emitted 15 cleanup categories; Codex SQLite vacuum failed with exit 1 because six DB files had active client PIDs, but the top-level cleanup command still returned success. The category runner intentionally continues after a child failure, but final command status does not expose the failed category.

## Provenance
- Run output: `/tmp/diskm-execute-20261010/clean-routine-0.2.187.log` (Codex SQLite vacuum reported active client PIDs and exit 1; the overall command returned 0).
- `scripts/disk_audit.sh:291-303` records category failures but `run_category` returns 0 to continue.
- `tests/test_cleanup_safety.sh:1057-1062` and `tests/test_unify_routine_cleanups.sh:256-263` currently assert rc=0 on a category failure.
- `scripts/disk_audit.sh:511+` runs the safe-clean categories and should preserve continuation while returning nonzero after the summary if any category failed.

## Desired behavior
Continue later categories and print the full failure summary, then return nonzero when one or more categories fail. Keep a clean run at exit 0 and test that later categories still execute after a failure.
