title: APPROVED 2026-09-24: IMPL agent_worktree.sh helper (redesigned from cross-repo to in-repo, see body)
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after the paired TEST bead
(disk_magician-9n1) closed AND T5-IMPL (disk_magician-agent-scratch-helper-impl-ned) closed.
Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required. **APPROVED 2026-09-24** by the user ("finish
all"). Redesigned scope (round-4 correction, 2026-09-24): the original bead framed this as "find the
owning orchestrator repo, needs cross-repo approval." That framing was wrong — the `~/.claude/state`
full-clone growth (bead isw, +15.6 GiB/week) is produced by ad hoc interactive Claude Code/Codex
sessions spawning codex/agy verifier lanes, not by a discrete automation repo disk_magician lacks
write access to. There is no separate repo to find. The actionable, in-repo fix is a helper any such
session can call instead of `git clone`; disk_magician owns and can ship this directly, with no
cross-repo approval needed. The companion machine-wide policy instruction telling sessions to
actually call it is a SEPARATE, already-tracked bead
(disk_magician-codex-agents-md-scratch-policy-2gp, itself approval-gated on `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`'s
own semantic-signoff rule) — do not duplicate that policy edit here.

**Round-4b correction (2026-09-24, independent Codex + Opus review of the original 2026-09-24
draft, both flagged the same defect):** the original draft had this helper allocate the worktree
parent via `agent_scratch_create "worktrees" ...`, nesting it inside
`/private/tmp/agent-scratch/<runtime>/<run-id>/worktrees/...`. That is a real safety bug: that
subtree is subject to bead B4/`scratch_budget.sh`'s size-budget+age eviction (bead i2o, once
enabled) and is removed wholesale by the A3 Stop hook
(`disk_magician-agent-scratch-cleanup-hook-impl-o4z`'s script) when a session ends — neither path is
worktree-aware, so either could `rm -rf` a worktree with uncommitted, unpushed work well inside the
repo `CLAUDE.md` "Worktree 7-day rule (hard)"'s protected window. Fixed below: this helper does NOT
call `agent_scratch_create` and does NOT allocate under the agent-scratch root at all — see Goal.

**Round-4c correction (2026-09-24, second-round Opus re-review of the round-4b fix): the round-4b
default, `/private/tmp/agent-worktrees`, was still unsafe** — `/private/tmp` itself (not just the
agent-scratch subtree) is scanned one level deep by `cleanup_tmp.sh --large`, which runs in
production TODAY via `pressure_sweep.sh` with no dependency on bead i2o, and would archive-then-purge
a top-level `agent-worktrees` container after ~4h of no file changes anywhere under it (confirmed
live: `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT` in `scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh` resolves via
`scratch_roots_get_private_tmp()`, `scripts/lib/scratch_roots.sh:52-55`, to literal `/private/tmp`;
`agent-worktrees` matches neither the `wt_*|worktree_*` unsaved-work-guard name pattern nor
`DEFAULT_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS`). Fixed by moving the default one more level away, to
`/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` — confirmed live via `grep -rn '/private/var/tmp' scripts/*.sh
scripts/lib/*.sh` returning zero matches, i.e. no sweeper in this repo scans `/private/var/tmp` at
all. Do not move the default back under `/private/tmp` without also adding `agent-worktrees` to
`DEFAULT_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS` in `scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh` and a test proving both `cleanup_tmp.sh
--large` and `scratch_budget_evict_root` skip it (out of scope for this bead pair).

## Goal
Create `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh` implementing `agent_worktree_create <label> <ref> <repo>`:
allocates a managed leaf directory directly under `AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` (env-overridable; defaults
to `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` — a different top-level system directory from
`/private/tmp/agent-scratch`, not a sibling under the same parent; see the Round-4b/4c corrections
above for why it must not reuse `agent_scratch_create` or live anywhere under `/private/tmp`), named
`<label>-$$-$(date +%s)`, validating `label` with `scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh`'s existing
`_agent_scratch_valid_component` (sourced for that validation only, not for root selection), then
runs `git -C "$repo" worktree add "$path" "$ref"`, and echoes `$path` on success. Rejects empty
`label`, empty `ref`, or a `repo` that is not a git working tree (`git -C "$repo" rev-parse
--is-inside-work-tree` must succeed first), creating no directory or worktree in any rejection case.
**Round-6 addition (2026-09-25, independent Codex + Opus closure-round review, both flagged the
same gap):** also rejects when `$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` already exists as a symlink, or exists but is
not owned by the current user — `/private/var/tmp` is world-writable-sticky
(`drwxrwxrwt root:wheel`), so a plain `mkdir -p` on a predictable child path does not prove this
session owns what's there; another local actor could pre-create it as someone else's directory or as
a symlink into a swept location. See Reuse/Steps for the exact `[[ -L ]]`/`[[ -O ]]` checks. Owned
files: `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh` (new), `src/disk_magician/scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh`
(new, generated by `sync_package_tree.sh` — `scripts/lib/*.sh` is in its mirrored `PATTERNS` set —
run in Step 3, do not hand-create). Depends on: the paired TEST bead (disk_magician-9n1) closed,
T5-IMPL closed (sources `_agent_scratch_valid_component` only). Line budget: ~45 new lines.
**Cleanup of `/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees` is explicitly out of scope for this bead** — do not add
it to `config/sweeper_roots.txt`, `scratch_budget.sh`, or the Stop hook; a follow-up bead (not
created here) would extend `worktree_hygiene.sh`'s repo-discovery config to cover calling repos it
doesn't already scan (see the spec's round-6 correction — `worktree_hygiene.sh` itself already
discovers a worktree here via `git worktree list` for any repo it scans, e.g.
`~/projects/worldarchitect.ai`, so this is a narrower gap than "nothing ever finds it").

## Reuse
`scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh`'s `_agent_scratch_valid_component` function only — source that file
at the top of `agent_worktree.sh` and call `_agent_scratch_valid_component "$label"` for validation.
Do NOT call `agent_scratch_create` (see Round-4b correction above) — allocate
`$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT/<label>-$$-$(date +%s)` directly with `mkdir -p`.

## Steps
1. Run: `bash tests/test_agent_worktree.sh 2>&1 | tail -5` (expect the RED failure from the paired
   TEST bead — confirms the test file exists and fails for the expected reason before you start).
2. Create `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh` with this exact content:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck shell=bash
# agent_worktree.sh — managed `git worktree add` helper for agent
# sessions spawning verifier/review lanes (bead
# disk_magician-orchestrator-worktree-not-clone-2nw: replaces the
# `~/.claude/state` full `git clone` pattern with a worktree checkout
# under its own managed root. Deliberately NOT nested under
# /private/tmp/agent-scratch: that root is subject to scratch_budget.sh
# eviction and the Stop hook's rm -rf, neither of which is worktree-aware
# — nesting there risks deleting a worktree with unpushed work inside the
# repo's hard 7-day protection window (see this bead's Round-4b note).
AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT="${AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT:-/private/var/tmp/agent-worktrees}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/agent_scratch.sh"

agent_worktree_create() {
  local label="$1" ref="$2" repo="$3"
  _agent_scratch_valid_component "$label" || { echo "agent_worktree_create: invalid label" >&2; return 1; }
  [[ -n "$ref" ]] || { echo "agent_worktree_create: empty ref" >&2; return 1; }
  git -C "$repo" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1 || {
    echo "agent_worktree_create: not a git working tree: $repo" >&2
    return 1
  }
  local path="$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT/${label}-$$-$(date +%s)"
  mkdir -p "$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT" || return 1
  if [[ -L "$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT" ]]; then
    echo "agent_worktree_create: refusing symlinked root: $AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ ! -O "$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT" ]]; then
    echo "agent_worktree_create: refusing root not owned by current user: $AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  git -C "$repo" worktree add "$path" "$ref" > /dev/null 2>&1 || {
    echo "agent_worktree_create: git worktree add failed for $repo -> $path @ $ref" >&2
    return 1
  }
  echo "$path"
}
```
   Note: `git worktree add` creates `$path` itself (it must not already exist), so this function
   only pre-creates the parent `$AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT`, not the leaf — unlike `agent_scratch_create`,
   which is deliberately not called here (see Round-4b note above and this bead's Reuse section).
3. Run: `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh` (no args) to mirror this file into `src/disk_magician/`.

## RED
Already proven by the paired TEST bead (Step 1 above reproduces it) — expected stderr contains
`No such file or directory` for `scripts/lib/agent_worktree.sh` (from the `source` line failing) and
the script exits non-zero (`set -uo pipefail` — an unset `$?` check is not needed; the non-zero exit
itself is the RED signal, no output-matching required beyond confirming the run failed).

## GREEN
Run: `bash tests/test_agent_worktree.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` → exact output `Results: 10 passed, 0 failed`
(the paired TEST bead's Step 2 content defines exactly 10 `record_pass`/`record_fail` call sites:

non-repo rejection created no dir, pre-existing symlinked root rejected (round-6), not-owned root
rejected + not-owned-root rejection created no worktree (round-6b — dynamic test pointing
`AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT` at `/private/var/tmp` itself, skipped only when running as literal root)). If
`tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` on disk has a different number of assertions than 10 when this
bead runs, run `grep -c 'record_pass\|record_fail' tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` and use that count
instead — trust the file on disk over this bead's count if they disagree, and note the discrepancy in

## Do not
Do not modify `tests/test_agent_worktree.sh` to make it pass. Do not touch `scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh`.
Do not add a machine-wide policy edit to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` or any other shared config from this

## Stop when
Run `grep -n '^_agent_scratch_valid_component()' scripts/lib/agent_scratch.sh` before Step 2. This

title: TEST: pressure-sweep plist enables scratch-budget eviction
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #71 + PR #73 merged (PR #71 adds the `--budget-gb`/`DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB` opt-in eviction feature to scripts/pressure_sweep.sh, shipped disabled-by-default; this bead's production step turns it on). Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Add a new test file tests/test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh proving launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-pressure-sweep.plist.template's EnvironmentVariables dict sets DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB to exactly 15 (a nonzero value — PR #71 ships this feature disabled by default at 0, and the root-cause finding is that $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR agent scratch, 28.2 GiB observed 2026-09-22, is this repo's single largest disk-fill producer, so leaving budget eviction off by default leaves that producer unaddressed even after every other bead in this plan lands). Owned file: tests/test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh (new — deliberately a separate file from tests/test_pressure_sweep.sh so this bead and T1's beads can run as parallel, non-conflicting lanes). Depends on: PR #71 merged (tracked via beads d45 and ka4 — round-2 `/advice` fix: earlier drafts of this bead only depended on cse+8to, not on PR #71 itself, which would let it run before the feature it enables even exists). Line budget: ~20 new lines.

## Reuse
Pattern exemplar: tests/test_pressure_sweep.sh lines 270-278 (existing "Test 11" plist-content assertion style — `PLIST_CONTENT="$(cat "$PLIST_TEMPLATE")"` then a plain `grep -qF` check), adapted to a standalone file with its own PASS/FAIL counters rather than reusing the shared ones defined earlier in that file (do not source tests/test_pressure_sweep.sh from this new file).

## Steps
1. Run: `grep -c 'DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB' launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-pressure-sweep.plist.template` (expect `0` — the key is not present in the plist's EnvironmentVariables yet; it exists today only as a shell env-var default inside scripts/pressure_sweep.sh).
2. Create tests/test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh — proves the pressure-sweep
# plist template turns on size-budget scratch eviction (PR #71's
# DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB, shipped disabled-by-default at 0)
# with a nonzero value, since $TMPDIR/DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR scratch is this
# repo's largest observed disk-fill producer (28.2 GiB, 2026-09-22).
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
PLIST_TEMPLATE="$REPO_ROOT/launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-pressure-sweep.plist.template"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

if [[ ! -f "$PLIST_TEMPLATE" ]]; then
  echo "  FAIL  plist template not found at $PLIST_TEMPLATE"
  FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
else
  PLIST_CONTENT="$(cat "$PLIST_TEMPLATE")"
  if grep -qF '<key>DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB</key>' <<<"$PLIST_CONTENT" && \
     grep -A1 '<key>DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB</key>' <<<"$PLIST_CONTENT" | grep -qF '<string>15</string>'; then
    echo "  PASS  scratch budget eviction enabled at 15 GiB"
    PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
  else
    echo "  FAIL  DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB=15 not found in EnvironmentVariables"
    FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
  fi
fi

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled tests passed."
```

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh 2>&1 | tail -3`
Expected failure: `DISK_MAGICIAN_PRESSURE_SCRATCH_BUDGET_GB=15 not found in EnvironmentVariables` — the plist does not set this key yet.

## GREEN
Not applicable to this bead (TEST-only; GREEN is proven by T4b-IMPL).

## Do not
Do not edit the plist template in this bead. Do not pick a different numeric value than 15 without updating both this test and T4b-IMPL's edit to match — the value must be identical in both beads (it is not: pick 15 here, and T4b-IMPL must also use 15).

## Stop when
Not applicable — this bead has no external-content dependency beyond confirming the plist template exists (Step 1).

## Report
Run: `br --no-auto-flush comments add <THIS-BEAD-ID> "$(bash tests/test_pressure_sweep_scratch_budget_enabled.sh 2>&1 | tail -3)"`

title: Stale methodology reference: docs pointed at frozen backup/<host>/, not live snapshots/ path (cron is healthy)
description:
Originally reported 2026-08-20 as a launchd-cron failure: `~/.disk_magician_backup/backup/jeffreys-macbook-pro/disk_snapshot.json` was 30 days stale (last write 2026-07-21 05:19 PT, commit `3fbaa50`), and the disk-fill investigation methodology in `~/projects_other/disk_magician/CLAUDE.md` referenced that legacy host-profile path as if it were the live floor.

**Actual root cause (Lane B, 2026-08-20):** path migration, not cron failure. Verified:
- `launchctl list | grep com.jleechanorg.disk-magician` shows the job loaded (`- 0 com.jleechanorg.disk-magician`; `-`=exited-cleanly, `0`=no error, both expected for an idle StartInterval job).
- Plist at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician.plist` is 612 bytes, RunAtLoad+StartInterval=1800, ProgramArguments `/Users/jleechan/.local/bin/disk-magician snapshot` -- all correct.
- uv-tool `disk-magician v0.2.52` is installed and the symlink resolves; `/tmp/disk-magician.log` shows recent successful runs.
- `git -C ~/.disk_magician_backup log` shows snapshot commits every ~30 min, latest `2909199` at 2026-08-21T06:10:58Z (~20 min before this entry was opened).

**The migration:** commit `43d9cf8` 2026-07-21 05:16:30 PT ("feat(state): snapshot write-path + grandfathering, PR 2/3") introduced `scripts/snapshot_commit.sh`, which writes the snapshot to `~/.disk_magician_backup/snapshots/disk_snapshot.json` and the 5 GiB ledger to `~/.disk_magician_backup/ledger/topdown-5g.json` (see `src/disk_magician/scripts/snapshot_commit.sh` lines 65-66). The legacy `backup/<host>/disk_snapshot.json` was grandfathered as a read-fallback only (`resolve_dispatch_snapshot_json()` in `src/disk_magician/disk_magician.sh:60-70`). First commit to the new path: `3c082b6` at 2026-07-21 04:52:45 PT. Last commit to the legacy path: `3fbaa50` at 2026-07-21 05:19:26 PT -- minutes after the migration commit. The legacy dir has been byte-stable ever since.

2. `~/.disk_magician_backup/backup/jeffreys-macbook-pro/README.md` added and committed (`761893c`) so anyone browsing the legacy dir sees the freeze notice before reading the stale `disk_snapshot.json`.
3. Methodology sections in both `~/projects_other/disk_magician/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` already point at `ledger/topdown-5g.json` (the correct live path) -- no change required there; only the operational-gotcha bullet was stale.

**Verification:**
- `git -C ~/.disk_magician_backup log -1 --format='%ai %s' snapshots/disk_snapshot.json` returns today's commit.
- `git -C ~/.disk_magician_backup log -1 --format='%ai %s' ledger/topdown-5g.json` returns a 2026-08-20 commit.
- `launchctl list | grep disk-magician` shows the parent job and all child jobs loaded.
- Plist byte-size and ProgramArguments unchanged from the template.

title: Add FSEvents watcher on ~/projects/ to capture future worktree deletions in real time
description:
After the 2026-07-26 47-worktree deletion (y7t), all log sources are exhausted — the macOS unified log does not record path-level filesystem ops, and git does not emit OSLog entries. The only way to catch future incidents is prospective instrumentation.

title: Fail closed on non-object report config roots
description:
## Provenance

Read-only reproduction on [PR #251](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/251) exact head `ec07d2c8ffa928aef856b890535682009326e814` (production +436/-47; non-production +699/-1). With `DISK_MAGICIAN_CONFIG` pointing to a valid JSON file whose root is `[]`, `scripts/disk_report_html.py` `_load_key_path_map()` raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` because the helper catches JSON/I/O/type errors but does not require an object root. This is a nonblocking P1 robustness gap outside the monitored-config mutation acceptance path.

## Acceptance criteria

- A valid JSON document with a non-object root is handled fail-closed by the report helper without an uncaught exception.
- The report command preserves its existing empty-map behavior for malformed or unusable config and continues to render a report from persisted snapshot inputs.
- Add a focused regression fixture for array, scalar, and null roots, preserving current object-root precedence behavior.
- Run the focused report tests and `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh --check` at the fix head.

## Reproduction

```text
TD=$(mktemp -d /tmp/disk-magician-report-p1.XXXXXX)
printf '[]\n' > "$TD/config.json"
DISK_MAGICIAN_CONFIG="$TD/config.json" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'import scripts.disk_report_html as m; print(m._load_key_path_map())'
# observed: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'; exit 1
```

## Scope

Follow-up only. No production change is requested in [PR #251](https://github.com/jleechanorg/disk_magician/pull/251); deployment, live-disk behavior, and merge authorization remain separate gates.

title: TEST: sweeper_health_check.sh ledger-freshness WARN
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main at merge time (no PR dependency — scripts/check_ledger_freshness.sh already exists on main today). Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Add a new test file tests/test_sweeper_health_ledger_warn.sh proving sweeper_health_check.sh emits a WARN line containing "ledger" and "stale" (case-insensitive) and exits 1 when scripts/check_ledger_freshness.sh reports STALE, by stubbing check_ledger_freshness.sh's output via a PATH-shimmed executable. Owned file: tests/test_sweeper_health_ledger_warn.sh (new). No dependency on any open PR. Line budget: ~45 new lines.

## Reuse
scripts/check_ledger_freshness.sh's contract (confirmed by reading it): prints exactly one line, first whitespace-tab-separated token is `OK`, `STALE`, or `UNKNOWN`, followed by a tab and a reason; exit code 0 for OK/fresh, 1 for STALE, 2 for UNKNOWN/error (scripts/check_ledger_freshness.sh lines 9-11, 39-41). sweeper_health_check.sh's existing WARN emission pattern to mirror: `printf "  [WARN] %-44s log=%s  (last write %s ago, errors in tail)\n" ...` at scripts/sweeper_health_check.sh line 219 (mirror the two-column `[WARN] <label>` shape, not the exact fields). sweeper_health_check.sh's final exit logic (already existing, do not change): `if [[ $WARN_COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then ... exit 1; fi` at scripts/sweeper_health_check.sh lines 264-267.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -x scripts/check_ledger_freshness.sh && echo EXECUTABLE || echo MISSING` (expect `EXECUTABLE`; this confirms the real script this test will shim).
2. Create tests/test_sweeper_health_ledger_warn.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_sweeper_health_ledger_warn.sh — proves sweeper_health_check.sh WARNs
# and exits 1 when check_ledger_freshness.sh reports STALE.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
TARGET="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/sweeper_health_check.sh"

TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t sweeper_health_ledger_test.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT

FAKE_BIN="$TMP_ROOT/bin"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_BIN"
cat > "$FAKE_BIN/check_ledger_freshness.sh" <<'MOCK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo -e "STALE\tno_published_ledger_commit"
exit 1
MOCK
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/check_ledger_freshness.sh"
cp "$TARGET" "$FAKE_BIN/sweeper_health_check.sh"
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/sweeper_health_check.sh"

# sweeper_health_check.sh resolves its own SCRIPT_DIR internally, so the
# stub above only wins if it is invoked via the copy that resolves
# check_ledger_freshness.sh relative to $FAKE_BIN, which is the case here
# because both files are copied into the same directory.
set +e
OUTPUT="$(cd "$FAKE_BIN" && DISK_MAGICIAN_STATE_DIR="$TMP_ROOT/state" HOME="$TMP_ROOT/home" ./sweeper_health_check.sh 2>&1)"
RC=$?
set -e

PASS=0
FAIL=0
if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -qiE '\[WARN\].*ledger.*stale|\[WARN\].*stale.*ledger'; then
  echo "  PASS  emits a WARN line mentioning ledger + stale"
  PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
else
  echo "  FAIL  no WARN line mentioning ledger + stale found in:"
  echo "$OUTPUT"
  FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
fi
if [[ "$RC" == "1" ]]; then
  echo "  PASS  exits 1 when ledger is stale"
  PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
else
  echo "  FAIL  exit code was $RC, expected 1"
  FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
fi

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All sweeper_health_ledger_warn tests passed."
```

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_sweeper_health_ledger_warn.sh 2>&1 | tail -5`
Expected failure: "no WARN line mentioning ledger + stale found" — sweeper_health_check.sh does not yet call check_ledger_freshness.sh at all, so the WARN never appears (RC may still be 0, also causing the second assertion to fail).

## GREEN
Not applicable to this bead (TEST-only; GREEN is proven by T3a-IMPL).

## Do not
Do not edit scripts/sweeper_health_check.sh in this bead. Do not assume sweeper_health_check.sh's internal `SCRIPT_DIR` resolution mechanism without checking it first if Step 1's shim does not produce the expected effect — if the stub is not picked up, stop per Stop-when rather than inventing a different shimming mechanism.

## Stop when
If, after Step 2, the OUTPUT captured in the test shows the real (non-stub) check_ledger_freshness.sh ran instead of the fake one (detectable because the real one's reason string differs from `no_published_ledger_commit`), stop and report to the parent — the PATH/SCRIPT_DIR shimming assumption in this bead's design was wrong and needs a different approach, not a guess.

Mechanism: scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh line 88 DEFAULT_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS=(worldarchitect.ai worldai_claw wa-missions); the comment explains the real intent -- a canonical evidence/repo root landing directly in /private/tmp (worldarchitect.ai's evidence path) must never be treated as scratch. Override is DISK_MAGICIAN_PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS or config.json protected_tmp_roots. Consequence measured 2026-10-12: a --large dry run logged 'Skipping protected root (in PROTECTED_TMP_ROOTS): /private/tmp/worldarchitect.ai' and never descended, so /private/tmp/worldarchitect.ai (32 GB, 431 entries) kept a 9.0 GB child 'split-gates' that was 26 hours idle with ZERO files modified in the previous 14 hours. The lane's own age gate never saw it. It was only reclaimed by an operator-approved manual removal after verification: no top-level .git, nested gist clones all clean (0 dirty) and fully pushed (0 unpushed commits), and scripts/safety_check.sh OK; after removal evidence/ was still present and the parent dropped 32 GB -> 23 GB. Fix: protect the canonical child paths (e.g. worldarchitect.ai/evidence) instead of the whole parent, or evaluate per-child staleness inside a protected root with a stricter threshold (e.g. 7 days), a per-child safety_check, and a clean/pushed check for nested repos; never touch the evidence path. Acceptance: a stale multi-GB child inside a protected root is either reclaimed by the lane once it passes the stricter age + safety gates, or reported with its size and age for an operator decision -- and the canonical evidence path is never modified.

title: IMPL: tmp_scratch_sweep.sh wrapper + plist repoint
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #74 + PR #73 merged. Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Create scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh (new wrapper) and repoint launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-tmp-scratch.plist.template's ProgramArguments at it. Owned files: scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh (new), launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-tmp-scratch.plist.template (modify), `src/disk_magician/scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh` (new) and `src/disk_magician/launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-tmp-scratch.plist.template` (modified) — both generated by `sync_package_tree.sh` in Step 4, not hand-edited. Depends on: T2-TEST closed. Line budget: ~35 changed/new lines across the wrapper + plist (generated mirrors excluded from the count, per this repo's own convention of not counting mechanically-mirrored files as hand-written change).

## Reuse
Confirmed live plist content before this bead (re-verify with Step 1 below, since T2-TEST or other beads may not have touched it, but never assume it is unchanged from this text): ProgramArguments is `@BASH@`, `@REPO_ROOT@/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh`, `--clean`, `--large`; EnvironmentVariables dict has `HOME`→`@HOME@` and `LARGE_TMP_APPROVED`→`1`.

## Steps
1. Run: `cat launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-tmp-scratch.plist.template` (read-only; confirm the ProgramArguments array still matches the block quoted in Reuse above before editing — if it differs, stop per Stop-when).
2. Create scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh with this exact content, then `chmod +x scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh`:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tmp_scratch_sweep.sh — hourly tmp-scratch job entry point (bead disk_magician-isw
# scheduling gap). Wraps cleanup_tmp.sh (--large) then cleanup_claude_state.sh,
# each with its own explicit *_APPROVED=1 gate, failure-continuing between steps.
set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
clean_flag="${1:---dry-run}"

if [[ "$clean_flag" == "--clean" ]]; then
  env LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=1 "$SCRIPT_DIR/cleanup_tmp.sh" --clean --large
  env CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1 "$SCRIPT_DIR/cleanup_claude_state.sh" --clean
else
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/cleanup_tmp.sh" --dry-run --large
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/cleanup_claude_state.sh" --dry-run
fi
exit 0
```
3. Edit launchd/com.jleechanorg.disk-magician-tmp-scratch.plist.template: replace the ProgramArguments array
```
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>@BASH@</string>
    <string>@REPO_ROOT@/scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh</string>
    <string>--clean</string>
    <string>--large</string>
  </array>
```
   with
```
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>@BASH@</string>
    <string>@REPO_ROOT@/scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh</string>
    <string>--clean</string>
  </array>
```
   and remove the `<key>LARGE_TMP_APPROVED</key>` / `<string>1</string>` pair from the `EnvironmentVariables` dict (the wrapper now sets this itself per Step 2), leaving only `HOME`→`@HOME@` in that dict.
4. Run: `bash scripts/sync_package_tree.sh` (no `--check`) to mirror scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh AND the edited plist template into `src/disk_magician/` (`launchd/*.plist.template` is also in its `PATTERNS` set, so this one invocation covers both changed files — do not run it per-file).

No `pyproject.toml` version bump in this bead (round-3 `/advice` correction): `scripts/check_version_monotonic.py`'s gate is `current version >= every historical version`, so an unchanged version trivially passes — a bump is not required for CI, and per this plan's own Task 7 finding, none of this plan's scripts need the uv-tool-packaged copy redeployed either. Bumping here would also be the exact `pyproject.toml`-collision risk flagged against parallelizing T1/T2 — not bumping removes that risk entirely rather than requiring serialization.

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh 2>&1 | tail -3` before this bead's edits → last line is NOT `All tmp_scratch_sweep tests passed.` (per T2-TEST's RED proof).

## GREEN
Run: `bash tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` after this bead's edits → exact output `All tmp_scratch_sweep tests passed.`

## Do not
Do not add TMP_WORKTREES_APPROVED=1 to the cleanup_tmp.sh call — the current tmp-scratch job does not grant it today (only pressure_sweep.sh's threshold path does), and adding it here would silently expand what gets deleted hourly beyond what was requested. ## Stop when
If the plist's ProgramArguments/EnvironmentVariables content does not match the block quoted in Reuse, stop and report the actual content to the parent instead of guessing where to edit.

title: TEST: tmp_scratch_sweep.sh wrapper assertions
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main after PR #74 + PR #73 merged. Interpreter: bash. No throwaway worktree required.

## Goal
Create tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh, a new test file proving a not-yet-created scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh wrapper: (a) calls cleanup_tmp.sh with `--clean --large` and `LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=1` set, then (b) calls cleanup_claude_state.sh with `--clean` and `CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1` set, in that order, and (c) still calls step (b) even if step (a)'s mock exits 1 (failure-continue). Owned file: tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh only (new file). Depends on: PR #74 merged (defines cleanup_claude_state.sh's CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1 gate this test asserts). Line budget: ~90 lines (new file).

## Reuse
Copy the exact structural skeleton of tests/test_pressure_sweep.sh lines 1-56 (shebang, SCRIPT_DIR/REPO_ROOT/SOURCE_SCRIPT resolution, mktemp TMP_ROOT + EXIT trap, MOCK_BIN dir, mock-script heredoc pattern, `cp`+`chmod +x` the copy into MOCK_BIN, run-helper function) — but point SOURCE_SCRIPT at `$REPO_ROOT/scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh` instead. Copy the `assert_contains`/`assert_not_contains`/PASS/FAIL helper block verbatim from tests/test_pressure_sweep.sh lines 58-81.

## Steps
1. Run: `test -f scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING` (expect `MISSING` before this bead's file is used to drive T2-IMPL).
2. Create tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh with this exact content:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh — Behavioral tests for tmp_scratch_sweep.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
SOURCE_SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh"

TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t tmp_scratch_sweep_test.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT

MOCK_BIN="$TMP_ROOT/scripts"
INVOCATION_LOG="$TMP_ROOT/invocations.log"
mkdir -p "$MOCK_BIN"
: > "$INVOCATION_LOG"

cat > "$MOCK_BIN/cleanup_tmp.sh" <<'MOCK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "cleanup_tmp $* LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=${LARGE_TMP_APPROVED:-0}" >> "${INVOCATION_LOG:?}"
[[ "${TMP_MOCK_EXIT:-0}" == "0" ]] && exit 0 || exit 1
MOCK

cat > "$MOCK_BIN/cleanup_claude_state.sh" <<'MOCK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "cleanup_claude_state $* CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=${CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED:-0}" >> "${INVOCATION_LOG:?}"
exit 0
MOCK

chmod +x "$MOCK_BIN/cleanup_tmp.sh" "$MOCK_BIN/cleanup_claude_state.sh"
cp "$SOURCE_SCRIPT" "$MOCK_BIN/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh"
chmod +x "$MOCK_BIN/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh"
SCRIPT="$MOCK_BIN/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

assert_contains() {
  local name="$1" needle="$2" haystack="$3"
  if grep -qF "$needle" <<<"$haystack"; then
    echo "  PASS  $name"
    PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
  else
    echo "  FAIL  $name (missing: $needle)"
    FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
  fi
}

echo "Test 1: --clean invokes cleanup_tmp.sh with LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=1"
: > "$INVOCATION_LOG"
INVOCATION_LOG="$INVOCATION_LOG" bash "$SCRIPT" --clean
INVOCATIONS="$(cat "$INVOCATION_LOG")"
assert_contains "cleanup_tmp invoked with --clean --large" "cleanup_tmp --clean --large LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=1" "$INVOCATIONS"

echo "Test 2: --clean invokes cleanup_claude_state.sh with CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1"
assert_contains "cleanup_claude_state invoked with --clean" "cleanup_claude_state --clean CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1" "$INVOCATIONS"

echo "Test 3: order — cleanup_tmp line precedes cleanup_claude_state line"
TMP_LINE=$(grep -n "^cleanup_tmp" "$INVOCATION_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
STATE_LINE=$(grep -n "^cleanup_claude_state" "$INVOCATION_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
if [[ -n "$TMP_LINE" && -n "$STATE_LINE" && "$TMP_LINE" -lt "$STATE_LINE" ]]; then
  echo "  PASS  tmp step runs before state step"
  PASS=$(( PASS + 1 ))
else
  echo "  FAIL  tmp step did not run before state step"
  FAIL=$(( FAIL + 1 ))
fi

echo "Test 4: failure-continue — cleanup_claude_state still runs if cleanup_tmp exits 1"
: > "$INVOCATION_LOG"
INVOCATION_LOG="$INVOCATION_LOG" TMP_MOCK_EXIT=1 bash "$SCRIPT" --clean
INVOCATIONS="$(cat "$INVOCATION_LOG")"
assert_contains "cleanup_claude_state still ran after cleanup_tmp failure" "cleanup_claude_state --clean CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=1" "$INVOCATIONS"

echo "Test 5: dry-run mode passes --dry-run to both, sets neither approval var"
: > "$INVOCATION_LOG"
INVOCATION_LOG="$INVOCATION_LOG" bash "$SCRIPT" --dry-run
INVOCATIONS="$(cat "$INVOCATION_LOG")"
assert_contains "cleanup_tmp dry-run, no approval" "cleanup_tmp --dry-run --large LARGE_TMP_APPROVED=0" "$INVOCATIONS"
assert_contains "cleanup_claude_state dry-run, no approval" "cleanup_claude_state --dry-run CLAUDE_STATE_APPROVED=0" "$INVOCATIONS"

echo ""
echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
if (( FAIL > 0 )); then
  exit 1
fi
echo "All tmp_scratch_sweep tests passed."
```

## RED
Run: `bash tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh 2>&1 | tail -5`
Expected failure: `SOURCE_SCRIPT not executable` style error or all 5 assertions FAIL, because scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh does not exist yet — script exits non-zero, last line is not `All tmp_scratch_sweep tests passed.`

## GREEN
Not applicable to this bead (TEST-only; GREEN is proven by T2-IMPL).

## Do not
Do not create scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh in this bead — that is T2-IMPL's job. Do not touch scripts/pressure_sweep.sh, launchd/*, or any other file.

## Stop when
If `$REPO_ROOT/scripts/tmp_scratch_sweep.sh` already exists with different behavior when this bead starts, stop and report to the parent instead of overwriting silently.

## Report
Run: `br --no-auto-flush comments add <THIS-BEAD-ID> "$(bash tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh 2>&1 | tail -3)"`

## Criteria
| ID | Check command | External anchor | Verifier | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T2T1 | `bash tests/test_tmp_scratch_sweep.sh > /tmp/t2test_out.txt 2>&1; grep -q "^Results: [0-9]* passed, [1-9][0-9]* failed" /tmp/t2test_out.txt && echo PASS T2T1 \|\| echo FAIL T2T1` | Real subprocess run at HEAD (RED state, before T2-IMPL) | Independent re-execution by a reviewer other than the author, at the bead's final commit SHA | FAIL |

title: cleanup_tmp --large is silently disabled on Linux: private-tmp root resolution is macOS-only
description: Verified 2026-10-20 on jeff-ubuntu with diskm 0.2.249. Every 'diskm cleanup-tmp --large' run logs 'Skipping --large scan: private-tmp root is unavailable (resolution failed closed)' because the private-tmp root resolves to /private/tmp, a macOS path that does not exist on Linux ('PRIVATE_TMP exists on linux? NO'). Result: the aggressive --large tier never runs on any Linux host, so pressure_sweep's strongest lever is a no-op there. The dry run still reported 1801 dirs / ~36 GB removable via the non-large path, so the tier is not useless on Linux, only the large scan is. Fix: resolve the private-tmp root from the platform (on Linux use /tmp or /var/tmp) instead of hardcoding the macOS path, keep fail-closed semantics when nothing resolves, and add a Linux regression asserting --large performs a real scan (e.g. the log must not contain 'private-tmp root is unavailable' and a >LARGE_TMP_MIN_KB fixture is considered). Acceptance: on Linux, cleanup_tmp --large dry run lists the large fixture and does not emit that skip line.
close_reason: Fixed and merged as a03564f (#225). Root cause: scratch_roots_get_private_tmp() hardcoded /private/tmp (macOS canonical path), which does not exist on Linux, so cleanup_tmp's --large scan resolved to empty and logged 'Skipping --large scan: private-tmp root is unavailable' on every Linux invocation — the aggressive tier never ran on any Linux host (verified on jeff-ubuntu with diskm 0.2.249). Fix: candidate list with first-existing-wins, DISK_MAGICIAN_PRIVATE_TMP_CANDIDATES default /private/tmp:/tmp; macOS unchanged; ka4 fail-closed preserved (no resolvable candidate, or a missing explicit override, still resolves empty and keeps the skip line). RED proof: reverting only the resolver fails exactly the 4 new assertions (4 pass/4 fail) and the baseline scanned the real /private/tmp because the seam did not exist. GREEN: tests/test_cleanup_tmp_private_root.sh 8/0; large_protections 141/0, container_descend 74/0, open_files 85/0, archive_purge 58/0, pressure_budget 37/0. Scope: this re-enables the SCAN, not the delete — removals still pass the cwd gate (kub3), where 17.6 GiB of Ubuntu /tmp is past retention and still blocked.

title: Centralize a strict lsof cwd parser for all four worktree-removal consumers
description: PR #208's reviewers (codex + agy, 4 rounds) found the fail-closed live-cwd property is re-implemented ad hoc in worktree_hygiene.sh, worktree_remove_hook.sh, cleanup_worktrees.sh and the deps/venvs cleaners, and each copy fails open differently: multi-'n' records in one p<pid> block silently overwrite (worktree_hygiene.sh); records before the first p block are discarded; an empty pid ('p' alone) is skipped instead of failing closed; ignored denied records count toward saw_cwd/seen so an all-uninspectable scan reads idle; worktree_remove_hook.sh wrh_live_cwd_reason only intercepts '/proc/*/cwd (readlink:*' and treats '/path (stat: Permission denied)' as a literal non-matching path. title: sandbox-context lint is file-level, not per-call-site
description:
## Environment
Repo root: /Users/jleechan/projects_other/disk_magician, branch main. Bash.

## Found by
PR #78 /advice rounds 2-3 (Codex + Opus, both independently confirmed).

## Context
tests/test_sandbox_context_lint.sh (bead disk_magician-lsl follow-up / PR #71
/advice HOLD) enforces that any test file invoking a destructive cleanup path
(cleanup_tmp.sh/cleanup_pr_scratch.sh/pressure_sweep.sh --clean/--large/--budget,
or a direct scratch_budget_evict_root() call) also references BOTH
DISK_MAGICIAN_TEST_CONTEXT and DISK_MAGICIAN_TEST_SANDBOX somewhere in the file.

## Root cause
The check is FILE-LEVEL (grep -q for each var name anywhere in the file), not
per-call-site. A file that already legitimately names both vars once (e.g. in
a docstring, or an explicit override in one unrelated test) passes the lint
even if a NEW destructive call site added later in that same file forgets to
carry them. Confirmed via mutation testing in PR #78 round 3 (Opus): stripping
run_budget()'s env lines from tests/test_scratch_budget.sh still passed the
lint because Test12 separately names both vars elsewhere in the file.

Also relevant (not itself a bug, but adjacent): tests/lib/sandbox_env.sh
deliberately does NOT `export` DISK_MAGICIAN_TEST_CONTEXT, so a bare
`bash "$SCRIPT" ...` invocation that doesn't prefix the var explicitly would
NOT see it (confirmed empirically). This is currently harmless because every
real destructive call site uses the explicit `VAR=val bash ...` prefix
pattern, but a future call site that relies on inherited environment instead
of an explicit prefix would silently defeat the guard even with the lint
"passing" today.

## Impact
Low, test-only blast radius: sandbox_guard_roots() (scripts/safety_lib.sh)
still fails closed in PRODUCTION regardless of this lint (both env vars unset
there). The exposure is limited to a hypothetical future test author who adds
a new destructive call to an already-"passing" test file and forgets the vars
on that specific call -- the lint would not catch it, and (depending on
whether they use an explicit prefix or rely on inherited environment) it
could run unconfined against real host paths, reproducing the bead
disk_magician-ka4 incident class, but only in a test run, not production.

## Goal
Make tests/test_sandbox_context_lint.sh per-call-site rather than file-level:
require both env var names to appear on the same line or an immediately
preceding continuation line (bash's `\` line-continuation convention already
used throughout these test files) as each destructive invocation, rather than
anywhere in the file. Consider also requiring `export` semantics or an
explicit-prefix-only convention be documented/enforced for
DISK_MAGICIAN_TEST_CONTEXT specifically, given
tests/test_lsof_skip_check_production_guard.sh relies on it NOT being
exported.

## Acceptance criteria
- tests/test_sandbox_context_lint.sh's check_file() (or a replacement) verifies
  BOTH sandbox vars are present within N lines immediately preceding each
  destructive invocation, not just anywhere in the file.
- A new RED test proves the lint now catches the exact mutation scenario from
  PR #78 round 3 (a destructive call added to an already-compliant file,
  missing its own vars).
- tests/test_lsof_skip_check_production_guard.sh's deliberate unexported-var
  behavior still passes.

title: worktree cleanup is a silent no-op: apply-path push check false-negatives every eligible worktree
description:
Measured 2026-10-22 on the Mac (~11:30-12:10 local). Worktree cleanup currently reclaims NOTHING because the
preview and the apply path disagree, and the apply path's push check produces false negatives.

RECEIPT (same worktree, same head, same age — only the mode differs):
  dry-run:  LEDGER repo-local ELIGIBLE  .../worldai_frontend/avatar-84 | age=4d size=179M head=47d8bba8
  --clean:  LEDGER repo-local PRESERVE  .../worldai_frontend/avatar-84 | not-pushed | age=4d size=179M head=47d8bba8
  Totals: `cleanup_worktrees.sh` (dry) -> "Repo-local: 25 eligible, 560 preserved, Reclaimable ~3.48 GB"
          `cleanup_worktrees.sh --clean` -> "Repo-local: 0 eligible, 586 preserved, Reclaimable ~0.00 GB"
  Zero removals, zero bytes.

GROUND TRUTH (the apply verdict is wrong, not the preview):
  $ git -C /Users/jleechan/project_worldai_frontend/worldai_frontend ls-remote --heads origin | grep -c fix/light-theme-avatar-84
  1
  $ git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD  -> 47d8bba874fc3c0cc7741a5f728a8bd6b662a751
  $ git -C <repo> branch -r --contains 47d8bba8  -> origin/main, origin/ci/ios-testflight-autotrigger-20261018,
    origin/ci/testflight-runner-signing-session-20261020   (i.e. merged / already in origin)
  `git ls-remote` itself is fast and healthy from this host (0.5s, rc 0), so this is NOT a dead-network case.

WHY IT MATTERS: in the apply run the preserve histogram was 317 young, 50 ahead-of-main, 48 untracked,
32 live-cwd, 30 dirty, 27 ao-owned, 20 hidden-state, and 17 not-pushed. Exactly the 17 "not-pushed" are the
ones the preview had called ELIGIBLE. So the push verification is the single gate turning the whole sweep
into a no-op, and `not-pushed` is reported in a way that is indistinguishable from a genuine unpushed branch.

WORKING HYPOTHESIS for the false negative: the apply-path push check is deadline/timeout bounded (C14 has
`--deadline-at` and returns `deferred:lsremote` / `kept:check-failed` elsewhere), and this host is thrashing
(swap grew 24 -> 43 GiB during the same window, available RAM 8.8 GB, `ps` taking minutes). A bounded
ls-remote that loses its race fails closed, and fail-closed here is spelled "not-pushed". Unconfirmed --
the next step is to instrument that one call with its elapsed time and raw verdict.

FIX SHAPE (proposed, not implemented):
1. Split the verdict: a definitive "not on any remote" must be reported differently from "could not verify"
   (e.g. `pushed-unknown`), so a broken/throttled check is never silently counted as a safety preserve.
2. Make dry-run and --clean call the SAME push checker with the same deadline (this divergence is the same
   defect family as cleanup_tmp's preview 4.2 GiB vs apply 0, and as q9ry/#212/#213 for codex documents).
3. Retry once with a longer deadline on `deferred`/`check-failed` before preserving, and surface the retry
   count in the summary so a degraded run is visible (cf. the #224 degraded gate).

This is the macOS analogue of disk_magician-kub3 (Linux unreadable-cwd made every lane a no-op) and should
be treated as the same severity class: a fail-closed gate with no observability silently disables a whole
reclaim lane, while ~/.worktrees holds 157 GiB (115 worktrees with dependency dirs).
close_reason: Merged PR #242 (2839e418efb412f8bcbca8003a77185a04c7f93e). C14 push obligations narrowed to the exact HEAD + ORIG_HEAD files + refs/**|logs/**; FETCH_HEAD (the false-negative source) excluded. /advice Codex approved at 60403178 after its ORIG_HEAD objection was implemented; merged on explicit single-reviewer acceptance. Measured effect: sweep 0 -> 10 worktrees, ~/.worktrees 157.0 -> 152.2 GiB.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-10-22, bash -x trace + direct probes) — structural, NOT network or load.

The verdict does not come from the hook's own refs/remotes check at all: the trace shows
'wrh_c14_verdict=kept:not-pushed', i.e. C14 decides. Inside c14_repo_pushed_ok
(scripts/lib/artifact_verdict.sh:85) a LINKED worktree takes the 'cd != gd' branch, which does:
  tips = $(c14_probe.py admin <gitdir>) + HEAD
  scope=() linked=1
  unp=$(git rev-list ${scope[@]+...} --stdin -n1 <<< tips + ^<advertised SHAs>)
  [[ -z $unp ]] || { echo kept:not-pushed; return 1; }
i.e. EVERY tip must be advertised by ls-remote. But c14_probe.py admin on a real linked worktree
returns dozens of local-only refs. Measured on worldai_frontend/avatar-84:
  gitdir=/Users/jleechan/project_worldai_frontend/worldai_frontend/.git/worktrees/avatar-84
  admin tips include 0cc1b770, 129b8066, 2391d992, 24fdd979, 109c8104, ... (dozens)
  HEAD=47d8bba8, and ls-remote DOES advertise '47d8bba8 refs/heads/fix/light-theme-avatar-84'
  (plus refs/pull/95/head, refs/tags/..., refs/wip/diskm/...)
Any single local-only admin ref therefore makes $unp non-empty -> kept:not-pushed, permanently.

CONSEQUENCE: a linked worktree containing any local-only admin ref can NEVER be removed by C14,
regardless of age or merge state. That is why the sweep reports 0 eligible — and it very likely
explains the earlier Linux measurement of '0 eligible of 716'. Worktree cleanup has been a silent
no-op machine-wide; the preview counts it as eligible because the preview path does not run this
check (hence 25 vs 0).

FIX SHAPE (now concrete):
1.  tips must not be treated as push obligations unqualified. Only refs that represent work
   the operator could lose belong in the negative-tip set — the branch tip and its reflog are the
   real content; per-worktree scratch refs (refs/worktree/*, refs/bisect/*, and diskm's own
   refs/wip/diskm/* bookkeeping) are local metadata by design.
2. Distinguish 'not advertised' from 'unverifiable' in the verdict (pushed-unknown), so this class of
   bug is visible instead of looking like a legitimately unpushed branch.
3. Make the preview path call the same check so dry-run cannot advertise removals the apply path will
   always refuse. Regression test: a linked worktree whose branch tip IS advertised but whose admin
   dir contains a local-only scratch ref must verdict 'remove'.
DO NOT simply drop the admin tips: they are what protects unpushed WIP (that is the whole point of
the check); the fix is to scope which admin refs count.

comments.text:
2026-11-10 scratch reclaim session: two blockers found on top of the PR #339 merge.

(1) FIXED in PR #340 (merged + deployed 0.2.366). scratch_budget_artifact_children.py fails closed for the ENTIRE batch when any candidate subtree is unreadable, and cleanup_scratch_top_level.sh pipes every candidate into one batch call. One unreadable top-level entry therefore disabled all Scratch reclamation: Linux Scratch/lost+found (root:root 0700, 16K) produced scanned=0 removed=0 deferred:artifact-discovery-unmeasurable-rc-1 on a 163 GiB volume, and /Volumes/diskm-scratch/.Spotlight-V100 did the same on macOS with empty stderr. Fix skips candidates that are not -r and -x before batching, preserving the helper contract (case 15 still pins rc=1). After deploy, Linux went scanned=0 -> scanned=543.

(2) OPEN, and it is why ~47 GiB stayed unreclaimed: the recency floor is applied to the top-level entry AGGREGATE mtime, not per child, and artifact discovery only expands ARTIFACT_NAMES so mirror-shaped dirs are never descended. Measured on Linux: Scratch/mirrors aggregate age 0h but 30 GiB of its 38 GiB is >=24h stale per child (dozens of children 34-95h); mirror-output 8 of 17 GiB stale; worldarchitect.ai 9 of 9 GiB stale. Fixing this is widening the class map plus per-child descent, per the AGENTS.md "per-file, never per-directory" rule. Tuning triggers will not reach it.

(3) Producer outran reclaim: during the scheduled --budget-pct 50 sweeper, Linux Scratch went 160 -> 169 GB used because other agent lanes were cloning git mirrors into Scratch (journal-perf-20261110 2.9G at 14:44, pr671-build 1.3G, pr672-build 1.3G, night-fidelity-20261110 1.2G; 6.6 GB of fresh data in 15 minutes).

(4) Parallelism ceiling is 1 for Scratch reclaim, not per-machine: scratch_lock.py serializes cleanup_scratch_top_level.sh on ~/.disk_magician_locks/scratch_cleanup.lock with a 20s wait then skipped:lease-busy, and the scheduled sweeper holds it 900s. Five lanes across two hosts were launched; only code-sign (5.85 GB), codex-db and quarantine-reconcile actually progressed concurrently. Worktree lanes additionally serialize on the lease registry lock.

title: cleanup_xcode hangs on unbounded 'xcrun simctl delete unavailable', blocking its 19.6 GB derived-data section
description:
Measured 2026-10-22/23 on the Mac. `scripts/cleanup_xcode.sh --clean` hangs indefinitely on an
UNBOUNDED `xcrun simctl delete unavailable`, and because that call sits BEFORE the derived-data
section, the hang blocks the script's own largest reclaim.

Receipt (lane log /tmp/lane_a_clean_xcode.log):
  18:02:03 Cleanup mode: APPLY
  18:02:03 Xcode DerivedData: deleting contents of .../DerivedData (0K)
  18:02:27 CoreSimulator Temp: deleting contents of ...
  18:02:28 CoreSimulator Caches: deleting contents of ...
  18:02:28 running: xcrun simctl delete unavailable
  ... no further output for 6+ minutes; the lane's bash call was still open at 240s+ and the script
  never reached its dd-dir section.

Why it matters: cleanup_xcode.sh:111 handles `$ptmp/worldai_frontend/*` and `*/*` (the
DerivedData-shaped build dirs the reclaim ledger ranks as the #1 all-time reclaim root at
76.15 GiB, owner cleanup_xcode.sh). /private/tmp/worldai_frontend is currently 19.6 GB again.
Because the simctl call hangs first, that section never runs, so the single biggest known location
on this host is unreachable whenever CoreSimulator is unresponsive.

Additional evidence the call itself is the problem, not the cleanup: `xcrun simctl list devices
booted` and `xcrun simctl list devices unavailable` also timed out (>200s, >400s respectively) in
separate probes during the same session; one `simctl` PID was TERMed and another respawned
immediately. CoreSimulator services were unreachable after `simctl shutdown all` had succeeded
earlier, so this is a wedged subsystem rather than a missing simulator.

FIX SHAPE (proposed, not implemented):
1. Bound the call: run it through the script's existing bounded-timeout helper (the repo already has
   one used by pressure_sweep; cleanup_xcode should not call a network/IPC tool unbounded), and
   treat a timeout as a non-fatal SKIP that is LOGGED (the script's own contract says it is
   "Non-fatal: exits 0 if tmutil is unavailable"), never as reason to abandon the rest of the run.
2. Move the simulator housekeeping AFTER the derived-data sections, so a wedged simulator subsystem
   can never suppress the primary reclaim.
3. Report the skip in the summary as DEGRADED (cf. the #224 degraded gate) rather than passing
   silently.
Note: this is housekeeping only -- deleting unavailable simulators reclaims little; its sole effect
today was to block ~19.6 GB of derived data.

Related: disk_magician-xt2y (scratch lock orphans block cleanup_tmp for the same /private/tmp pool),
disk_magician-vp7h (worktree push gate), disk_magician-kub3 (Linux cwd gate).

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my own initial analysis (2026-10-22 18:20), after reading the script's call order:

The hang does NOT block the derived-data section. cleanup_xcode.sh calls clean_custom_derived_data at line 146, and the simctl block starts at line 151 — so the custom-DD sweep runs FIRST and had already completed (silently) before the wedge. My earlier claim that the hang 'blocks its largest reclaim' was wrong; corrected here rather than left standing.

What actually happened in the wedged lane: clear_contents DerivedData/Temp/Caches all reported 0K, clean_custom_derived_data logged nothing at all (it logs only for SAFETY-SKIP / 'written within Nm' and is silent when no candidate matches the shape test), then the run wedged on the unbounded simctl call before printing its summary. Real reclaim was 0 for that lane, and the simctl hang only cost the summary + lane completion, not the reclaim.

Separately, the 19.6 GB in /private/tmp/worldai_frontend is NOT DerivedData-shaped and is not Xcode-owned at all. Measured contents:
  evidence        7392 MB
  native-build    3346 MB
  rt              2363 MB
  native-evidence  986 MB
  pkt / pkt2 / ci-local / pr238-main-baseline-*  ~200 MB each
  (plus screenshots 01-landing.png, 01b-google.png, 02-after-email.png at the root)
That is PR evidence + native build scratch for the worldai_frontend repo, owned by cleanup_tmp / cleanup_pr_scratch, both of which are scratch-flock gated -- i.e. it is blocked by disk_magician-xt2y, not by this bead.

So the unbounded-simctl defect is still real (it wedges the whole run and suppresses the summary, and would suppress anything appended after line 151) and the fix shape stands: bound it with the existing timeout helper, treat a timeout as a logged non-fatal SKIP, and report DEGRADED. But it is NOT the reason that 19.6 GB is unreachable. Priority for the /private/tmp pool belongs to xt2y.

title: Remediate scattered ~/wf_* checkouts (28.6 GiB) and ~/wf*_dd Xcode DerivedData (14.25 GiB) in /Users/jleechan
description:
## Context & Violation
35 /Users/jleechan/wf_* directories (comprising 11 full `git clone` copies of worldai_frontend + 20 linked worktrees + build/test scripts) consuming ~28.6 GiB, alongside 3 custom Xcode DerivedData directories (/Users/jleechan/wf_dd, /Users/jleechan/wf_ipad_dd, /Users/jleechan/wf_cache_dd at 4.75 GiB each = 14.25 GiB), were created directly in the user's home directory ($HOME) on 2026-10-17. Total unmanaged storage footprint: ~42.85 GiB.

## Root Cause
1. Multi-agent coordinator prompts in Pi (`01a14c44-c646-74d6-8c8e-1ba5e5e91f2e`, `01a14bea-39e9-70f1-9ea5-19c2cd7ee07c`), Codex (`01a14c91-2a74-7cb2-8932-87111c8d5a9a`), and handoff documentation in /Users/jleechan/roadmap/hermes-ios-handoff-2026-10-17.md explicitly hardcoded checkout targets like `/Users/jleechan/wf_<name>` and build flags `-derivedDataPath /Users/jleechan/wf_*_dd`.
2. Existing enforcement in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/worktree_guard.py only checks `git worktree add`, failing to intercept direct `git clone` invocations, and does not run within Pi/Codex/Hermes agent harnesses.
3. Existing cleanup in /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/cleanup_xcode.sh only targets /Users/jleechan/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData, completely missing custom `-derivedDataPath` locations such as `/Users/jleechan/wf_*_dd`.

## Remediation Steps
1. Extend /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/worktree_guard.py and agent pre-command hooks (Codex, Pi, Hermes) to detect and block top-level $HOME git clones and worktrees, redirecting to /private/tmp or /Users/jleechan/projects.
2. Update /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/cleanup_xcode.sh (or add sweeper pattern) to recognize and clean custom `*_dd` DerivedData directories in non-standard locations once builds complete.
3. Audit and prune the 35 `/Users/jleechan/wf_*` directories: verify git status and push status on remote branches, ensure 7d/3d recency compliance, and safely remove or relocate to /Users/jleechan/projects.
4. Purge the stale 14.25 GiB Xcode caches in /Users/jleechan/wf_dd, /Users/jleechan/wf_ipad_dd, and /Users/jleechan/wf_cache_dd.

title: Single Authoritative Worktree & Clone Registry + Hard 2-Root Enforcement
description:
## Goal
Establish a single authoritative worktree and clone registry (`config/worktree_roots.json` or `scripts/lib/layout_standard.sh`) and unified scanner in `disk_magician` that indexes ALL known legacy checkout locations across disk, while strictly enforcing a hard 2-root convention (`/tmp` for scratch/ephemeral, `~/projects` for persistent worktrees/clones) across all coding agents.

## Problem Statement
On-disk inventory identified 1,396 checkouts (475 linked worktrees + 921 standalone clones) fragmented across 9 non-standard buckets outside `/tmp` and `~/projects`. 
Crucially, standalone clones (`git clone`) in locations such as:
- `~/wf_*`
- `~/Documents/Codex`
- `~/cb-wa-*`
- `~/wc-wt/advice-*`
- `/private/tmp/worldai_claw`
- `/private/tmp/worldarchitect.ai`
- `~/.openclaw_prod_bak`
- `~/.dark-factory`

do NOT have `.git` files pointing back to a primary worktree parent (`gitdir: ...`). As a result:
1. `git worktree list` run from the primary repository (e.g. `~/projects/worldarchitect.ai`) completely omits them.
2. Canonical worktree sweepers (`cleanup_worktrees.sh`, `worktree_reap.sh`, `worktree_hygiene.sh`) only scan registered primary repos or hardcoded directories, leaving these 921 standalone clones invisible and accumulating unbounded disk space.
3. Multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Hermes, OpenClaw, ChatGPT Desktop) create ad-hoc checkout directories in arbitrary `$HOME` paths without a shared directory convention or lease tracking.

## Deliverables
1. **Canonical Registry & Discovery**:
   - Define `config/worktree_roots.json` (or standard bash configuration) listing all valid search roots for both linked worktrees and standalone git repositories.
   - Extend `diskm status` and `disk_snapshot.sh` to traverse and report all known buckets.
2. **Scanner & Sweeper Integration**:
   - Update `cleanup_worktrees.sh` and `worktree_reap.sh` to ingest the registry so standalone clones and non-standard worktree roots are audited, recency-checked, and safely cleaned.
3. **Hard 2-Root Policy & Guardrails**:
   - Enforce workstation convention: NEW checkouts must only reside in:
     - `/tmp/*` (or `/private/tmp/*`) for ephemeral test lanes, scratch checkouts, and automated verification.
     - `~/projects/*` for durable multi-day worktrees and primary repositories.
   - Ban creating ad-hoc checkouts in `$HOME`, `~/Documents`, or random root prefixes (`~/wf_*`, `~/project_*`).
   - Add preflight check / lint rule for agent harnesses.

## Governance & Reference
- Documented in `findings_wiki/2026-10-17-worktree-locations-inventory-and-space-savings.md`.

title: diskm worktree-new checkouts cannot push: git wrapper runs an LFS lock check on a repo with zero LFS files
description: A fresh checkout created by diskm worktree-new cannot push: the local git wrapper runs a Git LFS pre-push lock verification, and it fails with 'Authentication required: You must have push access to verify locks' even though this repo has ZERO LFS files ('git lfs ls-files' = 0, no filter=lfs in .gitattributes). Verified 2026-10-12 in /Users/jleechan/.worktrees/disk_magician/fix-worktree-hygiene-preserve-wip (branch fix/worktree-hygiene-preserve-wip): plain 'git push' and 'git -c credential.helper=!gh\ auth\ git-credential push' both failed; the push succeeded only with GIT_LFS_SKIP_PUSH=1 plus the gh credential helper. Pushes from the main checkout (same .git hooks, same remote) succeed, so this is specific to newly created worktrees. Impact: the documented worktree flow (diskm worktree-new -> work -> push) is broken out of the box for agents. Fix: detect that the repo has no LFS objects/attributes and skip LFS lock verification (set lfs.locksverify=false, or short-circuit the wrapper), or install/configure the hook so it succeeds. Acceptance: 'git push' from a worktree created by diskm worktree-new succeeds with no GIT_LFS_SKIP_PUSH and no gh-specific credential workaround.

title: Policy conflict & migration: ~/.worktrees/<repo>/<name> (78.6 GiB) vs two-root mandate (/tmp and ~/projects)

## Context & Violation
Approximately 400+ git worktrees consuming ~78.6 GiB of disk space currently reside under /Users/jleechan/.worktrees/<repo>/<name>. This violates the user's two-root mandate that requires all worktrees and clones to live exclusively in /private/tmp (or /tmp) for ephemeral work or /Users/jleechan/projects for persistent checkouts.

## Root Cause
On 2026-10-05, the following specification and scripts codified ~/.worktrees as the primary standard worktree root:

Furthermore, the PreToolUse hook `diskm guard-worktree-add` actively blocked agents from creating worktrees inside /Users/jleechan/projects, forcing them into /Users/jleechan/.worktrees.

3. Update PreToolUse hooks so `guard-worktree-add` permits creation in approved roots (/Users/jleechan/projects and /private/tmp) while rejecting root $HOME or other unapproved locations.
4. Triage and migrate active worktrees from /Users/jleechan/.worktrees into /Users/jleechan/projects, and reap/prune stale/merged worktrees (>7d/3d recency rules) using /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/cleanup_worktrees.sh and /Users/jleechan/projects_other/worktree_dropbox/scripts/worktree_hygiene.sh.

title: pressure-sweep timeout orphans cleanup_tmp and starves the scratch lock; dry-run overstates 4.2 GiB
description:
Measured on the Mac 2026-10-21/22 during a routine cleanup round. Two related defects, both with receipts.

A) A timed-out pressure sweep leaves an ORPHANED cleanup_tmp holding the scratch flock forever.
Receipt from ~/Library/Logs/disk-magician-pressure-sweep.log (run 1f908f8c, 2026-10-22T07:35:17Z):
  "outcome": "timeout", "duration_seconds": 1214.0,
  "safety": {"reason": "delegated to cleanup_tmp, ... (STEP1_RC=124, STEP1_TIMEOUT=true, ... STEP3_RC=124, STEP3_TIMEOUT=true)"},
  "postcondition": {"free_gb_before": 34, "free_gb_after": 32}
So the sweep ran 20 minutes and freed nothing (net -2 GB).
Meanwhile `lsof ~/.disk_magician_locks/scratch_cleanup.lock` showed pid 10271 still holding fd 4:
  cleanup_tmp.sh --clean --large   (from the DEPLOYED package, uv tools 0.2.255)
running 12+ minutes AFTER its parent sweep had already recorded its timeout. The wrapper kills/reports
itself but does not reap the child process group, so the child keeps the flock.
Consequence observed in the same round: every other cleanup that needs the scratch lock silently no-ops.
`disk_audit.sh clean` reported "Temp files (exit 75)" and "PR scratch & analyzers (exit 75)"; manual
`cleanup_tmp.sh --clean` returned "skipped, scratch lock held after waiting 20s" three times in a row.
Because exit 75 is the #224 degraded-gate signal, the routine correctly reported DEGRADED -- but the
underlying cause is lock starvation by an orphan, not a genuine refusal. Required fixes: (1) run
cleanup_tmp under a timeout that kills the whole process group, and (2) verify/steal a stale lock whose
holder is not a live descendant of the sweep (scratch_lock.py verify already exists -- extend it to
reap). Otherwise a single slow sweep permanently disables scratch cleanup.

B) cleanup_tmp dry-run overstates by 4.2 GiB because it does not apply the C14 verdict it enforces on --clean.
  $ bash scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh          -> "Dirs removed: 62  Total freed: 4379560 KB (~4276 MB)"
  $ bash scripts/cleanup_tmp.sh --clean  -> "Dirs removed: 0  Total freed: 0 KB (~0 MB)"
with every candidate logged as "Preserving (C14 kept:git-unbaselined)".
This is the same defect class that beads q9ry/#212/#213 fixed for cleanup_codex_documents.sh: the
preview path must evaluate the same gates the apply path enforces (per-candidate C14 verdict), otherwise
operators budget reclaim that cannot happen. The pressure-sweep record corroborates it:
"c14_kept_bytes": {"recent-activity": 330451, "git-unbaselined": 44416388, "not-pushed": 1218937975}.

Net effect: the ~4.2 GiB /tmp pool on this host is NOT reclaimable by design (git-unbaselined clones),
and the only reason it looked reclaimable was the inaccurate preview. Do not chase it as a space win.

Related: disk_magician-kub3 (Linux cwd gate, closed), disk_magician-kruh (Sparkle staging, merged #230).
close_reason: Merged PR #247 (4ed0c21): SIGKILL escalation prevents orphaned scratch-lock holders. Visibility/observability half tracked as a follow-up comment.

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE narrowed (code-level, 2026-10-22): the flock fd is deliberately inheritable — scripts/scratch_lock.py:111 does os.set_inheritable(fd, True) — so every child of cleanup_tmp inherits fd 4. flock lives on the open file description, so the lock is released only when ALL duplicates close. When 'timeout 1200' fires, cleanup_tmp traps TERM (scripts/lib/scratch_lock.sh:34-38, scratch_lock_trap_handler) and releases ITS fd, but any surviving child that inherited fd 4 keeps the description open and the lock held. This exactly matches the evidence: lsof showed TWO bash pids on ~/.disk_magician_locks/scratch_cleanup.lock at the same time (10271 = cleanup_tmp.sh --clean --large, and 61785), and the lock stayed held for 12+ min after the sweep recorded STEP1_RC=124/STEP1_TIMEOUT=true. run_step_timeout (scripts/pressure_sweep.sh:131) also passes no --kill-after, so a slow or hung TERM trap is never SIGKILLed. Candidate fix (NOT yet implemented, needs tests): give run_step_timeout a '-k <grace>' when the timeout binary supports it, and/or verify after a timeout that the recorded holder is gone and report the surviving pid instead of a generic skip. Do not simply make the fd non-inheritable: inheritance is load-bearing for scratch_lock_acquire's verify --fd coordination (scripts/lib/scratch_lock.sh:12).

comments.author: jleechan
comments.text:

title: Identify hidden daemon/launchd job writing to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain (sawtooth broken since 2026-08-17)
description:
Found during disk-attribution 2026-08-20: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain grew from sawtooth envelope of 2.5-13 GB to 38.7 GB over 3 days. Lane A verified: 592,475 files modified in last 7 days; recent transcript.jsonl / task-NNN.log files dated today; ps aux shows NO antigravity CLI but brain keeps growing. Top 5 subdirs of brain are session/state UUIDs totaling 31G (17G, 6.1G, 3.2G, 2.7G, 2.0G). Two-step fix needed:

(1) Identify the writer. Likely candidates: a launchd job not matching 'antigravity' in name (e.g. something under com.google.* or ai.google.* or a service account-owned process); or a parent daemon (e.g. NRD.UpdateBrainService-adjacent — though that one is Apple's, not antigravity's). Use: ps aux | grep -iE 'brain|gemini' ; launchctl list | grep -iE 'gemini|brain|antigravity|nrd'; lsof +D ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain 2>/dev/null | head.

(2) Once identified, decide: stop/restart the writer cleanly (so its GC fires and trims brain back to its 2.5-13 GB envelope); or, if writer can't be controlled, file an upstream bug with antigravity and put a temporary launchd watchdog in place.

Until (1) is done, do NOT delete brain contents — the writer will just regenerate. Full writeup: ~/roadmap/disk_magician/sidekick/disk-attr-aug-2026/LANE-A.md
